parts.label: L
parts.question: A character in this novel accidentally kills a puppy given to him by Slim by stroking it too hard. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this novel about the mentally disabled migrant worker Lennie, who one day dreams of owning a rabbit farm, and his friend George, who shoots Lennie when he breaks the neck of Curley’s wife.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American author wrote Of Mice and Men. He also wrote a novel about the Joads, a family of “Okies” who travel to California in search of a job during the Dust Bowl.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Steinbeck set both his novels Of Mice and Men and The Grapes of Wrath during this economic downturn in the early 20th century.
parts.answer: The Great Depression [prompt on Dust Bowl]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of this religious sect belong to a denomination formerly known as the Religious Society of Friends. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this religious denomination whose adherents believe in an “inner light,” a metaphor for the inward light of God. William Penn was a wealthy member of this religious denomination.

parts.label: B
parts.question: William Penn founded this modern-day state after Quakers were persecuted by the Puritans of the Massachusetts Bay colony. Quakers founded many small colleges in this state like Bryn Mawr and Swarthmore, both of which are just outside of Philadelphia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Some Quakers profess the universal priesthood, a belief that discards the idea of a separate class of priests. That belief comes from a verse in the First Epistle of this apostle, who is considered the first Pope.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Willard Libby developed numerous forms of this technique. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this technique that analyzes the decay of radioactive materials to determine the age of geologic substances. The most commonly used form of this technique uses the carbon-14 isotope.
parts.answer: dating [accept radiometric dating or radiocarbon dating or radioactive dating or radioisotope dating or absolute dating or carbon dating]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Due to its presence in many rock formations, the decay of this element into argon is also commonly used to date rocks. This alkali metal commonly found in fertilizers with nitrogen and phosphorus has atomic symbol K.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This isotope’s oxidation into HTO can be used to date water. This radioactive isotope of hydrogen has two neutrons.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these people named Harald Hardrada lost at the Battle of Stamford Bridge. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these warrior seafarers that ravaged the coasts of Great Britain in the late first millennium. They hailed from Scandinavia and had kings such as Cnut (k’NOOT) and Sven Forkbeard.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Vikings traversed the oceans in these narrow oared boats. Accomplished warriors were sometimes buried or cremated with them.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Vikings were the first to settle this modern-day country long-term. The Althing, which was founded in the year 930, is the parliament of this country, which is governed from Reykjavik.
parts.answer: Iceland [or Republic of Iceland or Lydveldid Island]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1890, the US House narrowly voted to award Chicago, rather than New York, hosting rights for one of these events scheduled for 1893. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these expositions, where cities showcased new technological achievements from around the globe. Buildings constructed for these events include the Crystal Palace in London and the Seattle Space Needle.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Chicago celebrates its hosting of the 1893 World’s Fair with one of four stars on this type of object. Another one of these objects in California depicts a brown bear, in honor of a “Bear Republic” named for one of these objects.
parts.answer: Chicago’s flag [accept Bear Flag Republic or California’s flag]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Today, the 1893 fair is famous for the activities of H.H. Holmes, a serial killer who owned one of these establishments during the fair. Holmes confessed to booking and killing 27 guests in this type of establishment, giving it the nickname “Murder Castle.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Goldman Equation is a modification of this equation applied to cell membranes which takes ion selectivity and concentration into account. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this equation which relates the reduction potential of a half-cell with the reaction quotient at a given temperature. A standard hydrogen electrode is used to determine the standard reduction potential within this equation.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Nernst equation uses the reaction quotient to account for the transfer of these species. These negatively charged particles orbit the nucleus.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The reduction potential of various half reactions can be experimentally determined using the cyclic form of this technique. This technique uses three electrodes to determine the potential of a half cell.
parts.answer: voltammetry [accept cyclic voltammetry, accept linear-sweep voltammetry]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one work, this woman is depicted to the right of the sun disk holding a child portrayed with an elongated skull. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this woman who is depicted in many artworks of the Amarna Period. This woman wears a large, flat-topped headdress in a painted limestone bust currently held at the Neues Museum in Berlin.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Much of the artistic innovation during the Amarna period was abandoned during the reign of this pharaoh, the son of Nefertiti’s husband Akhenaten. Howard Carter discovered a gold burial mask in the tomb of this “boy king.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] One lasting consequence of the Amarna style was the dominance of the “sunken” type of this sculptural technique. Elements are raised only slightly from the background in the “low” or “bas” (“bah”) type of this technique.
parts.answer: relief [accept sunken relief or sunk relief or low relief or bas relief]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Sir Charles Wyville Thomson predicted the existence of one of these features after detecting a great temperature disparity between parts of the Faroe-Shetland channel. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these long chains of elevated seafloor. Seafloor spreading causes these features to form in the middle of oceans, including in the Mid-Atlantic.
parts.answer: ridges [accept Mid-Atlantic Ridge or mid-ocean ridges or Wyville Thomson Ridge; prompt on underwater mountains or underwater mountain ranges or submarine mountains or submarine mountain ranges; do NOT accept or prompt on “seamount chains”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Gakkel Ridge is a mid-ocean ridge in this body of water. The Wyville Thomson Ridge separates the deep waters of this polar ocean from the Atlantic Ocean to its south.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is mostly underwater, but reaches almost eight thousand feet above sea level at Mount Pico in this archipelago. This archipelago is the site of a triple junction of the Eurasian, North American, and African plates.

parts.question: This deity has ten arms in her most powerful Maha form. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this goddess who is summoned to a battlefield through the frown lines on another deity’s forehead. This goddess of destruction then goes on to slay the demon Raktabija.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Kali is often depicted standing on top of this god. Since Kali is an aspect of Parvati, her consort is this Hindu destroyer god who composes the Trimurti along with Brahma and Vishnu.

parts.question: [M] After drinking Raktabija’s blood, Kali goes on a rampage and performs this action over the dead bodies of her victims. Shiva performs the tandava when he takes the form of Nataraja, the lord of this action.
parts.answer: dance [accept word forms such as dancing or Lord of the Dance]

parts.question: This quantity has Hicksian and Marshallian types. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name this quantity whose namesake curve meets the supply curve at the equilibrium point.

parts.question: [10] The derivatives of both Hicksian and Marshallian demands are used in this equation, first put forth  in 1915, that decomposes the substitution effect and the income effect.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This law from classical economics is sometimes shortened to “supply creates its own demand.”  Thomas Sowell's academic career began with writings on this law, which partly informed Republican  supply-side economics of the 1980s.

parts.question: A book of infamous headlines from this newspaper is titled for a 1983 frontpage that read “Headless  Body in Topless Bar.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Rupert Murdoch-owned newspaper, founded by Alexander Hamilton, that also operates  the gossip site Page Six.
parts.answer: New York Post [prompt on The Post]

parts.question: [10] The New York Post is considered an example of this type of sensationalist journalism, exemplified  by the British Daily Mirror. Newspapers in this physical format are singly-folded on a vertical spine, as  opposed to larger “broadsheets.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Murdoch also owns this business-focused newspaper founded by Charles H. Dow.

parts.question: This king's prime minister, Jules de Polignac (zhool day pah-lin-YAK), issued the Four Ordinances at  Saint-Cloud. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this last Bourbon king of France, who succeeded Louis XVIII (the eighteenth) in 1824 and  was toppled by the July Revolution in 1830.
parts.answer: Charles X (the tenth) [or Charles Philippe, Count of Artois; prompt on Charles]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This “Citizen King” elevated longtime ally François Guizot (FRAN-swah gee-ZOH) to prime  minister in 1847. This only Orléanist (UR-lee-AHN-ist) king of France took power when Charles X  stepped down and himself abdicated in 1848 after the June Days.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Louis Philippe won out in 1830 over supporters of restoring the house of this French emperor, who  was defeated at the Battle of Waterloo.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this warlord's death, his son Hideyori (HEE-day-YOR-ee) surrendered power to Tokugawa  Ieyasu (TOH-koo-GAH-wah EE-ay-YAH-soo). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this second “great unifier” of Japan, who launched the Imjin War and succeeded Oda  Nobunaga (OH-dah noh-boo-NAH-gah).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Imjin War consisted of two invasions of this peninsula, whose Joseon (joh-SAHN) navy forced  the Japanese to withdraw from Pyongyang.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hideyoshi also initiated the construction of a gigantic castle in, and named for, this city, where  Hideyoshi's son and wife Yodo-dono (yoh-doh-doh-noh) committed ritual suicide after the Tokugawa  burned the structure down.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Iditarod, a large sled dog race. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this state, where the Iditarod takes place. This state’s capital is Juneau.

parts.question: Although Juneau is Alaska’s capital, it is not on the Iditarod route. Instead, the race begins in this most  populous city in Alaska.

parts.question: [H] A leader of the Sons of Liberty with this surname organized the Boston Tea Party. Another man with this surname signed the Alien and Sedition Acts as president during the Quasi-War.
parts.answer: Adams [or Samuel “Sam” Adams; or John Adams]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Misfit kills the grandmother, while his associates kill the rest of Bailey’s family, in this Flannery O’Connor short story.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this financial instrument that, like the “fixed” type, is typically used for home purchases. This product, however, may “balloon” after an introductory period.
parts.answer: adjustable-rate mortgages (accept ARM; accept variable-rate mortgage; accept descriptive answers like “a mortgage where the interest rate can change;” prompt on “mortgage,” “loan,” or “home loan”)

parts.question: A thousand dollar loan may ultimately cost a borrower more than two thousand dollars to pay back; the extra money is the interest, while this term refers to the original thousand dollars that is paid back.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Grandfather clocks feature these harmonic oscillators, which naturally hang straight down and swing from left to right.

parts.question: When the harmonic oscillator is this type of compressible coil, then the formula for the restoring force is called Hooke’s Law.

parts.question: A harmonic oscillator may be simple, in which the only force acting on it is the restoring force, or it may have this feature, in which another force counters the restoring force and reduces the oscillation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Before the 20th century, it was generally held that these beings dressed in red, not green. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these beings sometimes considered a type of fairy in Irish folklore. These beings are most often depicted as little, bearded shoe-makers who enjoy partaking in mischief.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In more modern myths about leprechauns, they are said to hide their pots of gold at the end of one of these colorful natural phenomena.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These other creatures in Irish folklore are said to have red eyes from continual weeping. These female mound spirits are said to shriek, wail, or keen at the imminent death of a family member.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This field is present when electrical charges move, and can be visualized by the orientation of iron filings. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this field denoted by the letter B, whose strength is measured in Teslas. The Earth’s field of this kind protects it from the solar wind and cosmic rays.
parts.answer: magnetic field [or the Earth’s geomagnetic field]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] These navigational devices use a magnetic needle and the earth’s magnetic field to point to magnetic north, which is slightly different from geographic north.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Compasses and bar magnets can point north because they have this strongest type of magnetism, which allows iron, cobalt, or nickel to form permanent magnets.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In artworks, these rulers were typically depicted with a false beard wearing an ornate skirt known as the shendyt (shen-dit). For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these ancient rulers, some of whom wore Pschent (p’SKENT) crowns that combined the red and white crowns of lower and upper Egypt. These Egyptian rulers were mummified and buried in sarcophagi.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The discovery of this pharaoh’s tomb was monumental because it was nearly fully intact, with very few artifacts stolen by grave robbers. Howard Carter discovered the tomb of this pharaoh, the youngest ruler of Egypt.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This pharaoh, the husband of Nefertiti, fathered Tutankhamen with an unknown woman known only as The Younger Lady. This pharaoh founded the city of Amarna and introduced monotheistic worship of the sun to Egypt.
parts.answer: Akhenaten [accept Echnaton or Ikhnaton or Khuenaten or Amenhotep IV or Amenophis IV; prompt on Amenhotep or Amenophis]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This former schoolmate of Paul Allen at Lakeside High dropped out of Harvard to create his own computer software company. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this billionaire, a co-founder and former CEO of Microsoft. This man founded a charitable organization that supports public health projects with his wife Melinda.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Bill and Melinda Gates’s other philanthropic endeavors include signing this commitment. This campaign encourages extremely wealthy people to donate the majority of their money.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This man co-founded the Giving Pledge with Bill and Melinda Gates. This man known as the “Oracle of Omaha” is known for his investment prowess and for being the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about American architects named Frank.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Frank Lloyd Wright designed this building in southwestern Pennsylvania for the Kaufmann family. This building uses cantilevered floors to extend over a waterfall.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Architect Frank Shaver Allen designed the Kenosha High School and Christ Episcopal Church in Joliet, a city in this state. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Robie House in this state’s city of Chicago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Frank Gehry designed a building of this type in Bilbao for the Guggenheim Foundation. Frank Lloyd Wright also designed one of these buildings for the Guggenheims, which is down the street from another one called MoMa.
parts.answer: art museum [do not accept or prompt on answers containing “gallery”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Otto Theodor Benfey created a version of this diagram nicknamed for its resemblance to a snail. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this diagram which demonstrates the Law of Octaves. This diagram arranges all known chemical elements into a chart that depicts their atomic weight, atomic number, and atomic symbol.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Russian chemist used the Law of Octaves to predict the properties of germanium, gallium, and scandium and in the process invented the periodic table.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The element named for Mendeleev, mendelevium, is in this series of elements, which contains five other elements named for people. This series of elements lies under the lanthanides on the periodic table.
parts.answer: actinides [prompt on rare earths or period 7]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This river was accidentally diverted into the Coachella Valley of Southern California in 1905, which formed the modern Salton Sea. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this river of the southwestern United States, which forms the border between California and Arizona.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Colorado River has now been tamed by measures such as this massive dam, the largest in the world when it was opened in 1935. This dam is named after a Depression-era president.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This artificial lake between Nevada and Arizona was formed by the accumulation of the Colorado River behind Hoover Dam. This lake and Lake Powell are the two largest artificial water reservoirs in the United States.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These cells, which are also known as erythrocytes, can form stacks called rouleaux (roo-LOH) due to their unique disk shape. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these cells of the circulatory system. The oxygen-binding protein hemoglobin gives these cells their characteristic color.
parts.answer: red blood cells [or RBCs; accept red blood corpuscles or erythroid cells or haematids]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Heme groups in hemoglobin contain this element, which allows them to bind to oxygen. This metal with symbol Fe is oxidized to form rust.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This disease causes red blood cells to change shape, preventing them from properly binding to oxygen. People who are heterozygous for this disease’s allele are less likely to get malaria.
parts.answer: sickle-cell anemia [or sickle-cell disease or SCA or SCD; prompt on anemia]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one appearance, this character cashes in over $20,000 in Mom Bucks to buy himself a new motorcycle. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this title character of the second book in a series by Jeff Kinney. This character owns a white van that sports his garage band’s name, Löded Diper, on its side, and spends most of his time tormenting his brother Greg.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Heffleys star in this series of journal-like books about Greg and his daily adventures as depicted by his simple drawings. Dog Days and Cabin Fever are books in this series.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Jeff Kinney was also the primary creator of this online role-playing game in which players travel between islands and complete quests. Wimpy Wonderland and Wimpy Boardwalk are islands in this game about Diary of a Wimpy Kid that feature alongside other islands like Astro-Knights and Time Tangled.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Hermitian examples of these things consist of complex conjugates. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these things which are reduced into row-echelon form through Gaussian elimination. These rectangular arrays of numbers can only be multiplied if the column number of the first matches the row number of the second.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Logical matrices only contain values of zero and this number. In Boolean logic, zero corresponds to false while this number corresponds to true.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Boolean logic is this type of system, because there are only two possible values: true or false. Another system with this name uses ones and zeros to code for information in computers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The lwa that adherents to this religion venerate are associated with Roman Catholic saints. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Afro-Caribbean religion that originated in Haiti. Although the practice of sticking pins into effigies to induce illness is not prominent in this religion, those “dolls” are still named after this religion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] One branch of Vodou that developed from the practices of the African diaspora is named for this state. That branch of Vodou became syncretized with the Francophone culture of this state’s city of New Orleans.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Another branch of Vodou is named for its development in this island country in the Spanish Empire. Santería is an African diasporic religion practiced in this country that is often confused with Vodou practices.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man’s Doctor’s Plot involved accusing a group of Jewish doctors in Moscow of plotting to assassinate Soviet leaders. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this leader who aided a campaign of political repression and genocide known as the Great Purge. This leader, who organized his country’s economy into five-year plans, was the Soviet leader during World War II.
parts.answer: Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin [accept Ioseb Besarionis dzе Jugashvili]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] After Stalin’s death, this successor of his denounced him in a “Secret Speech” called “On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Kruschev and Stalin were both members of the Soviet party espousing this ideology. This ideology is structured around common ownership of the means of production, and was named after a manifesto written by Karl Marx.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The song of this river’s boatmen was arranged for orchestra by Igor Stravinsky. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this longest river in Europe, whose canal to the Don River helps ultimately connect cities like Kazan and Nizhny Novgorod to the ocean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Vologorad, a city on the Volga River, was previously known by this name. The massive Motherland Calls statue commemorates the five-month-long World War II siege of Volgograd under this name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Volgograd now lies in this country, the largest successor of the USSR.
parts.answer: Russia [or Russian Federation or Rossiyskaya Federatsiya or Rossiya]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared “friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled “Tryst with Destiny.” This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
parts.answer: Jawaharlal Nehru [accept Pandit Nehru or Chacha Nehru]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This was the surname of Nehru’s daughter, the first female Prime Minister of India. This was also the surname of a political leader who led nonviolent protests against British rule over India and was given the title Mahatma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During her time as Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi went to war with this country in support of Bangladesh’s independence. On the other hand, Mahatma Gandhi was against separation of India and this western neighbor.
parts.answer: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The motion of these devices can be simplified using the small-angle approximation, to solve the resulting differential equation. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these devices consisting of a weight suspended from a pivot that swings freely. Examples of these devices are often used in grandfather clocks.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pendulums are examples of these devices, which undergo periodic motion in which the restoring force is proportional to the magnitude of the object’s displacement. Another example of these devices is a mass on a spring.
parts.answer: simple harmonic oscillator or SHO [prompt on oscillator]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Leon Foucault (foo-KOH) used a pendulum to demonstrate the motion of this body. The quantity “little g” in the equation for a simple pendulum represents the acceleration due to the gravitational pull of this body.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This app is known in China as “Douyin.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this social media app that consists of short videos, often of people doing dances dubbed with music or other audio recordings.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This page on TikTok recommends videos to users based on the way the user interacts with the app. This page is located to the right of the “following” page.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In August 2020, President Trump accused this company, the owner of TikTok, of providing the Chinese government with users’ private information. This company began talks with Microsoft, but entered a partnership with Oracle instead.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The title character of this novel “had not the option” to be romantically involved with Sally Seton. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give this novel named after a character whose first name is Clarissa. In this novel, Septimus Smith is seen in the park before he jumps out of a hospital window to commit suicide.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This English author of Mrs. Dalloway wrote the stream-of-consciousness novel To The Lighthouse. She also created Judith, a fictional sister of William Shakespeare, in her essay “A Room of One’s Own.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] "A Room of One's Own" argues that women need money and physical space to establish a metaphorical space in the literary world. It's seen as an important text in this movement that advocates equality of the sexes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These fruits are made by trees in the genus Prunus, which makes them closely related to other fruits like plums, peaches, nectarines, and apricots. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these fruits which are classified as drupes, or stone fruits. These red, fleshy fruits can be soaked in sugar syrup and food coloring to make the maraschino kind, which is used alongside beverages.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Maraschino cherries are often made using two main types of cherries, one of which is this type of cherry which was developed in Washington state. These cherries are named for a mountain near Seattle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The other type used to make maraschinos, Royal Anne cherries, are also named for this man, whose coronation was depicted by Jacques-Louis David (dah-VEED). This French emperor was not actually of below average height.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man learned how to read and write by watching local ship workers. For ten points:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this former slave who published the The North Star and wrote “What to the Slave is the Fourth of July.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Douglass was the only African-American attendee of this event, which was planned by Elizabeth Cady Stanton. This event culminated in the Declaration of Sentiments.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Stanton fought for this right, which, nearly 70 years after the Seneca Falls Convention, was granted through the 19th amendment.
parts.answer: women’s suffrage [accept equivalents like women getting the right to vote or female suffrage; prompt on just suffrage or the right to vote by asking “For whom?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about the martial art of capoeira (kah-poh-AIR-ah).

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Capoeira developed as a way for slaves to train martial arts in this country, where escaped slaves often founded settlements called quilombos (kee-LOM-bohz). Today, capoeira is practiced primarily in this country’s favelas.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Capoeira uses music to disguise the martial arts, using instruments such as the pandeiro and atabaque (ah-tah-BOCK-ee), which are this type of instrument. These instruments, which include most drums, are played by being struck.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Capoeira batizados, or ceremonial graduations, often end with performing this activity, combining styles such as Maculele and Samba. Other kinds of this art form include Bachata, Merengue (muh-REN-gay), and Tango.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Each of these symbols are associated with either yin or yang as well as one of the Five Phases: fire, water, earth, metal, and wood. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this 12-sign classification system based on the lunar calendar. This cycle starts with the symbol of the rat since, according to myth, he won a race held by the Jade Emperor by riding on the ox.
parts.answer: Chinese zodiac signs [or shēngxiào; accept descriptive answers; prompt on zodiac signs]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This fourth animal in the Chinese zodiac cycle follows the tiger. The Jade one of these animals is said to have a mortar and pestle and accompany the immortal Chang’e (chong-UH) on the moon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This simian creature follows the goat in the Chinese zodiac cycle. One of the Four Chinese classics titled Journey to the West features a “king” of this general order of primates named Sun Wukong.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lie groups provide a natural model for the continuous form of this property. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property, the radial or rotational form of which is possessed by objects which look the same after a partial turn or rotation. Human bodies have the bilateral form of this property.
parts.answer: symmetry [accept radial, rotational, bilateral, or reflectional symmetry]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Functions described by this adjective lack symmetry across the y-axis. If negative f of x equals f of negative x, then f of x has this property, which also describes numbers that cannot be divided by two.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These mathematical constructs possess self-similarity, a property also known as expanding symmetry. Examples of these constructs include the Dragon Curve, the Koch (kahk) Snowflake, and the Sierpinski Triangle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The protagonist of this novel plays a flawless game of Pac-Man and wins a coin that turns out to be an extra life token. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this novel by Ernest Cline about Wade’s search for an Easter Egg in the OASIS (oh-AY-sis), a virtual reality world created by James Halliday. Wade goes by the avatar name “Parzival” when in the OASIS.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Ready Player One is set in 2045 and is part of this genre of literature characterized by a depiction of a severe decline in society. This genre’s name, which is Greek for “bad place,” is an antonym of “utopia.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In Ready Player One, players who search for the Easter Egg left by Halliday are referred to by this term. At the end of the novel, all the players described by this term band together to defeat the corporate forces of IOI.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In order to marry the lady-in-waiting Sophie Chotek, this man had to renounce his descendants’ rights to the throne. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this nephew of Emperor Franz Joseph I, who was assassinated in Sarajevo in 1914. This man’s death prompted the July Crisis, which eventually caused the escalations that led to World War I.
parts.answer: Franz Ferdinand [accept Archduke Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ferdinand was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip (PRIN-tzip), a member of the revolutionary movement Young Bosnia and one of a group of assassins working with this Serbian secret military society.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] As the eldest son of Archduke Karl Ludwig of this country, Ferdinand was the heir presumptive to its throne. The union of this country and Hungary was allied with the German Empire in World War I.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Maulana Karenga created this holiday during the aftermath of the Watts riots in 1966. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this holiday celebrated from December 26 to January 1 every year, ending with a feast of faith called Karamu Ya Imani. This holiday was developed as an annual celebration of African-American culture.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A common symbol of Kwanzaa, the kinara, features seven of these objects to represent the seven principles of Kwanzaa. In Judaism, nine of these objects are placed on the menorah during Hanukkah.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Kwanzaa began as an alternative to this holiday, because Karenga believed Jesus to be psychotic. However, many people practice both Kwanzaa and this holiday, which is on the day before Kwanzaa starts, December 25.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Questions like “What men or gods are these?” and “What wild ecstasy?” are addressed to the title “foster-child of silence and slow time” in this poem. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this poem whose narrator proclaims “More happy love! more happy, happy love!” that ends with a statement of “Beauty is truth, truth beauty,—that is all / Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] “Ode on a Grecian Urn” was written by this English Romantic poet of “Endymion” (en-DIE-mee-uhn) as well as many other odes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] One such ode by Keats is dedicated to one of these animals. That poem about one of these animals calls it a “light-winged Dryad of the trees” and is titled “Ode to a Nightingale.” A poem about another of these animals by Percy Shelley asks “how could thy notes flow in such a crystal stream?” and is titled “To a Skylark.”
parts.answer: birds [anti-prompt on nightingale or skylark; anti-prompt on “Ode to a Nightingale” or “To a Skylark”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about Renaissance Italian sculptor Donatello.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Donatello created the first ever free-standing bronze sculpture, which depicts this Biblical figure. In Donatello's depiction, this man holds a sword and rests his foot on the head of his slain enemy, Goliath.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Donatello was born in and studied classical sculpture in this Italian city. He also created sculptures of St. George and St. Mark for the Orsanmichele (or-san-mee-KEH-lay) in this city, which is also the site of the Uffizi Gallery.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Donatello also created many of these monuments, including ones for Cardinal Rainaldo Brancacci (brahn-KAH-chee) and Antipope John XXIII. Sepulchres (SEP-ul-kerz) and mausoleums are types of these monuments in or under which people are buried.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One leader of this former territory issued the Law of the Splintered Paddle while uniting its 6 major islands. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this island state, the most recent to join the US. This state’s "Big Island" shares its name with the state as a whole.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This capital of Hawaiʻi is home to a cosmopolitan district known as Waikiki. It is serviced by the David K Inouye (ih-NO-ay) International Airport.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The construction of the Thirty Meter Telescope on this tallest mountain on Hawaiʻi’s Big Island has been heavily protested by Native Hawaiians. This is the most sacred mountain in Hawaiian culture.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Levels of this molecule are decreased by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-controlling enzyme of the mevalonate pathway. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this molecule whose levels in the body can be decreased by statins. This molecule comes in a “good” HDL and a “bad” LDL form, high levels of which can block blood vessels and increase risk of heart disease.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Cholesterol serves as an essential structural component in this organelle. This organelle described by the fluid mosaic model consists of a phospholipid bilayer and separates the inside of the cell from its environment.
parts.answer: cell membrane or plasma membrane [do not accept or prompt on “cell wall”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] These compounds also known as lipids have a strong inverse relationship with HDL, or “good”, cholesterol. The body primarily stores these compounds in adipose tissue, high levels of which contribute to obesity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Cayley’s theorem considers all groups as a group of these entities. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these entities, which are the elements of symmetric groups. These entities are the different arrangements of the elements of a set, in which the particular order of the arrangement matters.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The number of permutations for a set of n distinct objects is this function of n. This function of n is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n, and is represented by an exclamation point.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This number is equal to zero factorial and therefore represents the number of permutations for a set of zero objects. This number is the multiplicative identity because any number times this number is the original number.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man reportedly died from a nosebleed on his wedding night. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this general who was known as the “Scourge of God” for his brutal battle tactics. Pope Leo I supposedly convinced this leader of the Huns not to sack rome.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Attila crossed the Rhine and reached Aurelianorum in an attempt to conquer this region, though he was stopped at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains. This region corresponds roughly to modern-day France.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Attila legendarily carried a weapon that was most likely referred to as “sword of the war god.” The historian Priscus referred to the weapon as the sword of this specific war god, the Roman counterpart of Ares.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about examples of onomatopoeia, in which words sound like the sounds they describe.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The phrase Autosomal Dominant Compelling Helio-Ophthalmic Outburst Syndrome is a spurious acronym for the onomatopoeic word “achoo”, the sound of doing this. “Bless you” is a common response to someone doing this.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This onomatopoeia is meant to represent the sound of a bird of the same name, a common example of brood parasitism. That bird sound is also used in clocks that often depict these birds and play their sound every hour.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Roy Lichtenstein’s painting named for an example of onomatopoeia, Whaam!, was inspired by this type of art. This type of art often inspired many works by Lichtenstein and other pop artists, who used Ben-Day dots.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Black Hills are an isolated mountain range almost entirely in the western portion of this state. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this state whose largest city is Sioux (soo) Falls and whose capital is Pierre.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Black Hills are home to this National Memorial, a sculpture of the faces of four presidents.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Near Mount Rushmore is an incomplete sculpture of this man which has been under construction since 1948. Along with Sitting Bull, this Lakota leader was present at the Battle of the Little Bighorn.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country formed an army corps with Australia that fought in the Gallipoli campaign and is honored on ANZAC Day. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, the location of silver ferns, which are featured on its airline’s planes and its coat of arms. This island country, whose capital is Wellington, is located southeast of Australia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The silver fern is also a common motif in the art of these indigenous New Zealanders. These peoples signed the Treaty of Waitangi for peace with the British, and are often compared to Australian Aborigines.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The first European to sight New Zealand was this Dutch explorer. This explorer names an island just south of Australia, which was once known as Van Diemen’s Land.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The program GIMPS searches for new examples of these numbers, which are tested for in the Lucas-Lehmer test. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these numbers. Specific versions of these numbers which are in the form of two to the n minus one for an integer n are named for Marin Mersenne.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Euclid-Euler (YOOK-lid OY-ler) theorem shows that there is a one-to-one relationship between Mersenne primes and even examples of these numbers. These numbers are equal to the sum of their positive divisors, excluding themselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This number is the smallest perfect number, because it is equal to the sum of its divisors one, two, and three. This number is also the number of sides on a hexagon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The story “In the Rukh” describes this character’s discovery by Gisborne, a British Forest Officer. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this character who was raised by a pack of wolves in the jungle. This character uses fire as a weapon to fend off the tiger Shere Khan and later kills him by trapping him in a ravine during a stampede.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Mowgli’s stories can be found in this collection of stories that also features stories about the mongoose Rikki-Tikki-Tavi and Baloo the bear. The character of Mowgli stars in a 1967 Disney adaptation of this name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Jungle Book was written by this English author of the novel Kim and the poem “Gunga Din.” This author was the first English-language writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some Westernizing efforts in this country included educational reforms under the advisement of John Dewey and the Hat Law of 1925, which banned the use of the fez in favor of more Western-style hats. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country which had its borders redefined in the Treaty of Lausanne. Soon after, this country moved its capital to Ankara, though its most populous city is Istanbul.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This leader enacted many westernization efforts in Turkey, as a part of his Six Arrows ideology. This leader overthrew the final sultan of the Ottoman empire and became the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
parts.answer: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk [accept Kamal Ataturk or Mustafa Kemal Pasha or Mustafa Kemal]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Ataturk abolished the caliphate that had power over Turkey, though he did not attempt to eradicate this religion. The Ottoman millet system allowed religious minorities to live outside this religion’s Sharia law.

parts.question: The title of this novel has come to mean any paradoxical and confusing situation, but originally refers to a rule that only sane pilots can fly missions, but that wanting to fly missions is a sign of insanity. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel that centers on Captain John Yossarian’s (yo-SAHR-ee-uhn) experiences as a U.S. Army pilot.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The 256th US Army Air Squadron is stationed on the island of Pianosa off the coast of Italy during this war. Night by Elie Wiesel and If This is a Man by Primo Levi are about the Holocaust, which occurred during this war.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Perhaps the most famous work of Holocaust literature is this author’s diary, which was mostly written in hiding during the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands. She later died in Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

parts.question: “Raindrops on roses and whiskers on kittens / Bright copper kettles and warm woolen mittens” is from a song that Maria sings in this film, which is about her favorite things. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this 1965 film that stars Julie Andrews as Maria and was inspired by the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical of the same name. Some songs from this film include Do-Re-Mi and My Favorite Things.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In the Sound of Music, Maria becomes a governess for this family and teaches the children to sing, and eventually falls for the widowed naval captain father.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Sound of Music takes place in Salzburg, the fourth largest city in this European country. The song “Edelweiss” (eyd-l-vahys) from the musical symbolized Captain Von Trapp’s loyalty to this country, whose capital is Vienna.

parts.question: The March of Dimes was originally founded to combat this disease. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this disease that primarily affects children and in some cases necessitates iron lungs to survive. Franklin Delano Roosevelt notably contracted this disease and survived.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] FDR’s work to combat polio, specifically with the March of Dimes, eventually led to the creation of this type of substance. These substances typically present the body with weaker versions of the virus to increase immunity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In 1953, with help from the March of Dimes, this man developed the first successful polio vaccine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: B.F. Skinner used operant conditioning to train these animals to play ping pong. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these animals, which Skinner also attempted to train to guide missiles for the US Navy. These birds were sometimes used in wartime to deliver messages, especially the “messenger” or “homing” types.
parts.answer: pigeon [accept doves or Columbidae or Columbiformes; prompt on birds or Aves or animals or Animalia or chordates or Chordata]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Skinner also trained pigeons to pass a common behavioral test named for these objects, which involves placing a dot on that object and seeing if the animal recognizes itself or thinks it sees another animal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This substance produced by pigeons was considered a valuable commodity because of its use in gunpowder. This substance was also used as a fertilizer because it is more potent that farmyard manure.
parts.answer: guano [accept feces or excrement or poop; prompt on manure]

parts.question: The chelating agent EDTA is often used in the complexometric form of this technique, which is used to detect metal ions in solution. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this lab technique, which can be used to determine the concentration of an unknown solution. In this technique, the endpoint occurs at a pH value determined by the indicator used.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] One form of titration distinguishes between these compounds and their counterparts using indicators like phenolphthalein (FEEN-ol-THAL-een). These substances have a pH value less than 7, unlike bases.

parts.question: [M] This scientist defined acids and bases as electron pair acceptors and donors, respectively. This scientist also names diagrams that uses lines to represent bonds between atoms, known as his “dot structures”

parts.question: Zeus was not very loyal to his wife. For ten points each, answer the following about demigods who were sons of Zeus and his lovers.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] This king of Sybilus was the son of Zeus and the nymph Plouto. He was punished for feeding the gods his son Pelops, who had his shoulder replaced by Hephaestus after it was swallowed by Demeter.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This son of Zeus and Alcmene (alk-MEE-nee) is often depicted with a club and the hide of the Nemean Lion. Slaying the Hydra was one of this legendarily strong hero's 12 labors.
parts.answer: Heracles [accept Hercules; accept Alcaeus; accept Alcides]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This demigod was the son of Danaë (DAN-ay), whom Zeus impregnated in the form of a golden shower. This hero was given Hades’ helm of darkness and advice from the Graeae to help him slay a gorgon.

parts.question: In this movie, Ulysses Klaue works with Killmonger to steal an African artifact, which he unknowingly tries to sell to an undercover CIA agent in Korea. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Marvel movie about T’Challa, the king of an isolated African country.. The phrase “Wakanda Forever” was popularized after this movie, whose title superhero was played by Chadwick Boseman.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In Black Panther, this woman heals CIA agent Everett Ross after a spinal injury using vibranium technology. This tech-savvy sister of T’Challa created the Black Panther suits.

parts.question: [M] In the end credits scene of Black Panther, Shuri is seen helping this man with his recuperation. This man uses a vibranium arm under the alias White Wolf, though Captain America usually refers to him as Bucky.

parts.question: One holder of this office under Franklin Roosevelt said it wasn’t worth a “bucket of warm spit.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this office, holders of which under FDR included John Garner and Henry A. Wallace. This position is called in to break ties in the Senate and is first in line to succeed the president.
parts.answer: Vice President of the United States [accept VP]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This politician had no vice president during his first term as president, but ran with Alben W. Barkley for his second term. This politician served as FDR’s last vice president, and succeeded him after his death.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] FDR’s former VP Henry A. Wallace opposed this plan, which Truman passed as president. This plan, named after the Secretary of State at the time, had the US give foreign aid to Western Europe to recover after World War II.
parts.answer: Marshall Plan [accept European Recovery Program or ERP; do not accept or prompt on “European Economic Recovery Plan”]

parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about musicals by Andrew Lloyd Webber.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This Lloyd Webber musical tells of the annual Jellicle Ball, where the title animals decide which one will be reborn after ascending to Heaviside Layer. T.S. Eliot’s poetry provided most of the lyrics to this feline musical.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Webber also wrote this musical about the title character whose facial deformations force him to wear a mask. That character sings “The Music of the Night” after luring his love into his lair under an opera house.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other musical by Lloyd Webber concentrates on the life of the title political leader from Argentina, the second wife of Juan Peron. That title character sings from her balcony in the song “Don’t Cry for Me Argentina.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about ancient Roman attire. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This type of robe was often worn by senators. Usually woven from white wool, it was draped over the shoulder and wrapped around the body.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Roman generals wore laurel crowns and purple togas during these ceremonies, which celebrated a successful war. Cleopatra avoided being paraded through one of these events by committing suicide.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Absolutely no attire was worn by athletes in these ancient games celebrated by the ancient Greeks and later by the Romans. The modern version of these athletic games started in 1896 and continues to this day, the 2021 version set to be held in Tokyo.
parts.answer: the Olympics [or the Olympic Games; accept the Ancient Olympics or the Modern Olympics]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Grashof number approximates the ratio of forces caused by this force to viscous forces. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this upward force exerted by fluids on an immersed object, the magnitude of which is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. This force gives objects the ability to float on water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This scientist’s principle states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. After making a discovery in the bathtub, this ancient Greek scientist ran naked in the streets shouting “Eureka!”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Archimedes names one of these devices, which is used to continuously transport water through a pipe. These simple machines are created by wrapping an inclined plane around a cylinder.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this city, “ancient grudge break[s] to new mutiny” and “civil blood makes civil blood unclean.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this city that features “Two households, both alike in dignity.” A play set in this city opens with a fight between Sampson and Gregory that is broken up by Prince Escalus.
parts.answer: Verona [prompt on but do not otherwise reveal the city in which Romeo and Juliet is set]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Those two households are the Capulets and this other house. Benvolio is a member of this house whose cousin falls in love with a member of the Capulets after seeing her at a party.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The feud between the Montagues and the Capulets serves as the central conflict in this Shakespearean tragedy. This play ends as the two young title lovers commit suicide, each assuming that the other is dead.

parts.question: This eight day holiday, which commemorates the Maccabean Revolt, starts on the 25th of Kislev. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Jewish holiday, called the “Festival of Lights”, in which participants eat jelly donuts, known as Sufganiyot, and spin dreidels.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In this other eight day holiday, beginning on the 15th of Tishrei, participants shake a lulav and etrog. The eighth day of this holiday is known as Shemeni Atzeret.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] 5 days before Sukkot, Jews celebrate this day of atonement with a 25 hour fast that begins with Kol Nidre (coal NEE-dray) and ends with Neila.

parts.question: The Pacific is divided into three main regions. Answer some questions about them, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This is the largest of the three regions, and is the namesake of a French territory and a wayfaring people, of which Moana is one.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Polynesia is shaped roughly like a triangle, its eastern terminus being this island under the control of Chile. This island is home to large head statues called Moai.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other Pacific region is named for the small islands within it. A country named the Federated States of this region has its capital at Palikir.

parts.question: This city is home to the Casa Rosada, a pink presidential place where Juan Peron lived for some time. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city where thousands of mothers gather in this city’s Plazo de Mayo to mourn for the loss of their children during the Dirty War. It is the largest city and capital of Argentina.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Argentina claims sovereignty over the South Sandwich Islands and this other group of islands in the South Atlantic. In the 1980s, Argentina fought and lost a war with the United Kingdom, at the time led by Maragaret Thatcher, for these islands.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Argentina splits Tierra Del Fuego, another island group, with this neighboring country. This country controls Easter Island and has a capital at Santiago.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this position, holders of which have primarily ceremonial and symbolic powers over the United Kingdom and commonwealth realms. The current holder of this position is Elizabeth II.
parts.answer: Queen of the United Kingdom [accept King or Monarch of the United Kingdom, Head of the Commonwealth, Defender of the Faith; prompt on His Majesty or Her Majesty]

parts.question: [H] Elizabeth II belongs to this reigning royal house, as the granddaughter of its founder King George V. This house shares a name with a large castle just outside of London.

parts.question: For ten points, each answer some questions about diacritical marks, symbols placed over letters.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] These diacritics are placed above letters to indicate nasalization. These wave-shaped marks are placed above the letter n in Spanish to make the ñ (enye) sound, such as in the word piñata.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] These marks are often placed above letters like a, o, or u to indicate a change in vowel quality. Though not diaeresis, these diacritics are represented by two dots and have a name stemming from German.

parts.question: [E] Umlauts and other accents are most commonly applied to these letters. These letters, which have sounds produced with an open vocal tract, are contrasted with consonants.

parts.question: [M] Benzene’s cyclic nature was confirmed by Kathleen Lonsdale, who used x-rays undergoing this process to do so. This process causes waves to bend around an encountered obstacle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In the Birch reduction of benzene, one of these structures is reduced. Benzene’s structure consists of single bonds alternating with these bonds, represented by two lines on a Lewis diagram.

parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about the miracles of Jesus.

parts.question: [H] The shortest verse in the King James Bible, “Jesus wept,” occurs after Jesus is invited to see this man’s burial place. Martha, his sister, then shows the site to Jesus, who prays to God and resurrects him.
parts.answer: Lazarus of Bethany [accept Lazarus of the Four Days or Saint Lazarus]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Another miracle of Jesus occurred at the Marriage at Cana, where Jesus turned this substance into wine. In a separate miracle, Jesus walked on this substance, in the Sea of Galilee.
parts.answer: water [accept H2O or hydric acid or dihydrogen monoxide]

parts.question: [M] In a miracle called “feeding the multitude,” Jesus fed four thousand people with a small amount of fish and this food. The Eucharist is considered a miracle because it turns this food into his body.

parts.question: Though many authors have written that this structure is large enough to be seen from the moon, it is sometimes not even visible from low Earth orbits. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this defensive fortification which, stretching from Liaodong to Lop Lake, protected China from Xiongnu (shong-NU) raids.

parts.question: [H] This Chinese emperor combined numerous pre-existing walls to form the Great Wall of China. This emperor, who ended the Warring States period by founding the Qin (chin) dynasty, was buried with an army of terracotta soldiers.
parts.answer: Shi Huangdi [or Qin Shi Huang or Ying Zheng or Zhao Zheng; prompt on Qin]

parts.answer: J. D. Salinger [accept Jerome David Salinger]

parts.answer: Tupac Amaru Shakur [accept either underlined portion]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One moon of this planet has the highest albedo of any body in the solar system for ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this planet orbited by Enceladus (en-SELL-ah-dus). This planet appears pale yellow due to ammonia crystals in its atmosphere, which also features periodic storms known as the Great White Spot.

parts.question: The same nursery rhyme is hung in every guest’s room in this novel. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel about ten seemingly unrelated people who are invited to an isolated island off the Devon Coast by U. N. Owen. Those guests are killed off one by one, and their deaths are mirrored by a decreasing number of figurines on the dining room table.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] And Then There Were None is a novel by this English mystery author of Death on the Nile and The Murder of Roger Ackroyd who created the Belgian detective Hercule Poirot (PWAH-roh).

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this organized criminal enterprise based in cities like New York and Chicago, often referred to as “La Cosa Nostra” by its members. It was represented in films like The Godfather movies.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Italian-American Mafia rose to prominence by selling bootleg alcohol following the passage of this policy, which outlawed the consumption and sale of alcohol.

parts.question: [H] The Italian-American Mafia can trace its roots to this Italian island, where original members extorted lemon farmers to pay “protection money” for help against potential thieves. The Mafia was largely eradicated from this island following the Maxi Trial.

parts.question: These particles share the atomic nucleus with, and are slightly more massive than, protons. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these neutrally charged particles, whose number determines the isotope of an atom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This force holds atomic nuclei together despite the electrical repulsion of neutrons and protons. This force has an extremely small range, the shortest of the four fundamental forces.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Republican senator who served as Senate Majority Leader from 2015 to 2021.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] McConnell said “Nevertheless, she persisted,” to refer to this senator’s actions during Jeff Sessions’ confirmation hearing. This senator from Massachusetts faced controversy over claims of Native American ancestry.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] McConnell represents this state in the Senate with Rand Paul. The highly publicized shooting of Breonna Taylor took place in a city in this state.

parts.question: This figure stole the secret of fire from the goddess Mahuika (mah-WEE-kah) after she threw her burning fingernails at him. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this hero who crawled into the body of the Goddess of the Night in an attempt to make mankind immortal. This figure sings “You’re Welcome” and is voiced by Dwayne The Rock Johnson in Moana.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Maui (mah-wee) is credited with the creation of the Hawaiian islands, which lie on this large body of water. Polynesian mythology originates from the culture of native people who live on islands in this largest ocean.

parts.answer: Maui’s fish hook [prompt on just hook]

parts.question: In one work by this composer, Prince Ivan defeats Kashchei (kuh-SHAY) with the help of the title animal. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this composer who included an “Infernal Dance” in his The Firebird. Another work by this composer sparked a riot at its Paris premiere and is called The Rite of Spring.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Stravinsky’s The Firebird and The Rite of Spring are works of this type. Stravinsky composed many works for this type of dance, often performed with specialized pointe shoes by tutu-wearing dancers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Stravinsky’s ballet Petrushka tells the story of the Wizard bringing to life three of these objects. In another work, one of these objects was brought to life after it was made by the woodcarver Geppetto.

parts.question: [M] T cells and other lymphocytes are blood cells named for this color. Neutrophils, basophils, and B cells are also cells named for this color, which act as the cells of the immune system.

parts.question: This country was ruled by a politician who claimed to have fought alongside the Americans in the Bataan Death March, though United States Army documents described those claims as “absurd.” For ten points each:

parts.question: [H] Name this country which was ruled by a kleptocratic dictator whose wife Imelda is known for owning thousands of pairs of shoes. That ruler, Ferdinand Marcos, was overthrown in this country’s People Power Revolution.

parts.question: This poem begins “midway in the journey of our life” and describes the protagonist’s encounter with a leopard, a lion, and a she-wolf. For ten points each:

parts.answer: The Divine Comedy [accept La Divina Commedia]

parts.question: [E] Dante wrote The Divine Comedy in this language. Petrarch, who wrote Il Canzoniere (IL cahn-zohn-EE-er-eh) and is often credited with initiating the Renaissance, wrote in this European language.

parts.question: The United States’ largest city is actually mostly composed of islands. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The heart of New York City is this island, site of the Harlem neighborhood and Central Park. The Williamsburg Bridge connects this island to the borough of Brooklyn.

parts.question: [M] Both Brooklyn and the borough of Queens are on this island, New York state’s largest. This island also contains the Hamptons, a popular vacation spot for the city’s most affluent residents.

parts.question: In this game, new players are hailed as “chief” by in-game villagers. For ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this mobile game where a player upgrades their Town Hall to go on raids and collect gold and elixir. In this game, players can join in-game groups and wage war on one another.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Chlorine belongs to this only group of the periodic table to have elements in all three phases of matter at room temperature, which lies directly to the left of the noble gases on the periodic table.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Denver is the capital of this state, where the Front Range is mostly located and which, on average, has the highest altitude among US states.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Front Range forms part of this boundary that runs down the Americas, which separates water that flows towards the Pacific from water that flows towards the Atlantic.
parts.answer: the Continental Divide [or the Continental Divide of the Americas or the Great Divide]

parts.question: At this figure’s funeral, her personal trainer Bryant Johnson did three push-ups in front of her casket. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this recently deceased justice who was nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993. This first Jewish woman to serve in her position died on the eve of Rosh Hashanah on September 18, 2020.
parts.answer: Ruth Bader Ginsburg [or RBG or the Notorious RBG]

parts.question: [E] Ginsburg served as an associate justice on this highest court in the federal judiciary system in the United States. John Roberts is the current Chief Justice of this national judiciary body.
parts.answer: Supreme Court of the United States [accept SCOTUS; prompt on court]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Donald Trump nominated this woman as Ginsburg’s replacement a week after her death, and she was quickly confirmed, despite the supposed precedent of Merrick Garland that justices were not to be confirmed in an election year.

parts.question: The region of Mesopotamia was home to some of the first civilizations in the world. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Mesopotamia was able to sustain large populations due to the ease of this practice. This practice is the cultivation of crops.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Mesopotamian civilization contained the city of Ashur and had rulers like Tigaleth-Pileser and Sennacherib. Its capital, Nineveh (NIN-ih-veh), hosted the largest library in the world at the time, built by Ashurbanipal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mesopotamia was known as the Fertile Crescent for the rich soil that the Euphrates (yoo-FRAY-tees) and this other river provided to the region. Baghdad lies on this river.

parts.question: According to Dante’s Inferno, this body of water can be found in the fifth circle of hell, where the wrathful fight on its banks and the sullen drown in its currents. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this river in the Greek underworld into which Achilles was dipped by Thetis. After the Titanomachy, Zeus decreed that oaths sworn on this river could not be broken.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Greek underworld is sometimes referred to by this name. This is also the name of the Greek god of the underworld who married Persephone after striking a deal with Demeter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In the Iliad, Zeus claims that this region of the underworld is “as far beneath Hades as heaven is above earth.” This deep abyss in the underworld was used as a dungeon for the most wicked of all and as a prison for the titans.

parts.question: The narrator of this novel steals food and a file for Abel Magwitch, an escaped convict whom he meets in the village churchyard. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel narrated by Pip, who visits the wealthy Miss Havisham at Satis House and falls in love with Estella, her cold and dismissive adoptive daughter.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This English author wrote Great Expectations. He also wrote about Ebenezer Scrooge’s encounters with the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Christmas Present, and Christmas Yet to Come in his novella A Christmas Carol.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Dickens set his novel A Tale of Two Cities in London and this French city. Quasimodo serves as the bellringer for a cathedral in this city in Victor Hugo’s The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

parts.question: This architect designed a tent-like building that looks over Lake Erie in Cleveland, Ohio. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this architect of the John F. Kennedy Presidential Library, the John Hancock Tower, and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, who died in 2019 at the age of 102.
parts.answer: I. M. Pei [or Ieoh Ming Pei]

parts.question: [M] Pei initially wanted to make the John F. Kennedy Library this three-dimensional shape, a shape which he later used in the design of his Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and for the glass building in front of the Louvre (loov).

parts.question: This organ contains numerous mechanoreceptors, including Pacinian (puh-SIN-ee-an) corpuscles and Merkel nerve endings. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest organ of the human body, which also acts as its first line of defense against infection. The epidermis is the outermost of the layers of this organ that covers the body.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This pigment in skin can protect humans from UV radiation and can prevent some of the reactions that lead to skin cancer. Dark skin is generally rich in this pigment, the primary determinant of skin color.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This protein is a key structural material in the outer layers of skin in many vertebrates. The hard beta forms of this protein are found in bird beaks and claws, while the softer alpha forms are found in humans’ hair and nails.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] During Jackson’s presidency, his Secretary of War’s wife was snubbed socially by a group Washington society women led by the wife of Vice President John C. Calhoun. That woman, whose first name was Peggy, had this last name.
parts.answer: Eaton Affair [accept the Peggy Eaton Affair]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Peggy Eaton Affair led to the creation of an unofficial group of advisors to Jackson nicknamed the “kitchen” version of this body. In general, this body largely consists of the Secretaries of the executive departments.

parts.question: [M] Name this region of space where Ceres and Vesta are found. This region of small rocky bodies separates the inner and outer solar systems and is found between the fourth and fifth planets from the sun.

parts.question: [H] Name this title character of an epistolary novel who commits suicide after writing a letter requesting two pistols from his friend Albert. This character suffers from depression due to his unrequited love for Charlotte.
parts.answer: Werther [accept Young Werther; accept The Sorrows of Young Werther]

parts.answer: Indonesia [or Republic of Indonesia or Republik Indonesia]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Paolini’s Inheritance Cycle focuses on the almost-extinct race of these mythical creatures. Companions of these creatures are called Riders and Saphira and Thorn are two examples of these creatures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another childrens’series about dragons is titled Wings of [this substance]. In most depictions of dragons, they are said to be able to blow this hot substance out of their nostrils or mouth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Since this city is the only major American city without zoning laws, many single-family houses are in this city’s flood-prone coastal areas. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest city in Texas. Since the Johnson Space Center, which contains NASA’s mission control center, is located in this city, Apollo 13 reported to this city that “we have a problem.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Houston had its own problem in 2017 when this hurricane overfilled its Buffalo Bayou, causing widespread flooding in its downtown. This hurricane was the most costly since Katrina.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Houston replaced this other nearby city as Texas’s central port after a 1900 hurricane named after this city devastated it, in the deadliest natural disaster in U.S. history.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At only 18 years old, this artist suffered a bus accident that left her unable to walk for 3 months and gave her lifelong medical problems. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Mexican painter. She lived in her childhood home, nicknamed La Casa Azul, after her divorce with fellow artist Diego Rivera.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Kahlo is most famous for her numerous paintings of this type, including one with a thorn necklace and a hummingbird. These works that Kahlo painted of her own image often included her signature unibrow.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] One of this artist’s self-portraits depicts himself holding a palette and is painted over a portrait of his wife Suzanne Leenhoff. Other works by this artist include Olympia and Luncheon on the Grass.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about country music. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This woman is arguably the most famous female country artist. Songs from her 51 studio albums include “Jolene” and “Nine to Five.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This other classic country music star has also become a symbol of the genre with his songs “On the Road Again” and “Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The country music industry is mostly centered in this state, where the Country Music Hall of Fame is located in the city of Nashville. Other major cities in this state include Knoxville and Memphis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure was among the first rulers of a larger and unified India. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this first great king of India. He came in contact with Seleucus (seh-LOO-siss) I and became a Jain upon his abdication.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Chandragupta was able to conquer much of India by weaponizing these large animals, 500 of which he gifted to Seleucus. These tusked animals were also minted on some Indian coins.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This man was Chandragupta’s grandson. He also receded into a religious life upon his abdication, becoming a Buddhist. This leader ordered several of his proclamations in his Rock Edicts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Karst topography often has sinkholes and these structures. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these underground open chambers formed by rock dissolution. The ceilings and floors of these locations often display icicle-like formations formed by dripping water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Dripping water in caves can form these two kinds of structures, mineral deposits found on the ceilings and floors of caves. Name both.
parts.answer: stalactites AND stalagmites [accept answers in either order]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The most common form of stalactites and stalagmites are speleothems, which are primarily made of this rock. This rock contains large amounts of calcite and other forms of calcium carbonate.

parts.label: L
