parts.question: The Constitution and Declaration of Independence were both signed in this city, which was the de facto early capital of the United States. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city, whose Independence Hall was the site of many important events in early American history. This city is the most populous in Pennsylvania.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This iconically cracked bell was long hung in the steeple of Independence Hall in Philadelphia, and is said to have been rung to commemorate the reading of the Declaration of Independence.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Before the building of Washington DC, American congresses met elsewhere. This city in New York was the site of a 1754 convention about the French and Indian War that served as precursor to many later congresses.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A handwritten postscript in this novella that reads “Exterminate all the brutes!” is added to a report commissioned by the International Society for the Suppression of Savage Customs. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novella. Charles Marlow narrates this novella from a boat called Nellie and tells about his obsession with Kurtz, a successful ivory trader.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Heart of Darkness describes Marlow’s journey up the Congo River into the Congo Free State in this continent. Chinua Achebe, a Nigerian novelist from this continent, criticized the racist themes of Heart of Darkness in a lecture titled “An Image of [this continent].”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In “An Image of Africa,” Achebe called this author of Heart of Darkness a “bloody racist.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The term “Parsi” refers to followers of this religion in India. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this monotheistic Pre-Abrahamic religion from ancient Persia whose founding text is the Avesta. This religion’s adherents believe that Ahura Mazda is the supreme being.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A list of 101 of these things is a central concept in Zoroastrianism. The tetragrammaton is the four-letter Hebrew one of these words, usually articulated as Yahweh or Jehovah.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] During these ceremonies in Zoroastrianism, the two participants sprinkle cups of rice on each other for good luck. During these ceremonies, a priest blesses the bond between the bride and the groom.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Cubical knucklebones are thought to be precursors to these things’ use in gambling. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these things which are rolled to generate “random” numbers in many board games. The most commonly-used one of these things is shaped like a cube with one to six pips on each side.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Dice with four, six, eight, ten, twelve, and twenty sides are used in this tabletop role-playing game. For example, combat initiative in the fifth edition of this game is the sum of one’s Dexterity ability modifier and a “d20” roll.
parts.answer: Dungeons and Dragons [or DND or D and D; accept Advanced Dungeons and Dragons]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Many dice are shaped like regular polyhedra. The d4 has the shape of this simplest Platonic solid, which has four faces, six edges, and four corners.
parts.answer: tetrahedron [accept equilateral triangular pyramid; prompt on pyramid]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character teases Cherubino about having to leave his loose lifestyle to join the military in the aria “Non piu andrai.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character, whose name is repeated in the aria “Largo al Factotum.” This man is the title Barber of Seville in a work by Gioachino (joh-KEE-noh) Rossini, and Mozart composed The Marriage of [this man].

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Barber of Seville and The Marriage of Figaro are both comic examples of this type of musical composition. These works of classical music typically contain speech-like recitatives and often high-pitched singing arias.
parts.answer: opera [accept comic opera or opera buffa]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In another opera by Rossini, William Tell, the title character must perform this action at an apple sitting on his son’s head. Robin Hood is also extremely proficient at performing this action.
parts.answer: shooting an arrow [accept logical equivalents to using a bow and arrow or using a crossbow]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about the health benefits of laughter.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Laughter decreases levels of stress hormones, such as cortisol and this hormone, also known as epinephrine. A rush of this hormone which mediates the “fight or flight” response is created by heightened emotions.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] An hour of laughter can burn up to 100 calories because it involves contraction of this muscle. This abdominal muscle’s contraction increases the thorax and therefore inflates the lungs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Laughter is indeed the best medicine, because it decreases stress by increasing levels of these hormones. These hormones which reduce pain and boost pleasure are released through exercise.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Thermidorian Reaction was a coup that took place during this larger conflict. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this period of political instability that included the Reign of Terror. This period also included the executions of Louis XVI and his wife Marie Antoinette, along with the establishment of the first Paris Commune.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This leader in the French Revolution was overthrown in the Thermidorian Reaction. His Committee of Public Safety unleashed the Reign of Terror on France.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Executions during the French Revolution, including those of Louis XVI and his wife, were often done using this device invented during the revolution. Its slanted blade makes it especially good at beheading.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A poem about this conflict ends by describing “The old Lie: Dulce et decorum est / Pro patria mori” and takes its title from the Odes of the Roman poet Horace. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this early 20th century conflict. Siegfried Sassoon wrote poems like “Counter-Attack” about the violent gas weapons and trench warfare that characterized this “Great War.”
parts.answer: World War I [accept WWI; accept First World War; prompt on Great War]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Sassoon’s works largely influenced this English author’s poetry. This author of “Dulce et Decorum Est” and “Anthem for Doomed Youth” wrote poems based on his personal experiences as a soldier in the war.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This novel by Erich Maria Remarque set during the first World War centers on Paul Baumer and his experiences as a German soldier. Its title refers to a headline on a newspaper at the novel’s end.
parts.answer: All Quiet on the Western Front

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Michelson-Morley experiment provided strong evidence against the luminiferous aether, which led to the development of this theory. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this theory that describes the relationship between space and time. In this theory, Lorentz transformations have many consequences including length contraction and time dilation.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This scientist developed special and general relativity, along with the equation E equals m c squared.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Special relativity also predicted the relativistic and transverse forms of this effect. An example of this effect is the change in pitch of a siren approaching and receding from an observer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This thinker introduced his idea of the categorical imperative in his Groundworks on the Metaphysics of Morals. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this thinker whose works in epistemology and aesthetics made him a central figure in the Enlightenment. This philosopher’s doctrine of transcendental idealism can be found throughout his Critique of Pure Reason.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Kant was a philosopher from this country. Martin Heidegger, another philosopher from this country, had deep ties with this country’s Nazi party.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Kant’s deontological theory in this field is based on the idea that nothing is “good without limitation” besides a good will. This field concerns the moral principles that govern human behavior.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This sea is home to the Greater Antilles. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this sea, the location of beach destinations like the Cayman Islands and Saint Kitts. The Bahamas lie just north of this sea, which is bounded by South America on the South and Central America on the west.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This is the second-largest island in the Greater Antilles. This island was the site of the first settlement in the Americas, La Navidad, and it is currently split between Haiti and the Dominican Republic

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other island nation of the Greater Antilles had its capital at Port Royal until that city sunk into the ocean. This is the only country in the world without red, white, or blue on its flag.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The half-brother of this country’s leader was assassinated in the Kuala Lumpur airport in 2017. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, led by the hereditary Kim family dictatorship. Its capital city, Pyongyang, is home to Juche (joo-chay) Tower, built by its first leader, Kim Il-Sung.
parts.answer: North Korea [or the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This is the current leader of North Korea, who took power after his father died in 2011. Rumors circulated in April 2020 that he was seriously ill, and that his sister, Kim Yo-jong, was running the country.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] North Korea is separated from South Korea by this boundary line, which runs approximately along the 38th parallel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poet claimed “You look like a world, ready to surrender” in “Body of a Woman,” the first poem included in his Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Chilean poet who commanded “Arise to birth with me, my brother” and “Speak through my words and my blood” in his “The Heights of Macchu Picchu.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Neruda wrote his poems in this language, the most-spoken language in his home country of Chile.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This tenth collection of poems by Neruda analyzes the history of the Western Hemisphere from a Hispanic American perspective. “A Lamp on Earth” is the first section of this 15-part collection.
parts.answer: Canto General [accept translations like General Song and other reasonable equivalents]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This deity punished Actaeon (AK-tee-uhn) for watching her bathe by turning him into a stag, after which his own hunting dogs tore him apart. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Greek goddess of the moon and the wilderness. Orion was a hunting companion of this virgin goddess before he was stung and killed by a giant scorpion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Artemis was born to Leto (LEE-toh) on the island of Delos along with her brother Apollo, who was a god of this heavenly object. Helios was another god of this object and drove it across the sky in his chariot.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The seven sons and seven daughters of this figure were killed by Artemis and Apollo after she bragged that she had more children than Leto. This Queen of Thebes was then turned into stone while she wept.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One world leader with this last name took control of his country in the 26th of July Movement. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Give this last name of a dictator who gave the “History Will Absolve Me” speech after a failed raid on the Moncada Barracks. That ruler with this last name ceded power to his brother Raul in 2008, and was named Fidel.
parts.answer: Castro [accept Raul Castro or Fidel Castro]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Castro took power over Cuba from Fulgencio Batista after defeating him in the Cuban Revolution, which involved an attack on the Presidential Palace in this city. This city is currently the capital of Cuba.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This organization reportedly attempted over 100 assassination attempts on Fidel Castro, including plots centered around poisoned milkshakes and an exploding cigar.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This substance is mainly harvested in the form of latex from Hevea brasiliensis, or the Pará tree. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this material consisting of repeating units of isoprene. This material, which is hardened in vulcanization, is used in pencil erasers and car tires.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Rubber is classified as a synthetic one of these compounds. Teflon and nylon are other examples of these materials, which consist of repeated subunits called monomers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Polymers can be separated from other molecules in the size-exclusion form of this technique. This technique which uses a mobile and stationary phase was named for its ability to separate mixtures into different colors.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One painting by this artist was described by The New York Times as “an explosion in a shingle factory.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this artist of Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2. This artist drew a mustache and goatee on a Mona Lisa and used an overturned urinal in his readymade Fountain.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] One sculpture by Duchamp (doo-SHAM) is titled for containing 50 cc of the air of this city. Duchamp’s Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2 was rejected from this city’s Salon des Independents.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] 50 cc of Paris Air is a sculpture made of this material, which Duchamp also used to make his The Bride Stripped Bare by Her Bachelors, Even. This material is commonly used to make lenses and windows.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A character in this story hides her cat Pitty Sing in a basket in the back of a car to secretly take him along on a vacation. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this story about an outlaw called “The Misfit” who kills the grandmother and the rest of Bailey’s family after they get stranded due to a car crash.
parts.answer: “A Good Man is Hard to Find”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] “A Good Man is Hard to Find” was written by this Southern Gothic author of the stories “Everything That Rises Must Converge,” “Parker’s Back,” and “Good Country People.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] O’Connor was born in this state’s city of Savannah. For a summer vacation, the family in “A Good Man is Hard to Find” travel to Florida from this state’s capital of Atlanta.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure was given grace by Aphrodite, the knowledge of fine crafts by Athena, and a keen mind by Hermes. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this first woman in Greek mythology. A jar often incorrectly called “[this figure’s] Box” was opened to release into the world all evils known to man until only hope remained.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pandora was created by Hephaestus as a punishment for mankind after this figure stole the gift of fire from the gods. This figure is credited with creating mankind from clay in Greek mythology.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Pandora’s daughter Pyrrha (PEER-uh) and her husband Deucalion were the only people to survive one of these events caused by Zeus. Noah is said to have made an ark to survive one of these events lasting for 40 days.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Betterton-Kroll process is used to extract bismuth from alloys containing this element. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this element that was used in pipes until its toxicity was discovered. Today, it is still used in acid car batteries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Thomas Midgley used lead to decrease engine knock and to boost this gasoline rating. More premium gasoline generally has a higher value of this rating shown on gas pumps.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Lead was once found in this substance, until it was discovered that it would crack and contaminate the environment. Watercolors are a type of art in which this substance is applied to canvas with brushes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one episode of this TV show, Thea is reanimated by Ra’s al-Guhl. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this TV show in which a hero is helped by characters like Spartan and Black Canary. The show is titled after a weapon used by its green-cloaked main character.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This is the civilian alter ego of the superhero Arrow. He is the son of a billionaire in Starling City and was stranded on the island of Lian-Yu for five years.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Arrow and his friend the Flash were created by groups of comic book writers working for this company, which is a rival of Marvel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During a battle in this war, a commander told his troops not to fire until they “see the whites” of the enemies’ eyes. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this war which featured the Battle of Bunker Hill. In this war, the American colonies fought for independence from the British.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Following the Revolutionary War Battles of Germantown and Brandywine, troops retreated to this Pennsylvania encampment. Washington’s army had to suffer through the harsh winter of 1777 in this location.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] At Valley Forge, this Prussian drill master developed an efficient training method for soldiers, which focused on usage of bayonets.
parts.answer: Baron von Steuben [accept Baron Friedrich Wilhelm August Heinrich Ferdinand Freiherr von Steuben or Baron Friedrich Wilhelm Ludolf Gerhard Augustin Freiherr von Steuben

parts.label: L
parts.question: This physicist proposed a thought experiment in which a radioactive substance would cause hydrocyanic acid to be released with probability one-half into a box with a cat inside. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this physicist, who used that thought experiment to demonstrate that the cat inside would be in a state of quantum superposition between alive and dead.
parts.answer: Erwin Schrödinger [or Erwin Rudolf Josef Alexander Schrödinger]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In another physics thought experiment, the Second Law of Thermodynamics is hypothetically violated by this small creature, which uses a door to sort fast and cold gas molecules into separate chambers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Laplace’s (la-PLOSS’s) Demon thought experiment implies that knowing this property and momentum for a particle, could determine its history and future. This property defines where a particle is, relative to its surroundings.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During the immigration boom of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, unrest in Europe led millions to go through this island to get to the United States. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this island located halfway between New York and New Jersey, home to the main historical immigration point for the East Coast.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Immigrants entering at Ellis Island would often see this structure while entering. A gift from France, this large green statue depicts a woman holding a tablet and a torch.
parts.answer: Statue of Liberty [or Liberty Enlightening the World, or La Liberté éclairant le monde]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other island was known as the “Ellis Island of the West.” Located in California’s San Francisco Bay, it saw most of its immigrants from China and Japan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In J. M. W. Turner’s Rain, Steam and Speed, a white rabbit runs alongside one of these vehicles in the distance. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this type of vehicle, a series of railroad cars moved as a unit, that is depicted in Edouard Manet’s The Railway.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This surrealist artist’s Time Transfixed includes a train exiting a fireplace. This Belgian artist’s work titled The Treachery of Images depicts a pipe, but says “This is not a pipe.” at the bottom.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This impressionist artist practiced en plein air, the act of painting outdoors, by painting the Gare Saint-Lazare (gahr sahnt-lah-ZAR) Train Station. This French artist also painted Impression: Sunrise and a series of about 250 Water-Lilies.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote about Amory Blaine, a Princeton student who declines into poverty and is rejected by Rosalind Connage, in his novel This Side of Paradise. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Jazz Age author. The title character of another novel by this author is shot by George Wilson in a swimming pool after being wrongly accused of Myrtle’s death by Tom Buchanan.
parts.answer: F. Scott Fitzgerald [accept Francis Scott Key Fitzgerald]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Tom Buchanan appears in this so-called “Great American Novel” by Fitzgerald narrated by Nick Carraway. The title character of this novel loves Daisy Buchanan and gazes at a green light at her house across the bay.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Great Gatsby is set in the towns of West Egg and East Egg on Long Island in this American city’s suburbs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to legend, this city was founded by twin boys raised by a she-wolf, Lupercal, who had saved them from drowning in a river. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city mythically founded by Romulus and Remus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] King Amulius allegedly sent Romulus and Remus to drown in this river. This river is the largest in Rome and meets the Mediterranean at the suburb of Ostia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] According to legend, the first seven rulers of Rome held this title; Romulus was the first and Tarquin the Proud was the last.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These beings are channeled by shrine maidens called miko during kagura dances. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give the original-language term for these beings central to prayer in Shintoism. These beings, examples of which are Izanagi, Izanami, and Amaterasu (AH-mah-ter-AH-soo), are worshipped in Shinto shrines.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shintoism is primarily practiced in this Asian country. Shinto adherents in this country go to shrines like the ones in Tokyo or Kyoto on New Year’s Day to pray to kami (kah-mee) for good luck in the coming year.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During New Year’s shrine visits, called hatsumode (haat-soo-MOH-day) in Japanese, people can be seen wearing this traditional Japanese garment. These square-sleeved garments are almost always worn with a belt called an obi.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The “ring” type of these structures can occur within collapsed volcanic calderas. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these structures that are classified based on the movement of their hanging walls in relation to their footwalls. Types of these structures include normal, reverse, and strike-slip.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Faults often occur along transform boundaries, which are located between two of these structures. These sections of the Earth’s crust move in a process known as continental drift.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Vine-Matthews-Morley hypothesis proposed this cause of continental drift. This process occurs when new oceanic crust is created at mid-ocean ridges and gradually moves away from the ridge.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1191, Richard I of England conquered Cyprus from the Byzantines while searching for his wife Berengia. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Richard did so while on the third instance of these military campaigns. These campaigns were first called by Pope Urban II to reclaim the Holy Land for Christendom, but most of them failed.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Crusades that Richard fought in pitted Islamic forces against Christian forces for control of this holy city. Today split into four quarters, this city is a hotbed for contention between Palestinians and Israelis.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Throughout his campaigns, Richard mostly faced, and lost to, this military leader, who retook Jerusalem for Muslim forces before the Third Crusade.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about cosmic latte, the average color of the universe.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] The discovery of cosmic latte was not the goal of the study that accomplished it. The study was actually intended to study these lines created by absorption and emission of light at certain frequencies.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Despite receiving less votes than names like “Astronomer Almond” or “Big Bang Beige,” researchers chose to name the color Cosmic Latte, claiming to be biased by this stimulant in coffee that keeps you awake.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Though cosmic latte is a shade of beige, the average color of the universe is shifting more towards this color. The light from stars reaching us is blue, though by now those stars may have changed into giants of this color.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The last stanza of a poem by this author states that “We must confess that we are the possible” and that “We are the miraculous, the true wonder of this world.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this American author whose poetry collection Just Give Me a Cool Drink of Water 'fore I Diiie was nominated for a Pulitzer. This author also wrote works like I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings is one of seven of these works by Angelou about her own life. Mom & Me & Mom, the most recent of these works by Angelou, describes her personal relationship with her mother.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This poem by Angelou opens with the line “A Rock, A River, A Tree” and ends by describing a rock’s cry of “You may stand upon me, / But do not hide your face.” Angelou read this poem at Bill Clinton’s inauguration.

parts.label: L
parts.question: William the Silent first led this country to its independance. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country which fought the Eighty Years War for independence from Spain. Provinces in this country include North Holland and Zeeland (ZAY-lont).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] During the golden age of the Netherlands, their East India Company, the VOC, shipped spices from modern-day Indonesia to this port city. This city is now the capital of the Netherlands.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Extensive shipping created an economic bubble due to the decline in value of these signature Dutch flowers. These flowers are still cultivated in the Netherlands today, making it the largest flower exporter in the world.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, name some pieces of computer hardware.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The QWERTY layout is the most widely used in these pieces of hardware because it is deliberately inefficient to reduce jamming. These devices are used to type numbers and letters into computers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] These devices contain components like the ALU and registers, and their clock rate is typically measured in gigahertz. These devices execute instructions and do most of the computations for computers.
parts.answer: CPU or central processing unit [accept central processor or main processor or just processor]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These devices with a similar name to CPUs are specialized circuits that use numerous computing units to operate on pixels. These devices accelerate the creation of images for output to a display device.
parts.answer: GPU or graphics processing unit [accept VPU or visual processing unit; prompt on integrated graphics or video card or graphics card or display card or graphics adaptor or display adaptor]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This number symphony has been deemed cursed, as many composers have died after the completion of their symphony of this number, such as Antonín Dvořák (dih-vor-JAHK), Franz Schubert, and Gustav Mahler. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this number, the most famous symphony of which uses text from Friedrich Schiller’s “Ode to Joy,” and is nicknamed the Choral Symphony for its use of voices.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Choral Symphony is by this composer, whose third symphony is known as the Eroica and his sixth is known as the Pastoral. His 5th symphony begins with a short-short-short-long rhythm that depicts fate knocking at the door.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Beethoven’s 5th symphony is in this key’s minor, which has 3 flats in the order B E A, and is the relative minor to E-flat major. This key’s major has no sharps or flats.
parts.answer: C [accept C major or C minor]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Asia is home to some of the largest river systems in the world. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] What river is named after the color of the soil that it drains into a sea of the same name? That river flows through the city of Luoyang.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Yellow River and Yangtze River are connected by this structure, which was built by the Sui Dynasty and restored by the Ming Dynasty.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Both the Yellow and Yangtze are in this country, the most populous in the world.
parts.answer: People’s Republic of China [do not accept or prompt on “Republic of China”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about the TNM staging system.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The TNM staging system classifies the severity of cases of this disease, types of which include melanoma, carcinoma, and leukemia. This disease is most commonly treated with surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The T in TNM represents the size and extent of these objects, which are formed through neoplasia. These abnormal masses of tissue can be benign, but malignant ones cause cancer.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The N in TNM describes the involvement of these organs. These organs found in the armpits and in the head and neck area serve as reservoirs for white blood cells, and may swell up during infection.
parts.answer: lymph nodes [or lymph glands; do not accept or prompt on “lymph” alone]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Construction of this cathedral began under Bishop Maurice de Sully, though there is debate over whether Sully or Pope Alexander III laid its cornerstone. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this cathedral in Paris which features enormous rose windows and was one of the first cathedrals to feature flying buttresses. This cathedral suffered extensive damages due to a 2019 fire.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Notre-Dame was built in this style of architecture, which developed from Romanesque architecture and was succeeded by Renaissance architecture. This style is marked by rib vaults, flying buttresses, and pointed arches.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Notre-Dame featured numerous examples of these sculptures which were used to divide rainwater into thin streams to minimize potential damage. These sculptures often depict demonic figures.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A character in this TV series is the puppet master and Akatsuki (AA-cut-suu-ki) member Sasori of the Red Sand. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this television show, whose main character has a Rasengan (RAH-sing-gone) attack and the ability to create shadow clones.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This character from Naruto is a member of a clan with a hereditary sight ability, the Sharingan. His older brother, Itachi, massacred that clan on the orders of Danzo (DON-zo).

parts.label: C
parts.question: Naruto is one of this Japanese type of cartoon. Other examples of this type of show include Dragon Ball Z and Demon Slayer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Early in his career, this tycoon worked under Thomas Gibbons to dismantle the steamboat monopoly held by Aaron Ogden. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this business magnate who became a steamboat entrepreneur before feuding with James Fisk and Jay Gould in a different industry. This entrepreneur was nicknamed “The Commodore.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gibbons and Vanderbilt competed with Ogden for control of the waters of New York, especially this river. The very first commercial steamboat trip took passengers from New York City to Albany on this river.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After working with steamboats, Vanderbilt rose to the top of the industry making networks of these tracks across the nation. A major event in that industry’s history was the construction of a Transcontinental one.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Petioles connect these structures to the stem. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these structures that contain high amounts of chlorophyll, a key pigment to photosynthesis which takes place primarily in these structures. These structures are usually green, but change colors during the Fall.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Leaves generally have one primary and many branching secondary examples of these structures which, as the vascular tissue of the leaf, transport water and nutrients in it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Leaves are often covered by one of these substances for protection. These layers of waxy coverings minimize water loss from leaves.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2015, the official name of this mountain was changed from that of a former president.

parts.label: A
parts.question: For ten points, name this tallest mountain in the United States. Its now-current name means "the High One" and is of Athabaskan origin.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Denali is located in this largest U.S. state, which is separated from Russia by the Bering Strait.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This island chain extends from the southwest of Alaska towards Russia, forming the northernmost portion of the Pacific Ring of Fire. Vitus Bering is credited with discovering this island chain.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these animals spots a bundle of ripe fruit on a vine trained along the branches of a tall tree. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this animal that, in a story, jumps repeatedly to try and reach a ripe bunch of grapes. It misses repeatedly until finally it gives up, claiming that it did not want sour grapes anyway.
parts.answer: a fox [accept “The Fox and the Grapes”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: “The Fox and the Grapes” is included in a collection of fables written by this ancient Greek slave. Other well-known stories attributed to him include “The Ant and the Grasshopper” and “The Frog and the Ox.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Aesop’s most often retold story is perhaps one about these two animals. One of these animals challenges the other to a race and ends up winning when the other takes a nap midway through.
parts.answer: “The Tortoise and the Hare” [accept turtle for Tortoise and rabbit or other obvious synonyms for Hare]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician succeeded Condoleezza Rice in a US Cabinet post after her defeat in the 2008 Democratic primary. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this political figure whose memoir What Happened describes her loss in the 2016 Presidential Election.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Before running for the presidency, Clinton served in this cabinet position. Under her tenure, Clinton helped organize sanctions against Iran to curtail its nuclear program.

parts.label: C
parts.question: During Clinton’s time as Secretary of State, an attack on a diplomatic outpost in this city led to the death of Chris Stevens, US ambassador to Libya.

parts.label: L
parts.question: It is said that Rome tilled the ground around Carthage with this resource, so the city would never thrive again. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this resource. The word “salary” comes from money paid to Roman soldiers to buy this resource, which was valuable for its ability to preserve and flavor food.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Romans adopted the use of this other kind of currency from the Greeks. Early Roman forms of these things included the Sestertius and Follis, which were often minted with the current Emperor’s head on one side.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Roman coins lost value during the Crisis of the Third Century due to this economic phenomenon. Emperor Diocletian minted a new coin, the Solidus, to counteract this phenomenon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Ogives are alternating light and dark bands on the surfaces of these objects. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these objects whose movement can form debris that is later deposited in moraines. These objects lose mass via ablation and calving, the latter of which results in icebergs breaking off of their edges.

parts.label: B
parts.question: These long, narrow inlets between cliffs are created by glaciers. The term for these features comes from Old Norse because they are commonly found in Scandinavia, Norway in particular.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Tarns are examples of these bodies of water formed in cirques. These bodies of water are surrounded by land, other than the rivers that drain or feed them, and “Great” examples of these bodies of water include Erie and Superior.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The first subseries of this novel series, The Prophecies Begin, centers on Fireheart’s discovery of Tigerstar’s treachery and the battle against BloodClan. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this series of children’s novels about the adventures of four different Clans. This series is written by multiple people under the collective pseudonym of Erin Hunter.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Clans in the Warriors series are made up of wild groups of these animals. Domesticated animals of this type owned by “Two-legs” are called “kittypets” by the Clans.
parts.answer: cats [accept logical equivalents like felines; prompt on kitties or kittens]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The four Clans’ belief system is based on this other Clan, which is supposedly made up of the Clans’ deceased ancestors. Medicine cats in the Warriors series serve as a channel between the four Clans and this spiritual Clan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Leon Trotsky negotiated the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk to pull this country out of World War I. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country that was in the midst of overthrowing its monarchy in St. Petersburg when the treaty was signed. The Mensheviks and Bolsheviks fought for control of this country throughout 1917.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This man led the Bolsheviks in the Russian Revolution and became the first leader of the USSR. St. Petersburg would be renamed after him upon his death.
parts.answer: Vladimir Lenin [accept Valdimir Ilyich Ulyanov; accept Leningrad]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This last Tsar of Russia and ruling member of the house of Romanov was overthrown in the Russian Revolution. He was murdered along with his entire family in 1918 by Bolsheviks in the Ipatiev House of Yekaterinburg.
parts.answer: Nicholas II [prompt on Nicholas or Nikolai]

parts.label: L
parts.question: At an early age, this woman enrolled in an all-boys school with the hopes of being an engineer, and was strongly discouraged when she applied to a medical school in Rome. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this woman who went on to graduate with honors and become a physician. This Italian woman names an education philosophy used in schools that view children as eager learners and stress discovery learning.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Montessori education is most commonly used with students in this grade level and below. This grade level, which comes from a German word, usually comes before first grade.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Most Kindergarten teachers use phonics to teach children this faculty. This faculty is thought to be best acquired during a critical period at a young age
parts.answer: language [accept speaking or reading a language]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the metallic form of these interactions, atoms experience attractive forces due to a cloud of free, delocalized electrons. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these interactions which are used to join two atoms. When one of them occurs between a metal and a nonmetal, they can involve transfer of electrons in the “ionic” type.
parts.answer: bonds or bonding [accept ionic bonds or metallic bonds]

parts.label: B
parts.question: In covalent bonds, electrons are shared between the atoms, but when there is a large difference in electronegativity the bond can have this property. The covalent bonds found in water have this property.
parts.answer: polar bonds [accept polarity or strongly polar]

parts.label: C
parts.question: While covalent bonds occur between individual atoms, these interactions occur between larger molecules and are determined largely by the polarity and location of electrons around the molecules involved. These interactions include both induced dipole and hydrogen bonding interactions.
parts.answer: intermolecular forces or attractions [accept van der Waals forces or IMF’s]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Following the death of Muhammad, his followers’ forces engaged in rapid military expansion from the Arabian Peninsula. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Muhammed’s followers were the first practitioners of this religion. Its kingdoms included the Rashidun and Ummayad Caliphates.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Rashidun Caliphate’s first capital city was this second-holiest city in Islam, which lies about 300 miles north of Mecca. Muhammad is buried in this city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Umayyad Caliphate would later be expelled by the Abbasids, but it maintained its rule on this peninsula. Christians on this peninsula would later lead a campaign against the Muslims called the Reconquista.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Diopters (DYE-op-terz) measure the strength of mirrors and these other devices. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these devices, typically made of glass or plastic, that focus or disperse light. Common examples of these devices are found in cameras and in glasses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Lenses work by means of this process, in which waves traveling between media change direction. This process is the reason why objects seem to bend when placed partly in water, and is contrasted with reflection.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This optical law relates the angles of incidence to indices of refraction and so can be used to determine how bent objects placed in water appear.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about Central European capital cities, for ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This city was the site of two Ottoman Sieges and a charge of winged hussars. Schonbrunn Palace, the seat of the Habsburg Dynasty, is located outside of this capital city of Austria.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Bratislava, the capital of this country, lies just east of Vienna. The Velvet Divorce of 1993 saw this country split from the Czech Republic.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Both Bratislava and Vienna lie on this European river, which also flows through two other European capital cities: Budapest and Belgrade. This river originates in the Black forest and empties into the Black Sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man composed a Cello Concerto in E minor that was famously performed by Jacqueline du Pré. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this English composer who included sections called “Ysobel” and “Nimrod” in his Enigma Variations, which he dedicated to his “friends pictured within.” He also composed Pomp and Circumstance.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Elgar’s Pomp and Circumstance is a collection of pieces in this genre, the first of which is often played at graduations. This genre of music is often played by military bands accompanied with walking soldiers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: John Philip Sousa, known as the “March King,” aided in the development of one of these instruments that wraps around the musician’s body. These instruments are the largest and lowest-pitched brass instruments.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This creature is an offspring of Typhon and Echidna, making it a sibling of such beasts as Cerberus and the Hydra. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this monster from Greek mythology. This part-lion, part-goat, and part-snake creature was slain at the command of King Iobates (eye-OBB-uh-teez) of Lycia after terrorizing his lands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This hero is credited with the slaying of the Chimera and once defeated the Amazons by dropping boulders on them. After sleeping in a temple to Athena, this hero met his most famous steed, a flying horse.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This was the name of Bellerophon’s (beh-LAIR-uh-fonz) steed. This winged horse was stung by a gadfly sent by Zeus when an egotistic Bellerophon tried to fly to Mount Olympus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Ununoctium was the placeholder name given to an element in this group, before it was named for Yuri Oganessian. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this group of elements that have extremely high ionization energies due to their stable electron configurations. These unreactive elements are typically monatomic due to their full valence shells.
parts.answer: noble gases [accept group 18, group 8A, or inert gases]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This noble gas is often used to fill the Geiger-Muller tube in Geiger counters. This noble gas is the third most common element in the Earth’s atmosphere, despite making up less than 1% of it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This noble gas’s red emission line indicated to scientists that it was an undiscovered element. This element with atomic symbol Ne is commonly used in brightly glowing lights.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event was planned by the “Hamburg Cell” and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this terrorist attack in which four hijacked airplanes destroyed the World Trade Center in New York.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] On 9/11, a hijacked plane was also crashed into this building, killing over 100 employees. This Arlington building, the headquarters of the Department of Defense, is named for its shape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The fourth hijacked flight on 9/11 is thought to have been intended for this building. Instead, passengers such as Todd Beamer stormed the cockpit, crashing the plane into a field in Pennsylvania.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about American holdings in the Caribbean, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This U.S. island territory contains the fort Castillo (cah-STEE-yo) San Cristobal in its capital of San Juan. This territory is often thought to be the most likely candidate for the 51st state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The US Virgin Islands were the only Caribbean holding of this Scandinavian kingdom until their sale to the US in 1917. This country’s only current overseas colonies are the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
parts.answer: the Kingdom of Denmark [or Kongeriget Danmark]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A US naval base at this location in Cuba is held in defiance of the Cuban government and has been the site of Geneva Convention-violating torture of enemy prisoners during the War on Terror.
parts.answer: Guantanamo Bay [or Gitmo or the Guantanamo Bay Naval Base or Base Naval de la Bahía de Guantánamo]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This substance’s pH is affected by its CEC, or cation-exchange capacity. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this substance that has different textures based on how much sand, silt and clay it is composed of. This mixture of organic matter and disintegrated rock is often placed in pots to grow plants in.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This fertile layer of soil, referred to as the A horizon, contains large amounts of decomposed organic matter called humus. Unless there is organic matter like plants or grass, this layer is the uppermost layer of soil.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Secondary structures made of this type of rock can form through pedogenesis, the formation of soil. This type of rock is formed from accumulation of small particles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Africa is home to more countries than any other continent, therefore making it home to more capital cities than any other continent. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Rabat is the capital of this North African kingdom that lies across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain. Other cities in this country include Casablanca and Marrakech (mAA-ruh-kEHsh).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This most populous country in Africa moved its capital to the master-planned Abuja from the more populous Lagos in 1991 in an attempt to move the capital to a more neutral position between contesting peoples.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While countries like Tanzania and Ivory Coast have two capitals, South Africa is the only country that has three: Bloemfontein, Pretoria, and this city.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one aria, this operatic character sings that “when [he] shook hands with Zhou (joh) En-lai… the world was listening.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this character who sings that “news, news, news… has a kind of mystery” after getting off of the plane “Spirit of ‘76.” This character meets Chairman Mao in an opera about his presidential visit to China.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Nixon in China is an opera by this composer, who also wrote Short Ride in a Fast Machine, Doctor Atomic, and Death of Klinghof er. This composer shares his name with an early President of the United States.
parts.answer: John Coolidge Adams [do not accept or prompt on “John Luther Adams”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Adams wrote the opera A Flowering Tree based on a folk tale from this country. Another minimalist composer, Phillip Glass, loosely based his opera Satyagraha on the life of a figure from this country, Mohandas Gandhi.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to a text from the sixth century, this creature was stopped from attacking a monk’s follower when Saint Columba made the sign of the cross and told it to back off. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this creature of which a “surgeon’s photograph” was taken in 1934 that has since been mostly debunked as a hoax. This large and long-necked creature supposedly inhabits a body of water in the Scottish Highlands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Like the Loch (lock) Ness Monster, this creature is a cryptid, since its existence is unsubstantiated. This creature is described as a hairy and ape-like humanoid creature in North American forests which leaves giant footprints.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Sightings of this cryptid whose name means “goat-sucker” have mostly been in northern Mexico. This spiny creature supposedly the size of a large dog is said to attack and suck the blood from livestock.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander the Great defeated forces from this empire. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this empire, which was ruled for some periods by Achaemenids, Safavids, and Afshars. Rulers of this empire included Cyrus the Great and Xerxes (ZERK-seez) the Great.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The losing forces and Issus and Gaugamela were led by a ruler of this name, though he supposedly fled out of fear at both battles. Another ruler of this name fathered Xerxes the Great, and was Cyrus the Great’s nephew.
parts.answer: Darius [accept Darius III or Darius the Great or Darius I]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Darius the Great, who overthrew Smerdis to become the ruler of Egypt, constructed one of these structures linking the Nile and Red Sea. Another one of these waterways is named for the Egyptian city of Suez.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Okazaki fragments are short segments of this substance, combined during replication by a ligase named for it. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this molecule, which is unzipped by helicase and copied by a polymerase named for it. This molecule made of nucleotide sequences serves as a genetic code and, unlike RNA, is double-stranded.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This process, developed by Kary Mullis, uses denaturation, annealing, and elongation phases to copy DNA. This process uses Taq (tack) polymerase to make billions of copies of DNA sequences.
parts.answer: PCR or polymerase chain reaction [prompt on cloning]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Taq polymerase, DNA polymerase, ligase, and helicase are all examples of these proteins. These proteins increase reaction rate by lowering the activation energy, thus acting as biological catalysts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This school’s current football coach, Ryan Day, threatened to “hang 100” points on one of its conference rivals, the University of Michigan. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this school, which has produced the third-most NFL players in history after Notre Dame and USC. This university’s mascot is the Buckeye, and its alumni include players like Nick and Joey Bosa and Ezekiel Elliott.
parts.answer: THE Ohio State University [do not accept or prompt on “Ohio”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Two players from THE Ohio State University, Malcolm Jenkins and Michael Thomas, currently play for this team. This team based in New Orleans won their first ever Super Bowl in 2009 behind quarterback Drew Brees.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Ohio State Football team has had this many undefeated seasons. Ohio State plays in a conference named for a “Big” set of this many teams, which actually has fourteen teams.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man conquered the Lombards at the 8th century Battle of Pavia. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this son of Pepin the Short, whose Carolingian Empire was divided amongst his grandsons in the Treaty of Verdun. This Frankish King was crowned Emperor of the Romans on Christmas Day in the year 800.
parts.answer: Charlemagne [accept Charles the Great; prompt on Charles]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Charlemagne was crowned Emperor of the Romans by Leo III, who held this position at the time. The holder of this position serves as the Bishop of Rome and leader of the Catholic Church.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The title Emperor of the Romans would later morph into this position, holders of which were chosen by German Prince-Electors. Other holders of this title included Otto the Great and Frederick Barbarossa.
parts.answer: Holy Roman Emperor [accept German-Roman Emperor or Romanorum Imperator or Rex Romanorum; prompt on Emperor; do not accept or prompt on “Roman Emperor”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Short bursts of these disturbances are known as “packets” or “trains,” and continuous periodic ones may be sinusoidal when acting like the graph of the sine function. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these oscillations which can be transverse or longitudinal. Surfers usually ride these oscillations in water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This property, along with wavelength, generally describes a wave’s size. For transverse waves, this property is defined as the wave’s maximum displacement from its equilibrium point.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This property of a wave is the inverse of its period, and describes the number of wavelengths that pass through a certain point over a given period of time. This value is measured in hertz.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This work takes place in a future country called Panem and in it the tribute Foxface dies when she unknowingly steals poisonous berries. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this novel in which Katniss and Peeta compete for their lives against children from eleven other districts until they are both declared victors.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Catching Fire, the second book in the Hunger Games series, had games of this type in which only victors participated. The first games of this type, which happen every 25 years, had districts vote on tributes to compete.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In The Hunger Games, this drunk is the only victor living in District 12 at the time of the 74th Games. This character insists that Katniss and Peeta run away from the Cornucopia when the Games begin to avoid the bloodbath.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This thinker dedicated “Schopenhauer as Educator,” one of his Untimely Meditations, to Arthur Schopenhauer since he was one of the only philosophers that this thinker respected. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this German philosopher, the author of works like Thus Spake Zarathustra and Beyond Good and Evil. The master-slave morality is a central theme of this thinker’s On the Genealogy of Morality.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In his The Gay Science, Nietzsche wrote that humanity has “still to overcome his shadow!” after declaring the death of this omniscient figure. In another of his works, Zarathustra famously declares that “[this figure] is dead.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In Thus Spake Zarathustra, Zarathustra also proposes this concept as an ultimate form of existence for humankind. This German-language term is usually translated “Superman.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following regarding Mormonism and the Latter Day Saint movement.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] This founder of the Mormon church published the Book of Mormon, which he claimed was translated from golden tablets with guidance from the angel Moroni. He was killed at Carthage Jail in 1844 by an armed mob.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] After Smith’s murder, a majority of Mormons followed Brigham Young to settle in what would become this state. The largest Mormon temple stands in this Western state’s Salt Lake City.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Smith was murdered partly because of his claim that this practice is biblically permitted. This practice of taking multiple spouses was officially renounced by the mainline Mormon church in 1890.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Objects in this language are managed by the Document Object Model. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this language, created by Tim Berners-Lee, which uses tags and attributes to construct web pages.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] HTML and CSS work with this language, standardized by ES6, to make websites interactive. Working with this dynamically-typed language, one might use a library called jQuery or a framework like React.
parts.answer: Javascript [Do not accept of prompt on “Java”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Web pages can be viewed in browsers like this most widely used browser on the planet. Google distributes this browser, which has an easter egg of a secret dinosaur game, visible when this browser can’t access the Internet.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After trampling a young girl, this character is forced by Richard Enfield to pay a hundred pounds to that girl’s family. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character. In a novel, Gabriel Utterson realizes that a note apologizing for the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, which is supposedly from this character, is in the handwriting of an esteemed doctor.
parts.answer: Mr. Hyde [prompt on “Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde” by asking “which one?”; do not accept or prompt on “Dr. Jekyll” alone]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Scottish author of Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde wrote about David Balfour, who visits the House of Shaws and is the rightful heir to his father’s fortune, in his novel Kidnapped.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In this other novel by Stevenson, Jim accompanies Long John Silver as a cabin boy to the title location, the supposed site of Captain Flint’s hidden riches. A parrot in this novel often squawks “Pieces of Eight!”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This metal alloy was used by cultures like Hyksos, Assyrians, and the Middle Kingdom of Egypt. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this alloy, primarily made with copper and tin, that was used throughout the ancient world to make weapons and tools.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This weapon became an extremely popular bronze weapon for warriors. Bronze’s strength allowed for smiths to create this weapon with a longer blade than daggers or knives.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These Greek soldiers used bronze shields, called hoplons, which are the origin of their name. These soldiers often entered battle in organized formations called phalanxes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this film, the Scarecrow wants a brain, the Tin Woodman wants a heart, and the Lion wants courage. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this film starring Judy Garland as Dorothy, a girl from Kansas whose house is taken up by a storm before landing in Munchkinland. Characters in this film follow the yellow brick road to the Emerald City.
parts.answer: The Wizard of Oz [accept The Wonderful Wizard of Oz]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This musical, which is based on a retelling of The Wizard of Oz, follows the story of Glinda the Good Witch and her friend Elphaba, the Witch of the West, who sings the show tune “Defying Gravity”.
parts.answer: Wicked: The Untold Story of the Witches of Oz

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The original Broadway cast of Wicked featured this actress in the role of Elphaba. This woman played Maureen Johnson in the movie Rent and voiced Elsa in Frozen.
parts.answer: Idina Kim Menzel [or Idina Kim Mentzel]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character visits Balnibarbi, a kingdom ruled from the floating island of Laputa, where he observes crazy experiments like softening marble to use in pillows and extracting sunbeams from cucumbers. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this character, who strives to fix a political divide between Lilliput and Blefuscu caused by a debate on which end of an egg a person should crack.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Gulliver’s Travels was written by this author, who proposed that the poor of a certain country sell their children as food to the rich as a solution for economic troubles in his essay A Modest Proposal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Swift was a satirist from this European country. James Joyce, another author from this country, wrote about people in its capital city in his collection Dubliners.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Jainism, this concept is thought of as a physical substance that pollutes the soul when someone kills, lies, or steals. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this concept in many schools of Hinduism and Buddhism. According to this concept, one’s intents and actions affect one’s current and future lives.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Jainism, Hinduism, and Buddhism were founded in this modern-day country. Many of the founding texts of religions from this Asian country were written in Sanskrit.
parts.answer: India [or Republic of India or Bharatiya Ganarajya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In Buddhism, dhyāna refers to this practice, taken up in Yoga exercises. This practice of focusing one’s attention is often performed in the lotus position, with both hands extended on a crossed lap.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scientist names a sensory receptor that senses changes in muscle tension. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Italian scientist who names a cell organelle that modifies and packages proteins into vesicles to be sent to their final destination.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Golgi also names a staining method that is used to visualize tissue made of these cells. These cells primarily found in the brain consist of axons and dendrites and are separated by synapses.
parts.answer: neuron or neurone or nerve cell

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Golgi reaction was initially named after the fact that it stains neurons this color. This color is produced by the absence or complete absorption of light.

parts.label: L
parts.question: While running to become governor of this state, a future president promised to “clean up the mess” at its state university’s original and flagship campus, though his actions partly led to the People’s Park protests. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this US state currently led by Gavin Newsom, who lives just outside of its city of Sacramento.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This governor of California later became the 40th president of the United States. This president fired thousands of striking air traffic controllers and created a missile defense program nicknamed “Star Wars”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Reagan discussed “Star Wars,” his Strategic Defense Initiative, at the Geneva Summit with this last Soviet General Secretary. This leader’s policies of glasnost and perestroika foreshadowed the end of the Soviet Union.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After his death, the inventor of these objects was cremated and his ashes were molded into one. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these toys once called Pluto Platters and Flyin’ Saucers. In 1958, Wham-O bought the rights to these objects, which today are used in a game called Ultimate.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Apocryphally, frisbees originated from the easily-throwable tins of the Frisbie Company, which made these desserts. These desserts are often made in flavors like pecan, pumpkin, or key lime.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this sport, players must get their frisbees into goals in the least number of throws, often in relation to par. This sport features specialized, smaller frisbees, often on a course with nine or eighteen holes.
parts.answer: disc golf or frisbee golf or folf or frolf

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name these Mediterranean islands, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The Knights Hospitaller ruled this island until they were kicked out by Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. A massive statue of the sun god Helios on this island was called its “colossus.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This island is the second most populous of the Balearic Islands, after Majorca (mah-YOR-kah). This island is a popular Spanish tourist destination, and is particularly known for its EDM scene.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Archimedes lived on this island, where he legendarily defended its largest city, Syracuse, against Roman invaders using a heat ray. Mount Etna lies on this largest island in Italy.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a form of spectroscopy named for this type of electromagnetic radiation, molecules can be determined from the fingerprint region of their spectrographs. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this type of radiation, which has wavelengths just longer than visible light. This type of radiation is commonly used in night-vision goggles and remote controls.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Like infrared radiation, this type of radiation at the high wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum is non-ionizing. These waves are used to broadcast using the modulation schemes AM and FM.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This type of electromagnetic radiation has a wavelength between those of infrared radiation and radio waves. This type of radiation is often used to heat up food in a kitchen device named for them.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This resident of Maycomb County, Alabama tells Scout that “You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view… until you climb into his skin and walk around in it.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character. This father of Jem and Scout defends a Black man from assault accusations by the white Ewell family during Tom Robinson’s trial in a 1960 novel.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Atticus appears in this novel by Harper Lee about racial injustice that centers on the Finch family. Go Set a Watchman was marketed as a sequel to this novel, but is now considered its first draft.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] To Kill a Mockingbird is set in the “Deep” part of this general region that includes states like Alabama and Mississippi. It is also a key part of the “Gothic” literature movement from this American region.
parts.answer: the South [accept Deep South; accept Southern Gothic]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a story by this author, Hauchecome picks up the title “Piece of String” and dies of a broken heart after being accused of stealing someone’s wallet. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author of short stories like “Mademoiselle Fifi” and “Ball of Fat.” In another of his stories, Mathilde and her husband live in poverty for a decade, working to repay Madame Forestier (for-ES-tee-ay).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That story about Mathilde by Maupassant is titled for one of these pieces of jewelry made of diamonds. At the end of that story, Madame Forestier reveals that this piece of jewelry had fake beads made of paste.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Maupassant was under the tutelage of this other French author. This author depicted a girl with a seemingly pointless life in his story “A Simple Heart” and wrote of Emma’s infidelity in Madame Bovary.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about ancient Greek mathematicians.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Playfair’s axiom is equivalent to this mathematician’s fifth postulate, in the system of geometry named for him. This “father of geometry” wrote that “parallel” postulate in his Elements.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This mathematician’s student Hippasus was supposedly drowned after discovering irrational numbers. This mathematician’s theorem states that, for the side lengths of a right triangle, a squared plus b squared equals c squared.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This Greek mathematician was the first known person to calculate the circumference of the Earth. This mathematician also developed a “sieve” used to find prime numbers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During a coup, this leader committed suicide by AK-47 at the Palacio de La Moneda. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this socialist leader, who was replaced by the far-right dictator Augusto Pinochet as a result of that coup.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Salvador Allende was president of this country before his death. The capital of this long, thin South American country is Santiago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Allende was the first self-identified follower of this political thinker to be elected president of a Latin American democracy. This thinker co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Friedrich Engels.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This post-World War II art movement developed out of New York and placed an emphasis on emotional expression, movement, and gestures. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this art movement, whose artists included Willem de Kooning and Mark Rothko. Action painting and color field painting are styles within this movement.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This abstract expressionist artist, known as “the Dripper,” used splatter-painting techniques on large horizontal canvases to produce paintings like Autumn Rhythm.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Jackson Pollock spent much of his time in this northeastern U.S. city, whose art museums include the MoMA, or the Museum of Modern Art, and the Met, or the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

parts.label: L
parts.question: With Josef Stefan, this scientist names a law relating the power radiated from a blackbody to its temperature. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this scientist who developed statistical mechanics and the H theorem. A constant named for this scientist is equal to the gas constant divided by Avogadro’s number, and his tombstone bears a thermodynamic equation.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The equation on Boltzmann’s tombstone relates this quantity to the natural logarithm of the number of microstates. This measure of disorder of a system is always increasing in the universe.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Boltzmann’s constant, along with many other constants in physics, is represented by this letter. A subscript of this letter under the letter E is used to represent kinetic energy, and it is also used to abbreviate Kelvins.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This soccer player has opened two fashion boutiques, along with co-designing a range of underwear and sock lines. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this player, the current goals leader among active players and fourth in career all-time goals. This forward left Real Madrid in 2018 after nine years with the team.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Ronaldo is the captain of this country’s national team, where he was born on the island of Madeira. One of his fashion boutiques is located in his hometown of Madeira, and the other is located in this country’s city of Lisbon.
parts.answer: Portugal [or Portuguese Republic or República Portuguesa]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] After his time with Manchester United and Real Madrid, Ronaldo left to play for this Italian team that competes in Serie A. Other players on this team include Paulo Dybala and Gianluigi Buffon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer wrote the music for musicals like A Connecticut Yankee and Babes in Arms. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this composer who had a longtime partnership with lyricist Lorenz Hart. This composer collaborated on musicals like Carousel and South Pacific as part of a duo with Oscar Hammerstein.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Rodgers and Hammerstein musical features a rendition of Uncle Tom’s Cabin and the song “Getting to Know You.” This musical follows the story of a British teacher hired to tutor Thailand’s royal children.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This musical, the first written by Rodgers and Hammerstein together, tells of Laurey’s courtship by rivals Curly and Jud. This musical is set in the title territory, which is now a state just north of Texas.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Friedrich Bessel discovered changes in the motion of this star, inferring its binary companion. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this brightest star in the night sky. This main-sequence star found in Canis Major forms the Winter Triangle with Procyon and Betelgeuse and is often called the Dog Star.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Sirius B, the binary companion of Sirius A, is this type of star. These stars that can come in black, brown, or white types are named for their small size.
parts.answer: dwarf star [accept white dwarf, brown dwarf, or black dwarf]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While white dwarfs are located at the bottom left of this diagram, red and orange dwarfs can be found in its main sequence. This diagram plots the luminosities, stellar classifications, and temperatures of stars.
parts.answer: H-R Diagram [or Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram or HRD]

parts.label: L
parts.question: China harvests about a third of the world’s supply of this crop. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this crop, farmed in paddies and terraces. During the Song Dynasty, a strain of this crop called Champa helped lead to a population boom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The ancient Liangzhu culture farmed rice around this Chinese river, whose drainage basin is home to approximately one third of China’s population. This river is spanned by the Three Gorges Dam.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Due to rice being a staple crop, a poor rice season led to widespread famine in the 1850s during this Chinese dynasty. This last Chinese dynasty faced the Taiping Rebellion partly as a result of that famine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This state’s five national parks include Arches, Zion, and Bryce Canyon, which are all in desert canyonland. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Western state with great geographical diversity whose capital is Salt Lake City.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] A prehistoric lake of this name left exceptionally flat salt flats in Northwestern Utah which share the same name. Those salt flats of this name are the site of many land-speed records.
parts.answer: Bonneville [or Lake Bonneville or the Bonneville Salt Flats]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Park City and Deer Valley are sites in northeastern Utah for this sport. Utah’s suitability for this sport is part of the reason Salt Lake City was awarded the 2002 Olympics.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A central deity in this civilization whose name translates as “Smoking Mirror” lost his foot during a battle against the Earth Monster. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Mesoamerican civilization conquered by Hernán Cortés in the early 16th century. This civilization with capital at Tenochtitlan made sacrifices to deities like Tezcatlipoca and Xipe Totec (SHEEP-uh TOH-tek).

parts.label: B
