parts.question: [E] After the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was sieged and destroyed, this North American country’s capital was built in its place. An eagle on a cactus on this country’s red, white, and green flag refers to the Aztec founding myth.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This central deity in Aztec mythology travelled to the underworld and stole bones that became the first people. This feathered serpent deity’s battles with his brother Tezcatlipoca created and destroyed the four ages.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2012, this man travelled to the deepest part of the Mariana Trench in the Deepsea Challenger submersible. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this director of such movies as The Abyss, Aliens, and The Terminator. This man also directed a movie telling the story of the Heart of the Ocean, a diamond discovered in an underwater shipwreck.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Cameron directed this movie, starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet as lovers aboard the title luxury ocean liner. DiCaprio’s character Jack dies of hypothermia after the title ship hits an iceberg and sinks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this other James Cameron-directed film, humans are colonizing the moon Pandora to mine unobtanium. To explore Pandora, scientists use the title blue-skinned alien-human hybrids.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Common deck archetypes in this card game include Burn, which relies on Instants and Sorceries to do quick damage. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fantasy card game, featuring 5 colors of mana and card types like Artifacts and Planeswalkers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Magic: The Gathering, burn decks typically consist of cards of this color. This primary color is also featured on cards like Incinerate and Lightning Bolt, and its mana symbol is a fireball.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Magic: The Gathering is published by this board game company that also produces Dungeons & Dragons.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city was the birthplace of Boeing, Microsoft, and Starbucks. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city in the Pacific Northwest. This city is home to the Space Needle.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Seattle is the largest city in this state. The Canadian province of British Columbia borders this state on its north.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This inlet connects Seattle and Tacoma to the Pacific Ocean via the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and as such defines the Olympic Peninsula of northwest Washington.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When unpolarized light undergoes this process at Brewster’s angle, it becomes perfectly polarized. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this phenomenon that for light can be “specular” or “diffuse.” This phenomenon occurs when a wavefront changes direction at an interface between media, returning to the original medium.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Reflecting telescopes use curved examples of these devices to observe distant objects. Common household examples of these devices use reflection to allow us to look at ourselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: For specular reflection, the incident and reflected rays have equal angles with a vector described by this adjective. This adjective describes any vector or line perpendicular to an object.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s first attempt at independence was known as the Fredonian Rebellion. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this state that gained independence from Mexico in an 1836 revolution.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This “King of the Wild Frontier” fought for the Republic of Texas, dying at the Alamo. This man is depicted in folk-lore stories and a Disney mini-series that popularized the image of him wearing a coonskin cap.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This man secured Texan independence by capturing Santa Anna at the Battle of San Jacinto. This first president of Texas is the namesake of the state’s largest city.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This phrase is uttered during the so-called “nunnery scene” of the Shakespeare play in which it appears. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this phrase contrasting life and death that is said by a prince in a soliloquy just before Ophelia returns his love letters. It is followed by a musing of “Whether ‘tis nobler in the mind to suffer.”
parts.answer: “to be, or not to be, that is the question”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The phrase “to be, or not to be” appears in this play about a Prince of Denmark. The title character seeks revenge on his uncle Claudius, who killed his father to claim the throne, in this tragedy by Shakespeare.
parts.answer: Hamlet [accept The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The courtier Osric delivers an invitation to one of these events to Hamlet. An event of this type between Laertes and Hamlet involving a poisoned sword ends with every character besides Horatio dying.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Bernoulli’s principle states that when fluid speed increases, either potential energy or this quantity must decrease. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity that is directly proportional to temperature according to Gay-Lussac’s Law. This force per unit area’s atmospheric type can be measured with a barometer and is commonly expressed in torrs, pascals, and psi.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Pressure is multiplied by volume on one side of an equation that describes the “ideal” form of this phase of matter, PV=nRT. This phase of matter has no fixed shape and higher kinetic energy than solids and liquids.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The ideal gas law is a combination of Avogadro’s Law, Gay-Lussac’s Law, Charles’s Law, and this law. This law relates pressure and volume and is typically expressed as P-one V-one equals P-two V-two

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following about unusual moves in the game of chess.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This move, the only one in which the king moves more than one square, requires no pieces between a king and a rook, and that neither has moved. Depending on which rook is used, this technique is “queen-side” or “king-side.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: If one of these pieces is still on its original square, it can move forward two spaces instead of the usual one. They also capture unusually, attacking one square diagonally in front of themselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This move with a French name involves a pawn capturing an adjacent opponent’s pawn, given that the opponent’s last move was to move their pawn two spaces forward from their original square.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Bronze Age Collapse was a sudden disruption for many major ancient civilizations. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The collapse affected civilizations around the eastern side of this body of water. Before the collapse, traders would sail on it from the Nile Delta in Egypt to the Hittite Empire in Anatolia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Dorian invasion of Greece during the Bronze Age Collapse spelled the end of this proto-Greek civilization. This culture wrote in Linear B script and is thought to be the civilization depicted in Homer’s war poems.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Mycenaeans (my-SEE-nee-anz) heavily practiced this art form, creating many vases and urns. Through this art form, they would display floral designs or depict the events of their myths.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author set many of his novels in Yoknapatawpha (YAWK-naw-puh-TAW-fa) County, Mississippi. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this American Author. He wrote about the death of Addie Bundren and her family’s transportation of her coffin to Jefferson in As I Lay Dying.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Faulkner wrote this novel about Benjy, Quentin, and Jason, three members of the Compson family. This novel’s last section focuses on Dilsey, one of the Compson family’s Black servants.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Faulkner wrote his first novel Soldier’s Pay in this city after getting inspiration from Sherwood Anderson. This home to the Faulkner House is the most populous city in Louisiana.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s first Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer (AH-den-ow-er), presided over its economic miracle, which is also called Wirtschaftswunder (veer-CHAHFTS-voonder) or the Miracle on the Rhine. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country which was part of the Western Bloc during the Cold War. Willy Brandt, a leader of this country, championed its philosophy of Ostpolitik which sought to normalize relations with its eastern neighbor.
parts.answer: West Germany [accept Federal Republic of Germany or FRG or BRD or Bonn Republic; prompt on Germany; do not accept or prompt on “East Germany” or “German Democratic Republic” or “GDR” or “DDR”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Willy Brandt’s government toppled when it was revealed that one of his advisors, Gunter Guillaume, was an agent for this organization. This organization was the secret police force of East Germany.
parts.answer: Stasi [accept Ministry for State Security or State Security Service]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although this city was fully inside East Germany, it was separated into West and East portions by an eponymous wall. This city is the current capital of Germany.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The holiday of Eid al-Fitr (EED al-FID-ur) marks the end of this month-long holiday. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this ninth month in the Islamic calendar during which Muslims commemorate Muhammad’s first revelation. This holiday is observed by Muslims as a period of reflection and prayer.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This practice is called sawm in Islam, and is obligatory for all Muslims who are healthy enough to keep it. Eastern Orthodox Christians partake in a partial form of this practice during Lent, when they abstain from eating animal products.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The daily fast during Ramadan begins at sunrise immediately after the morning meal of suhur and ends with this evening meal after sunset. Traditionally, three dates are eaten during this meal to break the fast.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about bears.

parts.label: A
parts.question: These bears possess a hump between their shoulders, which is actually a muscle that powers their forelimbs while they dig for roots and plant bulbs. This type of bear is also known as the North American brown bear.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other type of bear is very similar to the grizzly bear, though they are generally larger. These largest bears in the world inhabit an Alaskan archipelago.
parts.answer: Kodiak brown bears [prompt on Alaskan brown bear]

parts.label: C
parts.question: These bears have lost much of their habitat due to climate change. These white bears are considered marine mammals and are notably found in the Arctic Circle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: If two of these things get within 1,400 kilometers of each other, they can interact and merge in a process known as the Fujiwhara effect. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these weather phenomena. The Saffir-Simpson Scale measures the intensity of these phenomena.

parts.label: B
parts.question: An effect named for this kind of building explains the curvature of the eyes of hurricanes. The Superdome in New Orleans was one of these buildings which was used as a public shelter from Hurricane Katrina.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This force explains the direction of rotation of hurricanes. Storms rotate clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere and counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere due to the deflection caused by this force.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Before the damming of the Amu and Syr Darya rivers, this lake was one of the largest inland lakes in the world. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this lake in Central Asia, which is now split into six different parts. It lies east of the Caspian Sea.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The damming of the rivers was ordered to increase the production of this cash crop in Uzbekistan. This crop was also produced by slaves in the Southern United States before the civil war.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Aral Sea bordered Uzbekistan and this largest land-locked country, whose capital had its name changed in 2019 from Astana to Nur-Sultan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following questions about Bartholomeu Dias.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Dias was an explorer for this country, for whom he sailed to regions such as modern day Namibia and Angola. Another explorer from this country, Pedro Cabral, was the European discoverer of Brazil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: On his way back from a voyage, Dias discovered and rounded this cape on the southern tip of Africa. Dias gave this cape the name “Cape of Storms,” though John II later gave it a more optimistic name.
parts.answer: Cape of Good Hope [prompt on the Cape]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Though Dias wanted to continue his voyage to the Indian Ocean, his crewmates unanimously voted to return to Portugal. This explorer later completed the full voyage, becoming the first European to reach India by sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At the end of this novel, the protagonist sends his old English teacher an object engraved with the line “This object belongs to Mrs. Lorelei Granger, and she may call it any name she chooses.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this novel about Nick Allen, who finds a gold fountain pen in the street and comes up with the idea to create a new word for “pen.” That title word of this novel eventually gains national fame and is eventually added to a dictionary.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Frindle was written by this children’s author of works like No Talking, The Landry News, and Lunch Money.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lunch Money is about Greg Kenton, who, along with childhood rival Maura Shaw, founds a business at his school making and selling this type of book with paneled pictures and speech bubbles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A compound found in these organisms consists of alternating residues of N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these organisms whose peptidoglycan (PEP-tid-oh-GLEYE-can) is broken down by lysozyme. Infections with these single-celled organisms are treated with antibiotics like penicillin, and Salmonella is an example of one.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Lysozyme breaks down the peptidoglycan in these structures of bacteria. This rigid outer layer of cells found in bacteria, fungi, and algae is found outside of the cell membrane in plant cells, but not animal cells.
parts.answer: cell wall [do not accept or prompt on “cell membrane”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Hershey-Chase experiment used these specific organisms to infect E. coli to show that proteins do not function as genetic material. These organisms are a specific type of viruses that infect bacteria.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This artist completed most of his works in his studio, which he called “The Factory,” including his Orange Prince and his Coca Cola artworks. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this American pop-art artist who did many silkscreens during his career and who is known for his Campbell’s Soup Cans.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Andy Warhol used silk-screening to create a diptych of this moviestar pop icon that includes 50 multiplied images of her face. She was also photographed holding down her white dress while it was blown upward.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Gottfried Helnwein's painting Boulevard of Broken Dreams, he replaces the three patrons from this Edward Hopper painting with Marilyn Monroe and two other pop icons.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure’s familiars include the wolves Geri and Freki and the ravens Huginn and Muninn, who brought this deity news from all over Midgard. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Allfather and widely revered god in Norse mythology. This husband of Frigga and father of Thor and Baldr wielded the spear Gungnir and once rode his eight-legged horse Sleipnir (SLAIP-neer) into the underworld.

parts.label: B
parts.question: According to the Poetic Edda, Odin hung for nine straight days on a mythical one of these objects. The branches and roots of Yggdrasil, a cosmic one of these objects, extend into many different realms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The squirrel Ratatosk lives on Yggdrasil (IG-druh-sil) and carries messages from the eagle on top of it to this creature below it. This serpent chews on the corpses of the inhabitants of Náströnd and gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Node is used to run this language on backend webservers, while frameworks like React can be used to augment it on the front-end browser side. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this high-level language, which TypeScript compiles to. While HTML and CSS are used to display and style web content, this language handles dynamic behavior.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] JavaScript scripts can be run by event handlers attached to entries in this hierarchical model of a web page, which correspond to HTML elements. This model is often referred to by a three-letter abbreviation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The DOM takes the form of this data structure, which is hierarchical because elements may have children. The top-most node of this structure is called the root, while the terminating nodes are called leaves.
parts.answer: tree [accept specific types of tree like binary trees]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about polar expeditions that used the ship Fram:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott’s by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.
parts.answer: Roald Amundsen (“ROH-all AW-moon-sen”) [or Roald Engelbregt Gravning Amundsen; accept Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Fram was earlier used by this other Norwegian explorer for his 1893 Arctic expedition. This explorer won the Nobel Peace Prize for his namesake passports, which the League of Nations issued to stateless refugees.
parts.answer: Fridtjof Nansen (“FRIT-yoff NAWN-sin”) [or Fridtjof Wedel-Jarlsberg Nansen; accept Nansen passports]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Fellow Norwegian Otto Sverdrup (“AW-toh SVAR-droop”) led an 1898 expedition to the Arctic islands of this country aboard the Fram. The Norse settlement of Vinland was in this North American country’s province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the dedication of this collection, its composer wrote out a Latin phrase whose initials spell out “ricercar” (“ree-chair-KAHR”) For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this collection by J. S. Bach that includes a “Ricercar a 3” and a “Ricercar a 6,” both based on a thema regium or royal theme. Bach nicknamed the latter “Prussian” after this collection’s dedicatee.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That theme was given to Bach by Frederick II, who played and composed 121 sonatas for this instrument. The trio sonata of The Musical Of ering features this transverse woodwind, which is larger than the piccolo.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Musical Of ering is composed of one sonata, 10 canons, and two ricercars, which are pieces in this form. Similar to the canon, this contrapuntal form is composed of multiple voices that repeat and transform a given theme.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This chef’s exact kitchen, which was the setting for a cooking show this chef hosted with her longtime friend Jacques Pépin (“pay-PAN”), is now preserved whole in the Smithsonian. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Cordon Bleu-trained American chef, who popularized French cuisine to American audiences through books like Mastering the Art of French Cooking and her PBS show The French Chef.
parts.answer: Julia Child [or Julia Carolyn Child or Julia Carolyn McWilliams]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Child first learned to cook from this classic American cookbook by Irma S. Rombauer. This cookbook popularized the “action method” of introducing ingredients within recipe text rather than at the beginning.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Child is known for her love of this fatty ingredient. The thickener roux (“roo”) is most commonly made with flour and this dairy ingredient, which is spread on bread in a proverbial staple meal.
parts.answer: butter [or le beurre; accept bread and butter]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a series of novels by this author, Shigekuni Honda searches for reincarnations of his deceased friend Kiyoaki Matsugae. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Japanese author of The Sea of Fertility tetralogy. Mizoguchi burns down the title structure in this author’s novel The Temple of the Golden Pavilion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In The Temple of the Golden Pavilion, a kōan from this religion inspires Mizoguchi to burn down the temple. Mizoguchi is an acolyte for a priest of the Zen sect of this religion.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In a story by this other Japanese author, a Buddhist priest falsely claims that a dragon will rise up from a lake. The Buddha sends the thief Kandata back to hell after he selfishly tries to prevent others from climbing up to Paradise in another story by this author.
parts.answer: Ryunosuke Akutagawa [or Akutagawa Ryunosuke] (Those short stories are “Dragon: the Old Potter’s Tale” and “The Spider’s Thread,” respectively.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Color changes in indicators like phenolphthalein can be used to determine the concentration of an analyte in this technique. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this analytical technique used in acid-base chemistry experiments. “Curves” produced by this technique graph pH against the volume of liquid dispensed from a burette.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During titration, pH can be calculated by finding the negative log of the concentration of either H+ or this ion. No molecule can create a stronger acid in water than this ion, according to the leveling effect.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The equilibrium constant for an acid-base reaction equals 10 to the power of the difference in this quantity between the conjugate acid and the acid. Finding the inflection point of a titration curve requires finding the concentration where pH equals this value.
parts.answer: pKa [or pK-sub-a; accept power of the acid dissociation constant, do not accept or prompt on “Ka” or “acid dissociation constant”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the creation of geoglyphs, large artworks carved into or built on the natural landscape. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] 2021 soil dating suggested the Cerne Abbas Giant, a geoglyph made of this material, was from the Middle Ages, not the Bronze Age. Trenches filled with this material were used in prehistoric England to create hill figures like the Uffington horse.
parts.answer: chalk [prompt on calcium carbonate or calcite]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Early people in this country removed layers of red pebbles from the desert sand in order to create a series of hundreds of geoglyphs known as the Nazca lines.
parts.answer: Peru [or Republic of Peru or República del Peru]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Early Native American groups depicted animals in geoglyphs called “effigy mounds.” Examples include this state’s 1300-foot-long Great Serpent Mound and the Alligator Mound, which is near this state’s capital of Columbus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A politician with this surname reversed the decision in the Shah Bano case, which gave a Muslim woman the right to seek alimony from her ex-husband. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Give the surname of that politician, who was implicated in the Bofors Scandal. An earlier politician with this surname was assassinated after ordering the storming of the Golden Temple in Operation Blue Star.
parts.answer: Gandhi [accept Rajiv Gandhi or Indira Gandhi]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Rajiv and Indira Gandhi both served as Prime Ministers of this country. The unrelated Mahatma Gandhi worked with Indira’s father Jawaharlal Nehru to gain this country’s independence from the British Empire in 1947.
parts.answer: India [or Republic of India or Bharat Ganarajya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] As Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi ruled by decree in a period known as the Emergency, during which her son Sanjay oversaw a campaign of this practice. In the U.S., this practice was the subject of the case Buck v. Bell.
parts.answer: forced sterilization [or mass sterilization; accept descriptive answers; prompt on eugenics]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Belgian artist René Magritte:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Magritte was a member of this art movement. Many paintings in this 20th century art movement depict otherworldly subjects or were inspired by dreams.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In this Magritte work, a painting on an easel seems to directly depict the landscape seen through a window behind it. A second painting by Magritte with the same title as this painting features the same concept with a seascape.
parts.answer: The Human Condition [or La condition humaine; accept The Human Condition II or La condition humaine II]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] An enormous one of these objects fills up Magritte’s painting The Listening Room. Another of these objects floats in the air in front of the face of a man wearing a suit in Magritte’s The Son of Man.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote, “Christianity has died many times and risen again; for it had a God who knew the way out of the grave,” in his book The Everlasting Man. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this English Catholic writer who wrote about an anarchist council whose members are mostly undercover police in his novel The Man Who Was Thursday. He also created the priest-detective Father Brown.
parts.answer: G. K. Chesterton [or Gilbert Keith Chesterton]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This author described how Chesterton’s Everlasting Man drew him from atheism towards Christianity in his memoir Surprised by Joy. Aslan sacrifices himself and is resurrected in this author’s The Lion, The Witch, and the Wardrobe.
parts.answer: C. S. Lewis [or Clive Staples Lewis]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Everlasting Man is in part a rebuttal of this author’s Outline of History, which tries to stick to “apparent facts” by ignoring the theological significance of Christ. In a novel by this author, Martians invade the Earth using machines called “tripods.”
parts.answer: H. G. Wells [or Herbert George Wells] (The novel is The War of the Worlds.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Supreme Court cases decided in response to this series of programs included Schechter Poultry Corp v. United States and Wickard v. Filburn. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this set of policies proposed by Franklin Roosevelt to help the country recover from the Great Depression. This set of policies included programs like the Works Progress Administration and the Tennessee Valley Authority.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Schechter and Wickard involved differing interpretations of this Constitutional clause, which gives Congress regulatory power over a certain action between states. This clause was also at the center of Gibbons v. Ogden.
parts.answer: Commerce Clause [or Interstate Commerce Clause or Foreign Commerce Clause or Indian Commerce Clause or Article I, Section 8, Clause 3]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Schechter and Wickard were separated by a perceived shift in the Court’s leaning, caused by Owen Roberts concurring with the Court’s liberals. This humorous expression traced to Cal Tinney describes how that shift averted Roosevelt’s “court packing” plan.
parts.answer: the “switch in time that saved nine” [or “A switch in time saves nine” or “a switch in time’ll save nine”; accept any answer with the forms of the words “switch, time, save, and nine” in that order]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Forest ecologist Suzanne Simard has championed the view that “mother trees” use networks of these relationships to transfer nutrients to seedlings. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these usually mutualistic relationships which involve the transfer of sugar from plants to fungi in exchange for mineral nutrients like phosphorus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In contrast to ectomycorrhizae, arbuscular mycorrhizae penetrate the cells of these plant structures. These structures help plants absorb water from the soil and anchor them to the ground.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Mutualistic interactions like mycorrhizae often lead to this process in which two species simultaneously undergo natural selection based on selection pressure from each other. Certain long-petaled orchids can only be pollinated by hawk moths due to this process.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Bernardo is a stand-in for Leonardo da Vinci in a novel from this country in which the prince of an Italian city-state is advised by the title dwarf. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this country. In a chamber play from this country, the ghost of a milkmaid haunts the vengeful, wheelchair-bound Jacob Hummel.
parts.answer: Sweden [or Kingdom of Sweden or Sverige or Konungariket Sverige] (The first novel is The Dwarf by Pär Lagerkvist.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] That play, The Ghost Sonata, is by this Swedish author. The title character’s pet canary is decapitated by the valet Jean in this author’s play Miss Julie.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The author of The Dwarf, Pär Lagerkvist, is among the eight Swedish authors who have won this prize, which is awarded by the Swedish Academy. More recent recipients of this prize include Louise Glück and Bob Dylan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The semantic type of this process occurs when individuals consciously absorb facts and general knowledge. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this phenomenon divided into short-term and long-term types. This phenomenon is the ability of the brain to store and recall information.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Psychologist George Miller posited that humans’short-term memories can only retain a small amount of information, specifically this number of pieces of information, plus or minus two.
parts.answer: seven [prompt on magic number or magical number]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other psychologist studied the misinformation effect by testing the way a question’s wording affected participants’ memory of a car accident.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer some questions about hit songs from the Frozen franchise:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This power ballad from Frozen won an Academy Award for Best Original Song. In it, Elsa sings “the cold never bothered me anyway” as she constructs an ice fortress in the mountains.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This actress, who voiced Elsa in both Frozen and Frozen II, sang “Let it Go.” She also played Elphaba on the original Broadway cast of Wicked.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This Norwegian art pop singer provides backing vocals as The Voice on the song “Into the Unknown” from Frozen II. She included “Runaway” and “Running with the Wolves” on her 2016 debut album All My Demons Greeting Me as a Friend.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This film opens with Terry Malloy using a pigeon to trick Joey into climbing onto the roof, which he’s then thrown off of. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Elia Kazan film, which he made to defend his decision to testify before HUAC. In this film, Terry eventually testifies against the corrupt union leader Johnny Friendly.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In On The Waterfront, Terry’s career in this sport is destroyed when the mob forces him to throw a crucial fight. Jake LaMotta in Raging Bull and Rocky Balboa in Rocky also compete in this sport.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In a scene from Raging Bull, Jake quotes a monologue from On the Waterfront in which Terry laments his boxing career by saying, “You don’t understand! I coulda had class. I coulda been” one of these people.
parts.answer: a contender [accept “I coulda been a contender”; do NOT accept or prompt on synonyms]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Battle of Raseiniai saw the use of the KV model of this weapon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this weapon, other examples of which included the Panther and the Tiger models of Nazi Germany. The Molotov cocktail was originally designed to counter these weapons during the Winter War.
parts.answer: tanks [accept heavy tanks; accept armored tanks]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The KV and T-34 were some of the tanks used by this country as it fought Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front of World War II. This country was led by Joseph Stalin for the duration of the war.
parts.answer: Soviet Union [or Union of Soviet Socialist Republics; or U.S.S.R.; prompt on Russia]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This 1943 battle on the Eastern Front was the largest tank battle in history. This battle was codenamed Operation Citadel and included nearly one thousand German and Soviet tanks fighting at Prokhorovka.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The kinetic form of this force is weaker than the static form of this force because moving objects do not readily adhere to surfaces. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this force which is characterized by a coefficient symbolized mu. This force resists motion when two objects rub up against each other.
parts.answer: friction [accept kinetic friction or static friction]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The amount of kinetic friction experienced by an object moving on a plane is equal to the coefficient of friction multiplied by this force, which is orthogonal to the contact surface.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The angle of repose, which gives the steepest angle at which static friction prevents an object from sliding, is equal to this trigonometric function applied to the coefficient of friction.
parts.answer: arctangent [or arctan or inverse tangent; do NOT accept or prompt on “tangent” or “cotangent”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about poetry referenced in R.A.P. Ferreira’s album Purple Moonlight Pages:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The track “Golden Sardine” begins, “Head honcho in a poncho like Bob Kaufman,” referring to a poet from this movement. An author from this movement fictionalized other members like Gary Snyder and Neal Cassady in his novel The Dharma Bums.
parts.answer: Beat Generation [or beatniks] (The Dharma Bums is by Jack Kerouac.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] “Golden Sardine” also states “I publish the City Lights like Ferlinghetti” in reference to this city’s City Lights bookstore. The Beat Generation was based in this Bay Area city on the tip of a namesake peninsula.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In the track “Leaving Hell,” Ferreira describes “Strivin’ to be the type of poet [this poet] was.” Beat poet Allen Ginsberg asked this poet, “what were you doing down by the watermelons?” in “A Supermarket in California.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about musical instruments in Greek mythology:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Hermes gives this instrument in exchange for a herd of cattle to Apollo, who uses it to win a music contest against the satyr Marsyas. Earlier, Hermes had fashioned this instrument out of a hollow tortoise shell.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] To avoid being pursued by the god Pan, this nymph is transformed into water reeds upon reaching the river Ladon. When he arrives, Pan uses those reeds to create the panpipe, which is also referred to by this nymph’s name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This deity creates a double-reed woodwind instrument known as the aulos, but throws it away once she realizes that playing it makes her cheeks puff up. This deity is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

parts.label: L
parts.question: General Sherman, the largest tree by volume in the world, is in this national park and is of the species that this park is named for. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this national park immediately south of Kings Canyon in the Sierra Nevada mountains, which contains Mount Whitney as well as many of the “giant” species of its namesake tree.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Sequoias are one of the three redwood tree species symbolic of this state. Jeffrey and ponderosa pines are some of the trees that forest this state’s Yosemite National Park.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Another arboreally-named national park, Joshua Tree National Park, is in this desert mostly in California’s south. Death Valley is also in this desert, whose boundaries are largely defined by the range of the Joshua Tree.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A king in this modern-day country apocryphally killed the prince Mingyi Swa in a 1593 duel. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country where King Naresuan ruled the Kingdom of Ayutthaya. The Chakri dynasty would later take power in this country under the leadership of Rama I.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Naresuan’s duel with Mingyi Swa took place on the back of these animals. These animals were often used for war in Southeast Asia, where ivory was also harvested from their tusks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A 1688 coup in Ayutthaya saw the general Phetracha kill the heir to the throne, who was one of these people. The Shimabara rebellion in Japan was led by these people, who also make up the Twenty-Six Martyrs.
parts.answer: Roman Catholics [prompt on Christians by asking, “what denomination?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about a several-million-year-long period of heavy rain called the Carnian pluvial event, or CPE:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The CPE took place during this geologic period. The shift to a warmer, wetter climate helped the dinosaurs gain dominance during this period of the Mesozoic Era that occurred before the Jurassic.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The climate change that caused the CPE may be linked to a series of these events in Wrangellia. An earlier series of these events created the Siberian Traps and likely caused the Permian-Triassic extinction.
parts.answer: volcanic eruptions [or equivalents that mention volcanoes; accept lava flows or flood basalts]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The CPE devastated this group of now-extinct mollusks. Like nautiluses, these cephalopods (“SEH-fuh-loh-pods”) had spiral-shaped external shells that are common in the Mesozoic fossil record.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one novel, this author described “men without skin” who push “the woman with my face” into the sea in a stream-of-consciousness description of the Middle Passage. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author. Another novel by this author begins with a passage from “Dick and Jane” which is repeated without punctuation and then again without spaces.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Morrison used corrupted Dick and Jane quotes as chapter headings in this 1970 novel. At the end of this novel, Soaphead Church tricks Pecola Breedlove into poisoning a dog to convince her that she has the title feature.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Morrison also wrote Beloved, which is about an escaped one of these people who kills her baby before she is recaptured. Robert Hayden’s poem “Middle Passage” describes a journey these people were forced to undertake.
parts.answer: slaves [or enslaved people; prompt on Africans or African-Americans or Black people]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Gerald Finzi dedicated his song cycle Let us garlands bring to this composer and the piece was premiered on this composer’s 70th birthday. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this English composer. His Serenade to Music is scored for 16 solo voices with string orchestra, and he also composed fantasias on themes of Thomas Tallis and “Greensleeves.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The text for both Let us garlands bring and Serenade to Music were drawn from works by this playwright. Vaughan Williams also made an a cappella arrangement of “Full Fathom Five” from this playwright’s The Tempest.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Poems from Walt Whitman’s Leaves of Grass were adapted by Vaughan Williams in his first symphony, which is titled for this location. At its beginning, the choir declares, “Behold [this location] itself.”
parts.answer: the sea [accept A Sea Symphony; do NOT accept or prompt on the “ocean”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Chinese word chànà is derived from a Sanskrit word for a measure of this thing. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this thing. This thing is described in the kalacakra in Jainism, where it is divided into ascending utsarpini and descending avasarpini stages.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The avasarpini time cycle is divided into six periods, the current of which began three years after the death of this twenty-fourth tirthankara and founder of modern Jainism.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The cyclical nature of time in Jainism is used to explain why this process continually occurs. Samsara is the cycle of death and this concept, which in Hinduism involves the transfer of the soul to another body.
parts.answer: reincarnation [or synonyms like rebirth or being born again or transmigration]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Under the presidency of Eduardo Frei, this action was undertaken in Chile in the late 1990s and early 2000s. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Identify this action. An instance of this action targeting the municipal utility SEMAPA in 1999 resulted in a series of protests and riots in Cochabamba, Bolivia.
parts.answer: water privatization [or anything having to do with the privatization of a water supply; prompt on privatization by asking “of what commodity?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] As president of this country, Vicente Fox encouraged privatization of water by creating PROMAGUA. A pair of treaties govern how water from the Rio Grande is shared between this country and its northern neighbor, the United States.
parts.answer: Mexico [or the United Mexican States or Estados Unidos Mexicanos or México]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Water privatization in Latin America is often backed by this financial institution, which has been criticized for unfair lending practices in developing countries. Unlike the IMF, this institution is usually headed by an American.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, a boy uses a “magic lantern” to project a scene onto his bedroom walls depicting the medieval tale of Golo and the countess Geneviève de Brabant. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this novel in which the narrator asks the maid Françoise to deliver a letter to his mother after being deprived of her bedtime kiss. This novel’s narrator recalls his childhood in Combray after eating a madeleine dipped in tea.
parts.answer: In Search of Lost Time (by Marcel Proust) [or Remembrance of Things Past or À la Recherche du Temps Perdu; accept Swann’s Way or Du côté de chez Swann]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Instead of translating the French title of In Search of Lost Time literally, C.K. Scott Moncrieff took the title Remembrance of Things Past from one of these poems by Shakespeare. These poems have fourteen lines.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In In Search of Lost Time, the narrator’s friend Bloch praises this playwright’s line “The daughter of Minos and Pasiphaë” due to its “supreme merit of meaning absolutely nothing.” This French playwright wrote Phèdre.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One solution to the Fermi paradox posits that most intelligent life is trapped in these features. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these features, found under the icy crusts of the moons Europa and Enceladus. These bodies of water cover most of Earth’s surface.
parts.answer: oceans [accept underground oceans or subsurface oceans or subterranean oceans]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This probe discovered silica grains in Enceladus’s gas plumes, suggesting that its ocean may contain hydrothermal vents. This probe is named for an astronomer who observed a large “Division” between Saturn’s A and B rings.
parts.answer: Cassini [accept Cassini Division or Giovanni Domenico Cassini; prompt on Cassini–Huygens]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This other moon’s subsurface ocean is thought to be “sandwiched” between two or more layers of ice. This largest moon of Jupiter possesses its own magnetic field.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this country’s Supreme Court was fired and replaced by the ruling Nuevas Ideas party, the new court ruled that its current president could run for reelection to a second term. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Northern Triangle country, whose president Nayib Bukele has been accused of authoritarianism for actions like sending the military into the parliament building during a vote by legislators.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In September 2021, El Salvador granted this currency the status of legal tender. This first-ever cryptocurrency, invented by a mysterious “Satoshi Nakomoto,” controversially uses energy-intensive proof-of-work.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] El Salvador symbolically mined bitcoin in October 2021 using power generated from a volcano, which is in this category of sustainable energy sources that includes all energy generated from the Earth’s heat.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This official helped draft the Code Noir for France’s Caribbean colonies. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this French chief minister who implemented several mercantilist policies while in office from 1661 to 1683. This minister also encouraged the king of France to establish the French Academy of Sciences.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Colbert served as the chief minister to this French king, known as the “Sun King.” Colbert’s financial reforms were stifled by this king’s spending on the Palace of Versailles and the War of Spanish Succession.
parts.answer: Louis XIV [or Louis the Great or Louis le Grand; prompt on Louis]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Louis’ first chief minister was Cardinal Mazarin, who continued the policies of this other powerful French cardinal. This man led France during the Thirty Years’ War and was called the “Red Eminence.”
parts.answer: Cardinal Richelieu [or Armand Jean du Plessis]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about drawing techniques:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] These drawing implements have a layer of wood surrounding a lead. Different proportions of graphite and clay make them harder or softer, which influences how sharp the line they draw is; a medium grade of hardness is #2.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] When drawing with a pencil, this technique of overlapping lines can be used to suggest shading and depth. Where lines intersect more closely, figures appear darker under this technique.
parts.answer: cross-hatching [do NOT accept or prompt on “hatching”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other technique can also create texture or depth, using dots instead of overlapping lines. Unlike in pointillism, this technique only uses dots of one color.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Johann Bernoulli, who posed this problem, gave both an algebraic and geometric proof showing that its solution is a cycloid curve. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this problem from mechanics which asks which curve gives the least-time descent for a falling, frictionless bead.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Johann’s brother Jakob Bernoulli invoked this law in his solution because both it and the brachistochrone problem rely on the principle of least time. This law relates the sines of the refracted angles to the indices of refraction.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The brachistochrone problem was later solved in a challenge by this English physicist whose third law says that every force has an equal and opposite force.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A director with this last name collaborated with performer Gene Kelly on films like An American in Paris and Brigadoon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give this last name of that director, Vincente. A performer with this last name, Liza, rose to prominence by playing Sally Bowles in Bob Fosse’s musical film Cabaret.
parts.answer: Minnelli [accept Liza Minnelli or Vincente Minnelli]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Liza Minnelli worked with Fosse again when she subbed in for Gwen Verdon on the original production of this musical, which opens with the song “All That Jazz.” The 1996 revival of this musical is now the second longest-running show on Broadway.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Liza Minnelli is one of the few performers to have won an EGOT, meaning she has won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and one of these awards. These awards recognize performances live on Broadway.
parts.answer: Tony Awards [or Antoinette Perry Award for Excellence in Broadway Theater]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem in this language, a man searches in a garden for his “precious pearl without spot,” but he falls asleep and dreams that he meets his infant daughter in Heaven. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this language used to write that poem, Pearl. A romance in this language uses the bob and wheel metrical scheme and sees its title character survive a beheading contest with Sir Bertilak.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The title Arthurian knight faces Sir Bertilak in this romance usually ascribed to the anonymous author of Pearl. In this romance, Bertilak is revealed to be the same character as the knight named for the color of his skin.
parts.answer: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The verse of both Pearl and Sir Gawain and the Green Knight is based on this poetic technique. In this technique, all or most of the stressed words in a line begin with the same sound.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Supreme Court ruled that one form of this policy had to be justified by a compelling government interest in Adarand Constructors vs. Peña. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Identify this kind of policy. These policies were also litigated in the Supreme Court cases Grutter v. Bollinger and a case brought forward by Allan Bakke.
parts.answer: affirmative action [accept race-conscious admissions or race-conscious hiring or race-sensitive admissions or race-sensitive hiring]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Bakke sued this state’s university system after he was denied admission. A ban on racial preferences in admission in this state led to less Black and Hispanic enrollment at the Los Angeles campus of its university system.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Third Circuit Court of Appeals earlier defended this president’s Philadelphia Plan that required government contractors in the city to hire minorities. Archibald Cox, a lawyer in the Bakke case, was previously fired by this president in the Saturday Night Massacre.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organization employs violent criminals as expendable D-class personnel. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this fictional organization whose wiki describes paranormal objects like a statue that snaps people’s necks when no one is looking at it, designated 173.
parts.answer: SCP (“S-C-P”) Foundation [or the Foundation or Secure, Contain, Protect or Special Containment Procedures; accept SCP Wiki or SCP objects or SCP-173]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This character inspired SCP-582, an entity that takes on the properties of any stories written about itself. Some residents of the End in Minecraft are also inspired by this tall, thin Internet folklore character who stalks people in the woods.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] SCP-3008 appears to be an endlessly large one of these stores. This Swedish company, the largest furniture retailer in the world, sells flat-pack furniture and also snacks like meatballs in its stores.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mariano Azuela’s novel The Underdogs is likely the first novel about this conflict. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this conflict. Ambrose Bierce’s involvement and death in this conflict were fictionalized in The Old Gringo.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Mexican author and key figure in the Latin American Boom wrote The Old Gringo. This author detailed the final hours of a veteran of the Mexican Revolution in The Death of Artemio Cruz.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This real-life bandit and Mexican revolutionary orders the death of General Arroyo in The Old Gringo. Azuela’s The Underdogs drew on his experience working as a doctor for this man, who is known by the nickname “Pancho.”
parts.answer: Pancho Villa [or Francisco Villa or José Doroteo Arango Arámbula]

parts.label: L
parts.question: These things can be coated in “cages” of the triskelion-shaped protein clathrin. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these structures, the contents of which may be identified by SNARE proteins on their surfaces to aid in fusion.
parts.answer: vesicles [accept transport vesicles or secretion vesicles; prompt on membranes]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] SNARE proteins like VAMP1 in these structures can be broken down by tetanus toxin or botulism toxin. Secretion vesicles are responsible for release of neurotransmitters in the clefts of these junctions between neurons.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Vesicles targeted to this organelle from the ER are marked with the coat protein COPII. This organelle, named for an Italian biologist, packages proteins into vesicles for transport.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about phonetic changes currently occurring in North American English, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] In California and the “Northern Cities,” chain shifts of these sounds cause them to rotate around the trapezoid they’re visualized on. These sounds are pronounced without obstruction of the vocal tract, unlike consonants.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Many North American dialects are slowly adopting this property of pronouncing the “r” sound after vowels. Like most British dialects, a dialect that doesn’t pronounce the “r” in “heart” possesses the opposite of this property.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Non-rhotic dialects usually compensate for losing the “r” by giving the vowel this property. This property is often incorrectly attributed to English diphthongs in classrooms, or might be marked with a line above the vowel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this amino acid coded for by the single codon UGG. The genes that code for this amino acid’s production in bacteria are a common example of a repressible operon.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Tryptophan is a biological precursor to this pineal gland-secreted hormone responsible for controlling circadian rhythms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Deficiencies in serotonin, another tryptophan derivative, have been linked to this mood disorder characterized by extended feelings of sadness and emptiness.
parts.answer: clinical depression [or major depressive disorder or MDD; accept dysthymia]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem by this author, the speaker states, “I breathed my soul back into me” after a gust of wind blows the smell of an orchard to her. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this openly bisexual poet. She wrote, “All I could see from where I stood / Was three long mountains and a wood” to open that poem, “Renascence.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In “Renascence,” the speaker describes sinking into a grave and lying there until she hears the sound of this substance. In a nursery rhyme, this substance is told “go away / come again some other day.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] After the rainstorm, the speaker of “Renascence” lauds this “multi-colored, multiform” concept, which another Millay poem claims “Euclid alone has looked on.” John Keats wrote, “[this concept] is truth, truth [this concept]” at the end of “Ode on a Grecian Urn.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The parents of this animal are believed to be Orthrus and the Chimera, making it the grandson of Typhon and Echidna. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this animal. The killer of this animal uses its own claws to skin it and return home with its thick fur.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Nemean (“NEE-me-in”) Lion is slain by this man as part of the first of his twelve labors, which also include cleaning the Augean stables and killing the Hydra.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Heracles completes the twelve labors after being commanded to do so by this cousin of his. After Hera causes Heracles to kill his family, the Oracle at Delphi tells him to serve this king of Mycenae and Tiryns.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many of these features were destroyed by a 2007 mudslide in a “Valley of” them on the Kamchatka Peninsula. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these erupting hot springs. Yellowstone National Park is home to many of these features, such as a “Steamboat” one and Old Faithful.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The word “geyser” comes from Geysir (“GAY-seer”), the name of a geyser in this country. In 2010, much air travel was disrupted after the eruption of a volcano in this country.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Many geysers are also in this country’s Taupo Volcanic Zone, which is near its Bay of Plenty. In 2019, twenty-two people died in a volcanic eruption after tour groups failed to evacuate this country’s White Island.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about imported German princes who were made rulers in the Balkans:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Otto I from the House of Wittelsbach was installed as the king of this country after it won its independence. This country’s war for independence saw Edward Codrington defeat the Ottoman navy at the Battle of Navarino.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] William of Wied, the new prince of Albania, quickly faced pressure from this empire to provide troops for World War I. The war was sparked by the assassination of this dual monarchy’s Archduke Franz Ferdinand by a Serb.
parts.answer: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire; prompt on Austria or Hungary]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A German prince with this name from the House of Battenberg was forced to abdicate as prince of Bulgaria just seven years after taking the throne. Troops of a different ruler with this name fought with Bulgarian volunteers against the Ottomans at the Battle of Shipka Pass.
parts.answer: Alexander [accept Alexander of Battenberg or Tsar Alexander II of Russia]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The sound poem “Gadji beri bimba” was written by one member of this art movement, Hugo Ball. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this art movement. Another member of this movement created a series of readymades that included a urinal signed “R. Mutt” that was rejected from an exhibition with a no-rejection policy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That urinal, Fountain, was created by Marcel Duchamp, who also drew a mustache and a beard on this painting in his readymade L.H.O.O.Q. This painting by Leonardo da Vinci depicts a woman with an enigmatic smile.
parts.answer: Mona Lisa [or La Gioconda or La Joconde]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Duchamp was photographed cross-dressing as his alter-ego Rose Sélavy by this other Dada artist. This artist also showed Kiki de Montparnasse holding a mask while resting her head on a table in the photograph Noire et Blanche.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Erdős conjectured that if the sum of the reciprocals of a set of positive integers diverges, then the set contains arbitrarily long sequences of this type. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this type of sequence in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Ben Green and Terence Tao proved that there exist arbitrarily long arithmetic sequences whose terms are all this kind of number. These numbers are only divisible by themselves and one.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This mathematician proved that arithmetic sequences whose first term and common difference are coprime contain infinitely many primes. This mathematician also formulated the pigeonhole principle.
parts.answer: Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet [or Johann Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, a boy has a nightmare in which a wind-up penguin moves around their old house despite not having been wound up. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel in which a boy and his father travel towards the coast in hopes of finding civilization after an unexplained apocalypse.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Road is a novel by this American author of Blood Meridian, who often uses verbose, run-on sentences. This author created the bolt-gun wielding killer Anton Chigurh in his novel No Country for Old Men.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] McCarthy’s novels often blend post-apocalyptic themes with this genre, exemplified by roaming bands of Yuma and the violent Glanton gang in Blood Meridian. Books in this genre often include cowboys and shootouts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A popular Civil War marching song among Union soldiers states that this person’s body “lies a-mouldering in the grave” but “his soul is marching on.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this militant abolitionist who led anti-slavery forces in Bleeding Kansas. This person led the Pottawatomie Massacre and raided the Harper’s Ferry arsenal, seeking to secure arms for a potential slave uprising.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This preacher, a contemporary of Brown’s, was also a militant abolitionist. John Brown used the Sharps rifles smuggled into Kansas by this preacher, which were colloquially known as this man’s “Bibles.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Julia Ward Howe borrowed the tune of the song “John Brown’s Body” to write this patriotic song, which states that “God’s truth” is marching on. This song’s chorus repeats the phrase “Glory, glory, hallelujah.”
parts.answer: “Battle Hymn of the Republic” [or “Mine Eyes Have Seen the Glory”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: G.E.M. Anscombe’s 1958 article “Modern Moral Philosophy” is credited with reviving this approach to ethics. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this approach to ethics that primarily considers ideas like charity or kindness to tell right from wrong. This approach is contrasted with deontology and consequentialism.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] One of the founders of modern virtue ethics, Philippa Foot, formulated a “problem” involving one of these vehicles. In that problem, a person can choose to let one of these vehicles kill five people, or flip a switch so that it only kills one.
parts.answer: trolleys [or trams or streetcars; accept trolley problem]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Many contemporary virtue ethicists draw from this philosopher, who called the highest good a human can achieve “eudaimonia” in his work Nicomachean Ethics.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Budapest Memorandum of 1994 got three countries to give up their stockpiles of these weapons in exchange for guaranteeing their sovereignty. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these weapons, examples of which included the Tsar Bomba in the Soviet Union. The Soviets first developed these weapons four years after the U.S. used them against Hiroshima and Nagasaki to end World War II.
parts.answer: nuclear weapons [accept nuclear bombs or nukes or atomic bombs]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] One of the countries that gave up its Soviet-era nukes was this country where Alexander Lukashenko took power just five months prior to the agreement. Lukashenko has ruled this “last dictatorship in Europe” ever since.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other signatory to the memorandum claimed it was violated when “little green men” invaded its southernmost region in 2014. That invasion took place after the Euromaidan protests in this country.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Hugh Everett’s many-worlds interpretation avoids this process, instead proposing that the universe splits into parallel universes for each possible outcome. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this irreversible process, central to the Copenhagen interpretation, in which measurement of an observable causes the system to be non-deterministically reduced to a single eigenstate.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Like Everett, this earlier physicist held a position similar to the many-worlds interpretation. He names an equation that describes the evolution of the wavefunction over time.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In a critique of the Copenhagen interpretation, Schrödinger proposed a thought experiment where one of these animals would be thought of as both alive and dead, until observation caused it to collapse to just one of those states.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This kind of law was ruled constitutional in the 1926 Supreme Court Case Euclid v. Ambler, which upheld one of this kind of law disallowing industrial uses on some land in the town of Euclid. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this kind of municipal ordinance which divides lands into different areas that have different allowable uses. Policies of this kind that give areas single uses, like single-family residential, are called “Euclidean.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This term refers to zoning allowing for combined uses, in particular several floors of residential on top of retail space. This kind of zoning has become recently trendy due to its generally better sustainability and walkability.
parts.answer: mixed-use zoning [or vertical mixed-use zoning or mixed-use planning or mixed-use development]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In the five-over-one style of mixed-use buildings, the residential floors are framed with this most common framing material for US houses. “Stick” framing uses two-by-fours made of this inexpensive material.
parts.answer: wood [or lumber or timber or mass timber or engineered wood; accept specific kinds of wood]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This song is supposedly the second-most-recorded song ever, topped only by the Beatles’ “Yesterday.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this bossa nova song, originally written by Antonio Carlos Jobim, about someone who “just doesn’t see” the singer smile.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] American saxophonist Stan Getz collaborated with a guitarist of this surname on a landmark bossa nova album. That guitarist’s wife, Astrud, sang the vocals for the recording of “The Girl from Ipanema” on the album.
parts.answer: Gilberto [accept Astrud Gilberto or João Gilberto]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Astrud and João Gilberto were from this South-American country. Bossa nova developed from samba in the late 1950s in this country’s city of Rio de Janeiro.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Alinardo complains to William that his rival outcompeted him for this position by bringing back booty from Silos. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this position, held by the monk Malachi and his assistant Bernard, both of whom are found dead with dark stains on the fingers of their right hands in the novel in which they appear.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Adso of Melk and William of Baskerville discover that a poisoned manuscript was used to kill Malachi and Bernard in this novel by Umberto Eco, which is set at a monastery with a jealously-guarded library.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The poisoned manuscript was a copy of the second book of Aristotle’s Poetics, which analyzes this genre instead of tragedy. Jorge of Burgos considers this genre blasphemous because “laughter makes man similar to monkey.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Translation Movement in this city, which sought to translate works in Ancient Greek, was led by scholars like al-Kindi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this city whose House of Wisdom was a center of learning in the Middle Ages. The 1258 sack of this city resulted in a nearby river running black with ink from the discarded volumes of the House of Wisdom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The caliph Al-Ma’mun established the first one of these facilities in the Islamic world at the House of Wisdom. Ulugh Beg later established a large one of these facilities in Samarkand.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The House of Wisdom was destroyed as part of the 1258 sack of Baghdad by this people. This people’s Ilkhanate was led by Hulagu, the grandson of Genghis Khan, the founder of this people’s empire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Zaitsev’s rule states that these bonds will form between more highly substituted carbons after an elimination. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these bonds which are present between two carbons in alkenes.
parts.answer: carbon-carbon double bonds [prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, pi bonds]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Double bonds consist of one sigma bond and one bond denoted by this letter. This letter also names a constant equal to roughly 3.14.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This hybridization is possessed by carbons with exactly 1 double bond. Every carbon atom in benzene conforms to this hybridization scheme.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the High Priest, a position held by Zadok and Aaron:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Because no one else was permitted to enter this building’s Holy of Holies, the High Priest would tie a rope to his leg before entering so that he could be pulled out if necessary. The second version of this sacred building was destroyed in 70 CE.
parts.answer: Temple [accept the First Temple or the Second Temple or Solomon’s Temple]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The High Priest was appointed by this assembly, the highest body in the Jewish court system. This assembly had 71 members and met in the Temple in Jerusalem.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This ethnic group claims descent from the Israelites who rejected Eli as High Priest and instead followed Uzzi to Mount Gerizim. In one of Jesus’ parables, a traveller is helped by a “good” member of this ethnic group.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Polish virtuosa Wanda Landowska (“VAHN-dah lan-DOHV-skah”):

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Landowska commissioned Manuel de Falla to write a concerto for this instrument, which she played. This plucked-string keyboard instrument preceded the modern piano.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Landowska also commissioned this French composer to write his Concert champetre (“kon-SAIR shawm-PET”). This composer wrote the opera Dialogue of the Carmelites and was a member of Les Six alongside Arthur Honegger (“oh-neh-GAIR”) and Darius Milhaud (“mee-YO”).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Landowska made the first modern harpsichord recordings of this composer’s Goldberg Variations. This composer’s Italian Concerto and Well-Tempered Clavier were also recorded by Landowska.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a novel by this author, a teleportation-like ability called Conduction saves Hiram Walker after he falls into a river. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author who depicted slaves as “the Tasked” and slave owners as “the Quality” in his novel The Water Dancer. This author wrote the book Between the World and Me and the essay “The Case for Reparations.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In The Water Dancer, a character whose nickname comes from this figure tells Hiram that “memory is the chariot.” That character, Harriet Tubman, parallels this biblical figure who led the Israelites out of Egypt.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In 2016, Coates took on the job of writing several books in this form, including the series “A Nation Under Our Feet.” Adrian Veidt teleports a gigantic squid into New York City to avoid a nuclear war in Watchmen, a book in this form by Alan Moore.
parts.answer: graphic novels [or comic books or comics]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the Japanese popular music genre enka:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Because the genre is popular with older generations of Japanese and represents a romanticized view of traditions, many female enka singers wear this traditional Japanese garment secured by an obi sash.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A key characteristic of enka is the vocal technique of kobushi, which is often compared to this technique in Western music. For string instruments, this technique involves “wobbling” the finger on the fingerboard.
parts.answer: vibrato [do NOT accept or prompt on “tremolo”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The yona nuki scale used by many enka songs omits the fourth and seventh of the Western scale, making it effectively one of these scales common in East Asian music that can be played on a piano’s black keys.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this author who wrote about the love between Raina and the Serbian officer Bluntschli in the play Arms and the Man. In another play by this author, the professor Henry Higgins trains a flower girl to speak like a duchess.
parts.answer: George Bernard Shaw (The second play is Pygmalion.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Shaw’s Arms and the Man takes its title from the opening line of this poet’s The Aeneid.
parts.answer: Virgil [or Vergil or Publius Vergilius Maro]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The first stanza of The Aeneid introduces the anger of this figure. In Arms and the Man, Bluntschli hides from Bulgarian soldiers in Raina’s bedroom, which parallels a storm that this figure asks Aeolus to send to hinder Aeneas and the Trojans.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this text which begins with the Gylfaginning. Many Norse myths like the death of Baldr are known primarily from this text, which was compiled by Snorri Sturluson.
parts.answer: Prose Edda [or Younger Edda; prompt on Edda or Snorri’s Edda; do NOT accept or prompt on “Poetic Edda”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Gylfaginning describes a myth in which this god and his two brothers kill the primordial giant Ymir. In another myth, this chief of the Norse gods hangs himself from Yggdrasil to gain knowledge.
parts.answer: Odin [or Allfather; accept Wotan or Woden]

parts.label: C
parts.question: According to the Gylfaginning, after killing Ymir, Odin and his brothers make the sky out of Ymir’s skull and hold it up using four of these creatures. After Loki cuts off Sif’s hair, these creatures make a replacement.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this president, whose scandal-ridden administration also dealt with the Whiskey Ring and Credit Mobilier scandals.
parts.answer: Ulysses S. Grant [or Hiram Ulysses Grant]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Trader Post scandal involved Belknap accepting kickbacks from traders, partially because he was indebted from renting this politician’s former house. Earlier, this politician resolved the Trent Affair in one cabinet position.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Belknap was ultimately subject to this process by Congress wherein federal officials are charged with a crime. Andrew Johnson was subject to this process as president, which happened twice to former president Donald Trump.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these curved paths caused by gravitational interactions. They include the Earth’s trajectory around the Sun and the Moon’s trajectory around the Earth.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The efficiency of an orbital maneuver is typically measured by a value denoted “delta-[this quantity].” This quantity is squared and divided by radius to give centripetal acceleration.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Because delta-v budgets are limited, spacecraft may use these maneuvers to change speed without expending fuel. These maneuvers involve flying close to a massive object and using its orbital motion to modify the path of the spacecraft.
parts.answer: gravity assists [or gravitational slingshots; or swing-bys; prompt on fly-bys]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country led by John Curtin for the majority of the Second World War. Japan bombed this country’s cities of Darwin and Broome during the war, which also saw increased benefits for this country’s Aborigines.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Australian and American forces defended Australia’s Territory of Papua at the Battle of the Coral Sea, which saw the first combat engagement of these ships. The USS Abraham Lincoln is one of the Nimitz-class of these ships.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The 9th Australian Division sustained heavy casualties at a battle at this location. A later battle at this location saw Allied forces launch Operation Supercharge under the leadership of Bernard Montgomery.
parts.answer: El Alamein [accept First Battle of El Alamein or Second Battle of El Alamein]

parts.label: L
