parts.question: In an episode of this show, Kit throws a prom for Holden, who is slated to undergo heart surgery. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this critically-panned show airing on Hulu Plus as well as YouTube, which stars Lauren Kettering, Madi Monroe, and others as volunteers at the title hospital.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Most of the actors on Attaway General are stars on this social media platform. The Chinese company Bytedance owns this app, some stars of which also lived together in the “Hype House.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Dixie and Charli are TikTok-famous sisters with this last name. While only Dixie appeared on Attaway General, both sisters with this last name left the Hype House amid much drama in early 2020.
parts.answer: D’Amelio [or Charli D’Amelio or Dixie D’Amelio]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country that was home to a 1937 exhibition of so-called “degenerate art.” That exhibition mocked artworks that were part of some movements in this country like New Objectivity.
parts.answer: Germany [or Federal Republic of Germany or Bundesrepublik Deutschland; accept West Germany or Nazi Germany or the Third Reich]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Like many contemporary German artists, Anselm Kiefer’s work is heavily inspired by this World War II era genocide that killed two thirds of Europe’s Jewish population.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although he was an ardent Nazi, the most-exhibited artist at the Degenerate Art Exhibition was Emil Nolde, a member of this movement. Another artist from this movement showed himself in his studio with one hand amputated in Self-Portrait as a Soldier.
parts.answer: Die Brücke [or The Bridge] (Self-Portrait as a Soldier is by Ernst Kirchner.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about ocean acidification, “global warming’s equally evil twin”:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Ocean acidification occurs when this atmospheric gas dissolves in seawater, forming carbonic acid. This triatomic (“TRY-uh-tom-ick”) greenhouse gas is produced by the combustion of fossil fuels.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Ocean acidification disrupts the natural buffering system between carbonic acid and this anion (“AN-eye-on”). This ion has the formula HCO3 – (“H-C-O-three-minus”) and is found with sodium in a common leavening (“LEV-uh-neeng”) agent.
parts.answer: bicarbonate [or hydrogen carbonate; do NOT accept or prompt on “carbonate”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Ocean acidification is tracked by measuring this mineral’s saturation state. Reef-building corals make their skeletons out of this calcium-carbonate mineral that is less stable than calcite.
parts.answer: aragonite (“uh-RAG-uh-nite”) [do NOT accept or prompt on “limestone”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this ancient Greek poet whose surviving corpus consists mostly of short fragments. This poet addressed a “deathless” goddess with an “iridescent throne” in “Ode to Aphrodite.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Because Sappho wrote love poems about other women, she is the origin of “sapphic” and this other word, which derives from the name of her home island. The ‘L’ in “LGBT” stands for this word.
parts.answer: lesbian (Sappho was from the island of Lesbos.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Many of Sappho’s fragments were discovered at Oxyrhynchus, an archaeological site in this region. A palinode by Stesichorus about a woman who hid in this region inspired a poem set here by H.D.
parts.answer: Egypt (H.D.’s poem is Helen in Egypt.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city where during that defense a besieging fleet was supposedly hauled over land into the Golden Horn. The army protecting this city retreated to the Blachernae palace after the Theodosian walls were overrun.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Constantinople fell in 1453 to this empire. This empire ruled much of the Balkans and the Middle East until it was dissolved and became the modern Republic of Turkey.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The mercenaries led by Giustiniani primarily hailed from this city. Andrea Doria served as a capable admiral for and governed this Italian city-state, which was a maritime rival of Venice in the Mediterranean Sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about how to organize the books in a library:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This system, used to classify books in many US libraries, is hierarchical. For example, the 900 block for history contains the 930 block for ancient history in this “Decimal System.”
parts.answer: Dewey Decimal System [or Dewey Decimal Classification]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other classification system is used more often in larger libraries, like most university libraries. This system mixes letters and numbers to encode information like publication year and the first letter of the author’s last name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Since classifying books is basically organizing knowledge, most systems are ultimately inspired by the division of knowledge in this thinker’s Advancement of Learning. This thinker also anticipated the scientific method in his Novum Organum.
parts.answer: Francis Bacon [or Baron Verulam; or 1st Viscount St. Albans]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One member of this profession speaks through an interpreter who always says “my buttocks” when he means to say “myself.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this profession held by Mr. Brown and the hostile Mr. Smith. When members of this profession request a plot of land, they are given a part of the Evil Forest.
parts.answer: Christian missionaries [prompt on reverend or pastor or minister or other terms for religious leaders]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Christian missionaries arrive and upset the social order in Umuofia in this novel. After this novel’s main character hangs himself, the District Commissioner considers writing about him in a memoir about the “pacification” of “primitive tribes.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Things Fall Apart is by Chinua Achebe, who is from this country. The novels Americanah and Purple Hibiscus are by another author from this country, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Muslims claim that God revealed teachings to this figure through a work known as the injil. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this figure who was raised to heaven so that he can return to help the Mahdi kill the Dajjal.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Injil is considered one of the four holy books of Islam, alongside the Zabur, Torah, and this text revealed to Muhammad.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Apart from the four holy books of Islam, Muslims also study these texts, which are collections of sayings and deeds of the prophet Muhammad.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of this political party reportedly claimed “After Hitler, our turn,” because they believed Hitler’s reign as chancellor would be short-lived. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this political party that was led in the 1932 German elections by Ernst Thalmann. This party was founded by the leader of the Spartacist revolt, Rosa Luxemburg.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Communists lost the elections of 1932 to this far-right political party, which was led by Adolf Hitler. This party carried out the Holocaust and was in power until Germany’s defeat in World War II.
parts.answer: Nazi Party [or National Socialist German Worker’s Party or Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hitler and the Nazis were able to consolidate political power after this event through the Enabling Act. This event was blamed on a Dutch communist, resulting in the arrest of the entire Communist parliamentary delegation.
parts.answer: Reichstag fire [or Reichstagsbrand; accept any answers indicating the burning of the Reichstag]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A major milestone in this stage of development is the ability to recognize that objects still exist when they cannot be seen, called object permanence. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this cognitive stage, proposed to last from birth until the start of the preoperational stage at around two years old.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The sensorimotor stage is the first of this psychologist's four stages of cognitive development, which describe patterns in how children progress to adulthood.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Piaget observed that infants in the sensorimotor stage tend to develop an “anxiety” surrounding these people, due to fear of unfamiliarity and unpredictability. That anxiety may be reinforced by parental warnings about the “danger” of these people.
parts.answer: strangers [accept stranger anxiety or stranger danger]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about 20th century Hungarian composer György Ligeti (“jurj LIG-uh-tee”):

parts.label: A
parts.question: Ligeti rose to prominence after his micropolyphonic Lux Aeterna and Requiem were used without his permission in this film. Richard Strauss’s Also sprach Zarathustra plays as monkeys develop tools in this film.

parts.label: B
parts.question: From his Musica Ricercata, Ligeti extracted and rearranged six movements as six of these pieces for wind quintet. Beethoven’s Für Elise is another example of these often short and light pieces.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Ligeti’s avant-garde Poème Symphonique calls for 100 of these devices to be started all at once and gradually wind down. These devices produce clicks at regular intervals to help musicians keep time.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about advances in agricultural technology:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Medieval Europe saw the introduction of the three-field system of this process, in which one field was planted with oats or lentils and another left fallow. George Washington Carver advocated performing this process with legumes to increase the nitrogen content of soil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The 20th century Green Revolution saw a dramatic spike in crop production due to the use of pesticides and this technology. This general class of substances includes any material added to soil to provide plant nutrients.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This scientist’s work in Mexico led him to breed wheat varieties resistant to rust. This “father of the Green revolution” is credited with saving over a billion people from starvation by developing semi-dwarf wheat.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In an essay by this author, Officer Gerrans confiscates the author’s notebook. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this author who examined hippie life in the Haight-Ashbury district of San Francisco in her essay “Slouching Towards Bethlehem.” This author also wrote a 1979 book of essays titled The White Album.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Both the first sentence and the title of “Slouching Towards Bethlehem” reference a poem by this author. That poem by this author opens with an image of a falcon “turning and turning in the widening gyre.”
parts.answer: W. B. Yeats [or William Butler Yeats] (The poem is “The Second Coming”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: “Slouching Towards Bethlehem” appears in a collection that also includes an essay about this city’s Santa Ana winds. In Didion’s novel Play It as It Lays, the actress Maria Wyeth moves to the neighborhood of Hollywood in this city.
parts.answer: Los Angeles [or LA; accept “Los Angeles Notebook”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Victor Berger was the first member of a party representing this ideology to be elected to Congress in the United States. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this left-wing ideology, whose “sewer” type was used to describe some politicians around the turn of the 20th century. More recently, the “democratic” form of this ideology has been advocated by Bernie Sanders.
parts.answer: socialism [accept Socialist Party; accept democratic socialism or sewer socialism]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Emil Seidel became the first Socialist mayor of a major American city after being elected mayor of this city in 1910. “Sewer socialism” was coined to mock socialists from this city who bragged about their great sewer system.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] After being defeated in Milwaukee’s 1912 mayoral election, Seidel became the running mate for this Socialist presidential candidate. This politician ran the last of his five presidential bids from prison in 1920.
parts.answer: Eugene V. Debs [or Eugene Victor Debs]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A character in this play hurls a plate of linguini at the wall and complains about a note reading “We’re all out of Corn Flakes. F.U.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this play in which Felix Ungar stays with his friend Oscar after his wife kicks him out of their house. Felix moves in with the Pigeon sisters at the end of this play by Neil Simon.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Pigeon sisters, Gwendolyn and Cecily, are named for the female leads of this play. In this play, Jack and Algernon schedule a christening because Gwendolyn and Cecily refuse to marry them on the basis of their names.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The premiere of Neil Simon’s The Odd Couple and the American premiere of Oscar Wilde’s The Importance of Being Earnest both took place in this New York City theater district, which is home to many musicals.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This show’s third season was released in 2021 and follows the divorce of Denise, a Black lesbian novelist. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Netflix series that follows Dev Shah, a struggling Indian actor who moves to Italy to learn how to make pasta after breaking up with his girlfriend Rachel.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Master of None was created by and stars Aziz Ansari, who also starred in this comedy TV series about the title Pawnee, Indiana government department. Nick Offerman plays the libertarian Ron Swanson on this show.
parts.answer: Parks and Recreation [or Parks and Rec; prompt on PNR]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In Master of None, Denise is played by Lena Waithe, who titled one of her own shows after this home city of hers. A series about the workers of Firehouse 51 in this city spawned a number of spinoffs that all air on NBC.
parts.answer: Chicago, Illinois [accept The Chi or Chi-Town] (The other series is Chicago Fire, whose spinoffs include Chicago P.D., Chicago Med, and Chicago Justice.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Rosetta@home project aims to improve prediction of this process in part by analyzing user inputs to a video game that challenges users to simulate it as accurately as possible. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this process which would take an impossibly long amount of time to do by chance according to Levinthal’s paradox.
parts.answer: protein folding [accept word forms] (The name of the game mentioned in the leadin is called Foldit.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The deep learning algorithm AlphaFold predicts protein structure based only on the order of these subunits, which make up a protein's primary structure. In proteins, these compounds are connected by peptide bonds.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mutations in the PrP gene can cause the formation of these agents made of misfolded proteins that in turn cause other, normal proteins to take on their shape. Scrapie, kuru, and mad cow disease are all caused by these agents.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Leon Battista Alberti’s trabeated three-tiered design for the facade of one of these buildings progresses from rustication to ornamentation with each ascending floor. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these buildings, one of which Alberti designed for the Rucellai (“ROO-chuh-lye”) family. A copy of Michelangelo’s David stands in one of these buildings nicknamed “vecchio” (“VEH-kee-oh”).
parts.answer: palaces [or palazzo or palazzi; accept Palazzo Rucellai; accept Palazzo Vecchio]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Both the Palazzo Rucellai and Palazzo Vecchio stand in this city. Filippo Brunelleschi used a herringbone pattern to construct a dome in this city that, to this day, remains the world’s largest brick and mortar dome.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Many palazzi like the Palazzo Pitti now function as these institutions. Other examples of these institutions include the Uffizi and the Louvre.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A NASA space telescope named after this scientist is the most sensitive X-ray telescope in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Indian-American astrophysicist who calculated a “limit” equal to about 1.4 solar masses.
parts.answer: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar [prompt on Chandra X-ray Observatory]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Chandrasekhar limit gives the highest stable mass of these objects, above which they undergo Type Ia (“one-A”) supernovae. The Sun will become one of these objects at the end of its life.
parts.answer: white dwarfs [or degenerate dwarfs; prompt on dwarf stars or degenerate stars or compact stars or stellar remnants]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Below the Chandrasekhar limit, white dwarfs are stabilized against this force by electron degeneracy pressure. This attractive force occurs between all objects with mass, like the Earth and the Moon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem, this character remarks that Friday “had a pretty body” after lamenting, “If only he had been a woman!” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this character who narrates that poem set after his return to England. This character survives on a desert island for twenty-eight years with his companion Friday in a novel by Daniel Defoe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] That poem, “Crusoe in England,” is by this author. This poet wrote, “The art of losing isn’t hard to master” in her villanelle, “One Art.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In “Crusoe in England,” the speaker recalls failing to remember that “of solitude” is the phrase that succeeds this poem’s lines, “that inward eye / Which is the bliss…” The speaker sees a “host” of golden flowers in this poem by William Wordsworth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The 2020 iteration of this project had a much higher rate of unanswered questions than usual. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this project that surveys the entire U.S. population every ten years to gather demographic information and tally the country’s number of inhabitants.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Controversially, the 2020 census added this statistical phenomenon to its results as part of the practice of “differential privacy.” The ratio of signal to this phenomenon is used to quantify the purity of information.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] As a result of differential privacy, the 2020 census “counted” a non-existent second person in Monowi, a town in this state which actually only has one resident.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The first movement of this composer’s fifteenth and final symphony repeatedly quotes from Rossini’s William Tell overture. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this composer. His fifteenth symphony includes his “D, E-flat, C, B” or “D-S-C-H” monogram, and its finale is reminiscent of the “invasion theme” he wrote in a previous symphony.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The finale of Shostakovich’s fifteenth symphony quotes the fate motif from Die Walküre, an opera by this German composer of the Ring cycle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The finale of Shostakovich’s final composition, a sonata for viola and piano, paraphrases the repeated rising right-hand triplets G-sharp, C-sharp, E that begin this piece. A slow adagio sostenuto comprises the first movement of this Beethoven piece.
parts.answer: Moonlight Sonata [or Piano Sonata No. 14 or Fourteenth Piano Sonata or Opus 27 No. 2; prompt on partial answers]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This woman apocryphally declared that “purple is the noblest shroud” during the Nika Riots. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this empress of the Byzantine Empire who met her husband Justinian through their shared support for the Blue faction of the demes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Theodora originally worked as an actress and in this other profession, later advocating for women in this profession as empress. Hetairai were women in this profession in ancient Greece who often worked at brothels.
parts.answer: prostitution [accept any answers describing sex work]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While Justinian was ill with the plague, Theodora confiscated the wealth of this prominent Byzantine general. This general defeated the Vandals at the battle of Ad Decimum and captured Ravenna from the Ostrogoths.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One lover of this deity transforms into a cypress tree after accidentally killing a deer. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this lover of the boy Cyparissus. This Greek god of light and music is the twin of Artemis.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In another myth, Apollo becomes infatuated with this nymph after being struck by one of Cupid’s arrows. To escape his pursuits, this nymph prays to her father Peneus, who transforms her into a laurel tree.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Yet another unfortunate lover of Apollo is this man, who is killed after a jealous Zephyrus redirects a discus to hit him. After this man’s death, Apollo creates a flower out of his blood.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Edward Witten proposed that all versions of this theory could be united into a single M-theory, although a mathematical formulation for that theory has yet to be found. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this potential theory of everything, which models all elementary particles as vibrations of tiny harmonic oscillators.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] One theoretical success of string theory is its ability to replicate predictions of the thermodynamics of these things. These astronomical bodies are so dense that even light cannot escape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A niche theory in modern physics combines string theory with this other theory of everything, which proposes that every elementary particle has a partner whose spin differs by one-half.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This musician lost the use of two fingers on his left hand after he accidentally knocked over a candle, badly burning himself. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this French-Romani jazz guitarist. He composed the standards “Minor Swing” and “Nuages” with his Quintette du Hot Club de France.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Reinhardt’s album Djangology features a recording of the “I Got Rhythm,” a standard by this American composer. This composer fused jazz with classical music in pieces like An American in Paris.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Django Reinhardt also recorded a number of pieces with Duke Ellington, who played this keyboard instrument. Thelonius Monk and Herbie Hancock also played this instrument with 88 black and white keys.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician’s namesake act ended up dispossessing the Five Civilized Tribes of over 90 million acres of land, though he was displeased with the final version of the bill. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this politician. After serving as Senate Majority Leader, this politician served as Herbert Hoover’s vice president, becoming the first vice president with non-European ancestry through his Native American heritage.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Curtis was in favor of sending Native American children to be educated in “boarding” types of these places. Dartmouth, one of these places in New Hampshire, was originally founded to Christianize Native Americans.
parts.answer: boarding schools [accept more specific types of schools like colleges or university]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In Congress, Curtis introduced the first version of this proposed constitutional amendment that addressed women’s rights. This amendment was approved by Congress in the 1970s but failed to be ratified by the states.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An essay by this author argues that one character’s “tragedy” is that “he admits the possibility of his being sub-human and feels constrained, therefore, to battle for his humanity.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this author. The fourteen-year-old John Grimes experiences a religious revelation while lying on the threshing-floor of a church in this author’s novel Go Tell It on the Mountain.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In this essay, Baldwin criticizes the violence of Richard Wright’s Native Son and the “self-righteous, virtuous sentimentality” of a Harriet Beecher Stowe novel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] “Everybody’s Protest Novel” calls Bigger Thomas, the protagonist of Native Son, the “descendant” of this character created by Stowe. This character appears in an anti-slavery novel titled for “[this character’s] Cabin.”
parts.answer: Uncle Tom [accept Uncle Tom’s Cabin; or, Life Among the Lowly]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This test involves summing observed value minus expected value squared over expected value for each category, and then comparing the result to this test’s namesake distribution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this statistical test, used to determine the goodness-of-fit between a given distribution and the population distribution. This test is named for a Greek letter.
parts.answer: chi-squared test [or chi-square test; prompt on chi]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Like Student’s t-distribution, the chi-squared distribution takes this single parameter, equal to the number of categories minus one. This quantity can be thought of as the dimension of the domain of a random vector.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The central limit theorem can be used to show that as the degrees of freedom approach infinity, the chi-squared distribution approaches this distribution. This symmetric, bell-shaped distribution is ubiquitous in statistics.
parts.answer: normal distribution [or Gaussian distribution; prompt on bell curve]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The demons Beelzebub, Apollyon, and Legion build this place to tempt people passing through with “merchandise” like “lusts, pleasures, and delights of all sorts.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this place. A jury including Mr. Blind-man and Mr. Cruelty imprison Christian and order Faithful to be burnt at the stake after they refuse to buy goods from this place.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Christian and Faithful travel through Vanity Fair while on their way to the Celestial City in this allegorical novel by John Bunyan.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Meg dresses up to attend a party hosted by the wealthy Annie Moffat in this novel’s chapter “Meg Goes to Vanity Fair.” The March sisters are inspired by The Pilgrim’s Progress to take up their burdens and lead a Christian life in this novel by Louisa May Alcott.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, name these counties along the southern coast of Britain:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Commoners are allowed to let their ponies graze in this county’s New Forest, one of the last areas of unenclosed land in England. This county lends its name to a U.S. state east of Vermont and southwest of Maine.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This county in the east of England shares its name with the first of the seven Anglo-Saxon kingdoms to convert to Christianity. Canterbury Cathedral is in this Home County, which borders the Thames Estuary to its north.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In the other direction, this county west of Devon contains the westernmost point of mainland England, Land’s End. This county is considered a Celtic nation and is the home of Tristan in the Arthurian legends.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Nurbanu Sultan, the real power behind the Ottoman throne from 1574 to 1583:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Nurbanu was the mother of Murad III, the successor to a sultan with this name. The first sultan with this name defeated the Safavids at the Battle of Chaldiran and destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate to conquer Egypt.
parts.answer: Selim [accept Selim I or Selim the Grim or Selim II or Selim the Sot]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Nurbanu claimed to be from this polity, and she actively promoted policies benefiting this polity. The Ottomans took over the islands of Cyprus and Crete from this polity, which controlled them as part of the Stato da Mar.
parts.answer: Venice [accept Most Serene Republic of Venice or Venetian Republic]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Nurbanu commissioned Mimar Sinan to construct one of these buildings in the Uskudar district of Istanbul. The Hagia Sophia was converted into one of these Muslim religious buildings after the Fall of Constantinople.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These arguments are called “non-constructive” if they show that an object exists but do not provide a method for creating it. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these logical arguments that show a given statement is true by deriving it according to accepted rules of inference. In high school geometry, these arguments are often organized into two columns.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This type of proof is also called an indirect proof, since it contrasts with proofs that directly derive a statement from axioms. In this type of proof, one supposes the statement to be proved is false and then derives an absurdity.
parts.answer: proof by contradiction [prompt on reductio ad absurdum; do NOT accept or prompt on “proof by negation”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Proof by contradiction is not a valid form of proof in intuitionistic logic because it rejects this law. This law states that, for any statement X, either X or ¬X (“not X”) is true.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The French government recalled its ambassadors to the United States and this country in response to a 2021 nuclear submarine deal which replaced an existing deal with France. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country. Joe Biden and this country’s prime minister, Scott Morrison, announced that the U.S. would sell nuclear submarines to this country.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This near neighbor of Australia won’t allow its nuclear submarines into its territorial waters, in keeping with its “Nuclear Free Zone” policy. The Rainbow Warrior was sunk by French agents in this country’s city of Auckland.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The United States, New Zealand, and Australia are three of the countries in this intelligence alliance of English-speaking countries. This intelligence alliance uses the Stone Ghost network to share information.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This ethnic group’s holy books are generally considered to be forgeries from the 1910s written in response to Western interest in their religion. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Iraqi ethno-religious group persecuted by ISIS for being “devil worshippers” due to their veneration of the Peacock God Melek Taus.
parts.answer: Yazidi [or Ezidis; or Yezidis; prompt on Kurds]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Yazidis have two main religious texts, one which describes the sayings of Melek Taus. That text shares its name with this Biblical book by “John of Patmos” that opens with letters to seven churches and features events such as the opening of seven seals.
parts.answer: Book of Revelation [do NOT accept or prompt on “Revelations”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The other Yazidi holy book, the Black Book, describes the beliefs of the Yazidis, such as how they are descended from this first man, but not his wife, Eve.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Naumachiae were events that featured these things. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these things that made up the Classis Misenensis and Classis Ravennas in ancient Rome. The Romans equipped many of these things with a corvus.
parts.answer: Roman ships [accept hexaremes or quinquiremes or quadriremes or triremes or liburnians; accept naves]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Naumachiae were naval battles that were sometimes held in amphitheatres that typically held fights between these people. The retiarius and murmillo were types of these people who fought in the Colosseum.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Before the construction of the Colosseum, this emperor and husband of Agrippina the Younger held a massive naumachia on the Fucine Lake. This emperor’s other maritime spectacles included fighting a killer whale in the harbor of Ostia.
parts.answer: Claudius [or Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of this author’s characters takes her name from the island where she finds mystical “spirit water.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this postmodern Japanese author. In a novel by this author, Toru Okada contacts his missing wife Kumiko after the psychic sisters Malta and Creta Kano show him the link between reality and dreams.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Toru originally meets Malta Kano to help him perform this action in The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle. In Murakami’s other novel Kafka on the Shore, Nakata makes money by using his supernatural abilities to perform this action.
parts.answer: finding lost cats [accept anything that indicates searching for cats; prompt on answers about searching for missing pets or animals by asking “what type of animal?”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Tengo reads a book about a young man getting lost in a town of cats in Murakami’s novel 1Q84, which takes its title from this British author’s dystopian novel 1984.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the chemistry of cleaning products, for 10 points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Soaps and detergents are surfactants, which are substances that decrease this force. This force arises because of water molecules’ cohesion, makes droplets form from a stream and allows some insects to walk on water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This substance is the key ingredient in the soap-making process, where saponification transforms it into soap and, usually, glycerin. This strong base was traditionally made by leaching wood ash with water.
parts.answer: lye [or sodium hydroxide or NaOH; accept potassium hydroxide or KOH]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Dilute solutions of this other base are used as another cleaning product, and work by forming soap when reacting with oily dirt. This compound, which is most widely used in fertilizers, is made using the Haber process.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A character of this type gives Special Order 937, which states: “Priority one: Insure return of organism for analysis. All other considerations secondary. Crew expendable.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this type of character. One of these characters called “Mother” intended for that order to be communicated to Ash, but not to Ripley and other crew members aboard the Nostromo.
parts.answer: computer [or artificial intelligence or AI; accept answers describing space ship control system; do NOT accept or prompt on “robot”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The computer “Mother” features in this 1979 Ridley Scott film, whose title creature quickly grows in size after gaining access to the Nostromo by latching onto Kane’s face.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In Alien, Ash is one of these characters, a robot designed to look human. The replicants in Blade Runner are based on characters of this type in a Philip K. Dick novel whose title asks whether they “Dream of Electric Sheep.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: A Charles Mingus track varyingly titled “Fables of” this politician lambasts him as “sick” and “ridiculous” for not permitting integrated schools. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Arkansas governor who refused to allow the Little Rock Nine to enter Little Rock Central High School until Dwight Eisenhower sent the 101st Airborne Division to force integration.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Faubus’s decision to keep Arkansas public schools segregated violated the Supreme Court’s ruling in this case, which held that segregated public schools violated the Equal Protection Clause.
parts.answer: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Equal Protection Clause is part of this constitutional amendment, one of the three passed during Reconstruction. This amendment was invoked in the case Lochner v. New York.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These functions are formally defined as a bijection from a set to itself. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these functions that rearrange the elements of a set. The number of these functions for a set of n distinct elements is given by n! (“n factorial”).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] A permutation is called a derangement if it does not have any of these points. These points are elements that are mapped to themselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The limit of the ratio of the number of derangements of a set of size n to the number of permutations as n approaches infinity is one over this number. This irrational number is the base of the natural logarithm.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about sports in postmodern American literature:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The death-obsessed Gary Harkness plays this sport in Don DeLillo’s novel End Zone. DeLillo also wrote The Silence, in which a global blackout prevents five friends from watching this sport’s 56th Super Bowl.
parts.answer: American football [or gridiron; do NOT accept or prompt on “association football”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This author recounted his experience as a “near-great” youth player of tennis in his essay “Derivative Sport in Tornado Alley.” In a novel by this author, James and Avril Incandenza run the Enfield Tennis Academy.
parts.answer: David Foster Wallace (The novel is Infinite Jest.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The narrator recalls the athletic prowess of Swede Levov at the opening of this author’s novel American Pastoral. Alexander Portnoy reminisces on his time as a “center fielder for the Seabees” in this author’s Portnoy’s Complaint.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When this deity vows to kill a thousand people every day, her husband says that he will create fifteen-hundred more in response. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this goddess who marries her twin brother in a ceremony where they both circle a pillar in opposite directions. Later, this goddess dies after giving birth to Kagutsuchi, the god of fire.
parts.answer: Izanami [do NOT accept or prompt on “Izanagi”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] After the death of Izanami, many of these deities are created from the tears of her husband Izanagi. Izanami and Izanagi themselves are examples of these Shinto spirits, as are their children Amaterasu, Tsukoyomi, and Susano’o.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] To retrieve his dead wife, Izanagi journeys to Yomi, which is the Japanese version of this place. Because Izanami has already eaten food cooked in this place similar to hell, she is unable to return to the land of the living.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One album from this country consists of two sets of four untitled songs with a 36-second gap of silence in between, and features the characteristic bowed guitar and falsetto vocals of its singer, Jónsi (“yawn-see”) For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, where bands like Hjaltalín and GusGus were founded in the capital city of Reykjavík.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Jónsi released that album, whose title is just a pair of parentheses, with this Icelandic post-rock band. All the vocals for that album were sung in an invented language called “Hopelandic,” which this band has also used for songs like “Mílanó” and “Hoppípolla.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This other Icelandic artist sang with alt-rock band The Sugarcubes until their 1992 breakup. She collaborated with director Michel Gondry on surrealist music videos for her songs “Human Behavior” and “Army of Me.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The title character of this play believes that he willed his house to burn down by staring at a crack in the chimney, since the troll within him has power over the devils of the world. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this play. At the end of this play, Halvard Solness climbs to the top of a roof at the urging of Hilda, but he falls off and dies.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This playwright wrote about Solness in The Master Builder. In another play by this author, the sound of a door shutting is heard offstage as the title character leaves her husband, Torvald.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Henrik Ibsen was from this country. Knut Hamsun’s Hunger follows a man who “wandered about and starved” in this country’s capital Christiania, which is now called Oslo.
parts.answer: Norway [or Kingdom of Norway or Kongeriket Norge]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about hydrocarbons in microbiology:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Members of this domain of life produce the simplest hydrocarbon, methane, in marshes and in the guts of herbivores. Analysis of the 16s rRNA gene led Carl Woese to differentiate this domain from Bacteria.
parts.answer: Archaea [or archaeon or archaeans; accept Archaebacteria]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This phylum of bacteria employs the hydrocarbon pentadecane to help stabilize their thylakoid membranes. Chains of these bacteria contain specialized heterocysts, which are the most abundant nitrogen fixers in the ocean.
parts.answer: Cyanobacteria [or cyanobacterium or blue-green algae or Cyanophyta]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Some bacteria feed on the hydrocarbons that comprise this liquid, released from underwater “seeps.” A 2010 spill of this liquid from Deepwater Horizon destroyed ecosystems in the Gulf of Mexico.
parts.answer: crude oil [or petroleum; accept oil seeps or oil spill]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One member of this art movement, Gustave Caillebotte, depicted people and a dog walking on a bridge in Le Pont de l’Europe. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this art movement that was characterized by thick brushstrokes and capturing proper lighting, often done by painting outside, or en plein air. Claude Monet’s Water Lilies series is from this movement.
parts.answer: impressionism [accept word forms like impressionist; accept Impression, Sunrise]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This impressionist artist painted Parisian couples enjoying festivities at an outdoor dance hall in Bal du moulin de la Galette. One figure in this artist’s Luncheon of the Boating Party is modeled after Caillebotte.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other impressionist artist painted a woman with a parasol sitting on a stone wall in Harbor at Lorient. This sister-in-law of Edouart Manet also painted a woman watching her sleeping daughter in The Cradle.
parts.answer: Berthe Morisot [or Berthe Marie Pauline Morisot]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Shah Alam II granted this organization Diwani rights in the Treaty of Allahabad, meaning that it could collect land taxes and administer courts. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this organization which won those rights after defeating Mir Qasim at the Battle of Buxar. Earlier, this organization won the Battle of Plassey under the leadership of Robert Clive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shah Alam II was the monarch of this empire, which ruled much of India until it was conquered by the British. Babur founded this empire, whose ruler Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This earlier Mughal emperor fought the East India Company in Child’s War, forcing the company to pay a massive fine. This emperor came to power after defeating his elder brother Dara Shikoh at the Battle of Samugarh.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This story opens by describing signs which show that winter is imminent, such as women who want new warm coats being extra nice to their husbands. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this story in which the homeless man Soapy repeatedly fails to get sent to jail in Blackwell’s Island for the winter, decides to reform himself, but then is quickly arrested for loitering.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] “The Cop and the Anthem” is one of the stories about New Yorkers in this author’s collection The Four Million. Another story by this author opens with a character crying on Christmas Eve after repeatedly counting her $1.87.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In this story from The Four Million, Della sells her hair in order to buy a watch chain for her husband Jim, only to find that Jim has sold his watch to buy combs for her hair.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about price discrimination, in which firms charge different amounts to different customers for equivalent products:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The Robinson-Patman Act forbids price discrimination if it hinders this phenomenon. Markets characterized by the “perfect” form of this phenomenon can’t engage in price discrimination because individual firms have zero market power.
parts.answer: competition [accept word forms like competitive; accept perfect competition]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Firms in this market structure can practice first degree price discrimation, capturing the entirety of the consumer surplus. Antitrust laws like Robinson-Patman aim to prevent these anticompetitive market structures, in which there’s only one firm.
parts.answer: monopoly [accept word forms like monopolize; do NOT accept or prompt on “monopolistic competition”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A monopoly practicing first degree price discrimination would theoretically be able to eliminate this quantity. This term refers to the economic inefficiency resulting from production below the socially optimal level of output.
parts.answer: deadweight loss [or excess burden; accept DWL]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A group called EOKA fought for the end of British rule of this country and unification with another country as part of the policy of enosis. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this country, whose first president was overthrown by hardline supporters of enosis. That overthrow of this country’s president precipitated an invasion that resulted in the creation of the Green Line in this country.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This country carried out the aforementioned invasion of Cyprus because this country did not want to see Cyprus join Greece. This country’s capital was moved to Ankara from Istanbul by its first president Mustafa Kemal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] A failed plan to solve the Cyprus dispute was put forward by Kofi Annan, a holder of this position. An earlier holder of this position from Sweden, Dag Hammarskjöld, was killed in a 1961 plane crash in modern-day Zambia.
parts.answer: Secretary-General of the United Nations [or Secretary-General of the UN; prompt on Secretary-General; do NOT accept or prompt on “General-Secretary”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about best practices to use when coding, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] These constructs are human-readable text and annotations used to document code. Lines used for these constructs might be denoted with a hash mark in Python or two slashes in Java.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] When working with other programmers, you might use this version control system to manage changes. In this system, “commits” are revisions which can be “pushed” or “pulled” to a “Hub” website named for this system.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] It’s good practice to test code using both integration tests, which test the system as a whole, and this kind of test, which is for individual classes or methods. A Java framework for this kind of test is named “J”- this kind of test.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These people often hunted with a throwing weapon made of weights attached to leather cords called a bola. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these people, whose payada ballads influenced the epic poem Martín Fierro. These cowboys roamed the plains of Argentina and Uruguay in the 18th and 19th centuries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Many gauchos carried a long one of these tools called a facón, which they also used for fighting. The Swiss Army type of these tools combines one of them with other things like a screwdriver and a can-opener.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Most Argentine gauchos lived in the Pampas or in this region, which stretches from the Colorado River to Tierra del Fuego. The Tehuelche people are indigenous to this region in the south of Argentina and Chile.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of a group named for a “Menace” described by this adjective wrote the manifesto “The Woman-Identified Woman” and included Ellen Shumsky and Rita Mae Brown. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this adjective. Thousands of LGBT government workers, particularly at the State Department, were forcibly outed and lost their jobs in an event named for this adjective.
parts.answer: lavender [accept Lavender Menace or Lavender Scare]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This president prompted the Lavender Scare, a mass firing of LGBT government workers, by signing Executive Order 10450. This president also began construction on the Interstate Highway System.
parts.answer: Dwight D. Eisenhower [or Dwight David Eisenhower; prompt on Ike]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The color lavender became slang for homosexuality after Carl Sandburg wrote that one of this president’s male friendships had a “streak of lavender.” This president issued the Emancipation Proclamation during the Civil War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem titled for this form, George Oppen described “small nouns / Crying faith” in a “forest” where “wild deer / Startle, and stare out.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this form of sacred poetry. A book of the Old Testament titled for this form includes a poem that states, “the Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
parts.answer: psalm [accept the Book of Psalms; prompt on hymn]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] A young man exclaims, “Life is real! Life is earnest! / And the grave is not its goal” in this poet’s “A Psalm of Life.” A woman “thought of Christ, who stilled the wave / On the lake of Galilee” in this poet’s “The Wreck of the Hesperus.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This poem’s repeated reference to a “valley of death” originates from a line in Psalm 23, which describes “the valley of the shadow of death.” This poem describes a journey “into the jaws of Death, / into the mouth of hell.”
parts.answer: “The Charge of the Light Brigade” (by Alfred, Lord Tennyson)

parts.label: L
parts.question: These processes are used in MCMC methods, which can model random walks. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these stochastic processes in which the probability of an event depends only on the previous state. These processes can be modeled as a directed-edge graph where the nodes are possible states.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Markov chains can be modeled by the “transition” type of these constructs. These rectangular arrays of numbers are invertible if their determinant is non-zero.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] While modeling Markov chains, transition matrices are applied repeatedly using this operation. This operation can only be performed on two matrices when the number of columns of the first matrix is the same as the number of rows of the second matrix.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A running internet gag revolves around people telling someone that they look like this athlete, without realizing that they are in fact talking to this athlete. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this athlete nicknamed “Birdman.” This athlete was the first to land the 900, a two-and-a-half-revolution aerial spin performed on a ramp.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tony Hawk is an athlete in this sport, which often features obstacles like handrails and ramps and comes in park and street styles. Yuto Horigome won a gold medal in this sport at the 2020 Summer Olympics.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This skateboarder was favored to win men’s street at the 2020 Olympics, but finished 7th after failing to land 4 tricks in a row. This American skateboarder has won 10 X Games Street gold medals, the most in X Games history.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This musician featured an extended scat section quoting from Charlie Parker’s “Ornithology” in the version of “How High the Moon” she recorded in Berlin. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this jazz singer. This “First Lady of Song” reworked a nursery rhyme about a “brown and yellow basket” for her song “A Tisket, A Tasket.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] With this other jazz artist, Fitzgerald released three collaboration albums, including a set of excerpts from Porgy and Bess. This jazz trumpeter sang about “trees of green / Red roses too” in “What a Wonderful World.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] At a concert in Berlin, Fitzgerald improvised new lyrics to this song referencing Louis Armstrong because she forgot the original ones. Armstrong’s own 1955 cover of this ballad excerpted from The Threepenny Opera helped establish it as a jazz standard.
parts.answer: “Mack the Knife” [accept “The Ballad of Mack the Knife” or “Die Moritat von Mackie Messer”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the interpretation of Biblical prophecies during the Reformation:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Martin Luther wrote that the “little horn” in this book’s vision of four beasts represented the Pope, who he identified with the Antichrist. This book also describes a giant statue made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] To refute the idea that the Antichrist was the Pope, theologians from this religious order like Francisco Ribera argued that Biblical prophecies would be fulfilled in the distant future. This order was founded by Ignatius of Loyola.
parts.answer: Jesuits [or Society of Jesus or SJ]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another Jesuit theologian, Luis del Alcázar, argued that the Antichrist had arrived far in the past in the person of this Roman emperor. This emperor is said to have fiddled during the Great Fire of Rome, which he blamed on Christians.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Leif Segerstam conducted the Galicia Orchestra in a performance of this symphonic suite in which he and the orchestra shouted during its swashbuckling fourth movement. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this symphonic suite by a Russian composer. Its title character is depicted in a high-pitched triplet violin solo that opens its second movement, “The Kalendar Prince.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Scheherezade exemplifies Rimsky-Korsakov’s mastery of this compositional technique, in which different parts are assigned to different instruments. This term can also mean the adaptation of a solo work for an ensemble.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In Rimsky-Korskov’s orchestration of Scheherezade, this instrument accompanies the solo violin in the title character’s leitmotif. This instrument uses pedals to change keys and has 47 vertical strings that are plucked.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the pincer movement, in which separated forces attack the enemy from both flanks at once:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This Chinese general argued against the efficacy of the pincer movement in his treatise The Art of War, which also recommends to “appear weak when you are strong, and strong when you are weak.”
parts.answer: Sun Tzu [or Sunzi; prompt on Sun]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Hannibal Barca executed a pincer during this battle of the Second Punic War, inflicting heavy casualties on the forces of Aemilius Paulus and Terrentius Varro. This battle resulted in the formal adoption of the Fabian strategy.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This ruler executed a successful pincer at the Battle of Hydaspes against the forces Porus. Earlier in his military career, this ruler constructed a causeway during his successful Siege of Tyre.
parts.answer: Alexander the Great [or Alexander III of Macedon; prompt on Alexander]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organ’s eight muscles include ones originating from the styloid process and the hyoid bone. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this papilla-studded muscular organ. An abnormality in the shape of the frenulum that anchors this organ causes ankyloglossia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The tongue and mouth are lubricated by this substance, secreted by the parotid and submandibular glands. This substance is used to wet the mouth and conduct chemicals to taste receptors, and it contains digestive and antimicrobial enzymes such as amylase.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Saliva carries the calcium, fluoride and phosphate ions deposited in this outer layer of the teeth in the process of remineralization. This hard white tissue covering the crowns requires daily repair because of damage from acidic foods and bacteria.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these people is discovered to have transformed into a parrot when the casket is opened at his funeral in Jorge Zalamea’s The Great Burundún-Burundá Has Died. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these despotic leaders described in novels like I, the Supreme and El Señor Presidente. Real-life examples of these leaders include Rafael Trujillo and Fidel Castro.
parts.answer: dictators [accept dictator novels or caudillos or caciques]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] El Señor Presidente is set in this country, the home of its author Miguel Ángel Asturias. Rigoberta Menchú chronicled the genocide of this country’s indigenous population during its civil war in her autobiography, I, Rigoberta Menchú.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] El Señor Presidente was one of the first dictator novels to contain elements of this genre. This genre places fantastical elements within a naturalistic setting, as seen in novels by Juan Rulfo and Isabel Allende.
parts.answer: magical realism [or magic realism or marvellous realism or realismo mágico or realismo maravilloso; do NOT accept or prompt on “realism”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: An aerial bomb that failed to explode helped Bill Blizzard avoid being convicted of treason for his role in this event. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1921 clash between West Virginia coal miners and government authorities over unionization efforts. Nearly 100 people, mostly striking miners, were killed during this week-long conflict.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Another 1921 aerial bombing occurred during a 1921 race massacre in this state, when private individuals and law enforcement officers firebombed people and businesses in the Greenwood district of this state’s city of Tulsa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Battle of Blair Mountain and Tulsa Race Massacre both took place during the tenure of this president. This president promised a “return to normalcy” in his successful campaign over Democrat James M. Cox.
parts.answer: Warren G. Harding [or Warren Gamaliel Harding]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader originally won his country’s presidential election in 2015, representing the Tet Kale party, but allegations of fraud resulted in a re-contested election in 2016, which he also won. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this world leader who was assassinated in his home in July 2021 by Colombian mercenaries posing as US Drug Enforcement Administration agents. This leader’s wife Martine was also seriously wounded in the attack.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Moise was president of this Caribbean island nation. A devastating magnitude 7.2 earthquake that struck this country in August 2021 had an epicenter 100 miles from its capital of Port-au-Prince (“port-ow-PRANZ”).
parts.answer: Haiti [or Republic of Haiti or Republique d’Haiti or Repiblik d Ayiti]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During his tenure, Moise faced protests over misuse of loans obtained from this country through the Petrocaribe oil alliance. The U.S. recognizes Juan Guaidó as this country’s legitimate president.
parts.answer: Venezuela [or Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela or República Bolivariana de Venezuela]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Systems with this property, like the logistic map, may undergo a period-doubling bifurcation where new trajectories emerge from existing ones at increasingly fast rates. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property which occurs when a deterministic system is extremely sensitive to its initial conditions, so its behavior cannot be predicted.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] An example of chaos in physics is one of these systems named for Chua which uses a nonlinear component to initiate period doubling. Norton and Thevenin’s theorems both describe these systems.
parts.answer: circuits [accept electronic oscillators; prompt on oscillators]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Chua’s circuit contains a nonlinear, negative resistor that acts as one of these components. These circuit components allow current to flow in only one direction and have a “light-emitting” type abbreviated LED.
parts.answer: diodes [accept light emitting diodes or LEDs; accept Chua’s diode]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a story by this author, the narrator stares at axolotls in an aquarium every day until suddenly he is one of the axolotls watched by the person he used to be. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Argentinian author of “Axolotl” and “Blow-Up.” The reader is advised to start at Chapter 73 and then jump around in a prescribed order in the “Table of Instructions” of this author’s novel Hopscotch.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Much of Hopscotch uses this literary technique, which may ignore grammatical conventions to depict the thoughts of a character as a constant interior monologue.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] “Axolotl” and part of Hopscotch are both set in this city, where Cortázar is buried in the Montparnasse Cemetery. A poem by César Vallejo begins, “I will die in [this capital of France] with a rainstorm.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This essay defines the absurd as “sin without God” and rejects Kierkegaardian leaps of faith as “philosophical suicide.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1942 essay that examines man’s place in a meaningless universe. It ends by claiming that “One must imagine [the title figure] happy.”
parts.answer: The Myth of Sisyphus [or Le Mythe de Sisyphe]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The author of The Myth of Sisyphus, Albert Camus, is often considered a member of this philosophical movement. Another member of this movement, Jean-Paul Sartre, stated that this movement “is a humanism.”
parts.answer: existentialism [accept word forms like existentialist or existential]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Unlike the Christian existentialist Søren Kierkegaard, both Sartre and Camus ascribed to this philosophical and theological position, which holds that there is no God.
parts.answer: atheism [accept word forms like atheist; do NOT accept or prompt on agnosticism]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Art collectors often invest enormous amounts of money in works which seem to have little or no intrinsic value. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Recently, investors have spent millions buying these things, which use blockchain technology to represent a piece of digital art. Although these things cannot be copied, the digital files they represent can easily be copied and shared.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In 2019, a collector spent over thirty-thousand pounds on this artist’s work Morons, which contains text mocking the collectors who buy his artwork. This artist destroyed one of his artworks at an auction with a shredder hidden in its frame.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Also in 2019, collectors spent $120,000 each on two copies of Maurizio Cattelan’s Comedian, which is just one of these curved, yellow fruits duct taped to a wall.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character, who thinks of himself as “standing alone on the last barrier of civilization,” rants about how people have started to ignore “family institutions” before declaring his opposition to interracial marriage. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character. In an earlier scene, this character claims that civilization is “going to pieces” as he describes reading the book The Rise of the Coloured Empires.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tom Buchanan and his wife Daisy appear in this novel set during the Jazz Age. The title character longs after a “green light” he sees on Daisy’s dock in this novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During an encounter on Fifth Avenue, this character confronts Tom about the murder of Jay Gatsby. This character, the novel’s narrator, ultimately returns to the Midwest after growing disillusioned with New York.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1855, army generals intentionally flooded this waterway to quell an ongoing rebellion. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this longest constructed waterway in the world. The Golden Dragon Great King river god was promoted by the state to build support for the construction of this waterway.
parts.answer: Grand Canal [or Jing-Hang Grand Canal or Dà Yùnhé or Ta Yün-ho or Jing-Hang Yunhe or Capital–Hangzhou Grand Canal]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Grand Canal was long made unusable due to the flooding and a course change in this major river connected to it. This river in north China empties into the Bohai Sea in Shandong Province.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Today, the Grand Canal runs from Hangzhou to this capital of China. This city is home to Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The failure of this plan wreaked havoc on the Scottish economy because about 20 percent of all the money circulating in Scotland was dedicated to backing it. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this scheme that sought to establish a Scottish settlement in modern-day Panama. The failure of this scheme and the resulting bankruptcy of the Scottish government led them to accept the Act of Union with England.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This dynasty’s final ruler, Queen Anne, became the monarch of a united Great Britain with the Act of Union in 1707. James I was the first king of England from this dynasty that followed the Tudors.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Act of Union gave rise to the Scottish branch of this 18th-century intellectual movement which emphasized rational thought. Adam Smith and David Hume were part of the Scottish branch of this movement.
parts.answer: the Enlightenment [or the Age of Enlightenment or the Age of Reason; accept the Scottish Enlightenment]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points, answer the following about the Mohs scale:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The Mohs scale measures this quantity from 1 to 10 based on which minerals can scratch each other. Diamond, which represents 10, has one of the highest known values of this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A 1 on the Mohs scale corresponds to this mineral made of hydrated magnesium silicate. This soft, white, clay mineral is ground to produce baby powder.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A group of minerals known by this name represent a 5 on the Mohs scale and are made of calcium phosphate. A mineral of this name prefixed “hydroxy-” (“hye-DROCK-see”) is the main component of human bones.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The speed of these waves equals the square root of the ratio between the medium’s modulus of rigidity and its density. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these transverse waves whose “shadow zone” results from their inability to pass through liquid.
parts.answer: S waves [or secondary waves or shear waves; prompt on seismic waves or body waves; do NOT accept or prompt on “surface waves”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The S-wave shadow zone reveals the liquid nature of this layer of the Earth. According to dynamo theory, Earth’s magnetic field results from the motion of this layer below the mantle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The difference in arrival time between S waves and P waves allows seismologists to triangulate this location, the point on Earth’s surface that lies directly above where an earthquake originates.
parts.answer: epicenter [or epicentre or epicentrum; do NOT accept or prompt on “focus” or “hypocenter”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, a group of characters “with their tongues cocked and loaded, the only real weapon left to weak folks,” is described as swaying like palm trees. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this novel whose protagonist marries twice before finding love with the much younger Tea Cake. This novel is framed as a conversation between Janie Crawford and her friend Pheoby in the town of Eatonville.
parts.answer: Their Eyes Were Watching God (by Zora Neale Hurston)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Janie shoots Tea Cake after he is injured by one of these animals during a flood. In To Kill a Mockingbird, Atticus Finch shoots one of these animals named Tim Johnson in the street.
parts.answer: a rabid dog [accept descriptions of a dog with rabies; prompt on dog by asking “with what condition?”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] During one of these events after Tea Cake’s death, the prosecutor Mr. Prescott tells Sop-de-Bottom to “shut your mouth up.” Atticus Finch fails to convince the jury to acquit Tom Robinson during one of these events.
parts.answer: trials [accept court cases; accept specific kinds of trials like murder trials or rape trials]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician conceded the nomination but stood by his call for a national health insurance policy in his “Dream Shall Never Die” speech at the 1980 Democratic National Convention. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Massachusetts senator who lost to Jimmy Carter in the 1980 Democratic primary. Mary Jo Kopechne died in a car accident while this politician was driving in a scandal called the Chappaquiddick Incident.
parts.answer: Ted Kennedy [or Edward Moore Kennedy; prompt on Kennedy]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Due to the Chappaquiddick incident, Ted Kennedy declined an offer to be this candidate’s running mate. This politician was soundly defeated by Richard Nixon in the 1972 presidential election.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Ted Kennedy’s campaign against Carter struggled to gain attention from the media because of heavy coverage of a hostage crisis in this country. Ayatollah Khomeini overthrew this country’s Shah in its 1979 Islamic Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The “New” way of this dance style includes sharper movements and tutting, while the “Old” way emphasizes fluid movement. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this style in which dancers strike poses in imitation of a photoshoot. This style was featured in a Madonna song of the same name, in which she tells the listener to “strike a pose” and “let your body move to the music.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Voguing originated from the ballroom scene of this neighborhood. During the swing era, tap dancers like Bill “Bojangles” Robinson performed in this neighborhood’s Apollo Theater.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Vogue battles are often featured at competitions of this performance art. “Queens” of this art form often use elaborate costumes and makeup to perform femininity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Striking sandstone formations like the Kissing Camels and the Cathedral Spires are in this city’s Garden of the Gods park, which may have been named by Helen Hunt Jackson. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this city. The two US Olympic Training Centers are in New York’s Lake Placid and this city, which also contains the headquarters of the US Olympic Committee and USA Swimming.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This tallest mountain in the southern Front Range is just west of Colorado Springs. Colorado Gold Rush participants used the slogan “[this mountain] or bust,” despite no gold having been found near this mountain.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Colorado Springs is the second-most populous city in Colorado, after this city. This “Mile High City”, which is about 70 miles north of Colorado Springs, is Colorado’s capital.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the molecular vehicles called nanocars:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] James Tour’s original nanocar had “wheels” made of this molecule with formula C60 (“C-sixty”). Kroto et al. discovered this molecule in soot left over from vaporized graphite.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Nanocars are powered by electric currents from a type of “scanning microscope” named for this quantum phenomenon, in which a particle travels through a classically forbidden potential energy barrier.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Nanocars travel fastest on surfaces made of this precious transition metal. This yellow metal symbolized Au is found directly below silver on the periodic table.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Soumay Tcheng was the only female delegate at this event. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this conference at which Tcheng and her fellow delegates unsuccessfully sought to regain the city of Qingdao (“CHING-dao”) for China. China joined the League of Nations when it was established after this event.
parts.answer: Paris Peace Conference [or Versailles Conference or Conference of Versailles]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Paris Peace Conference ended this war, during which Japan captured Qingdao from the German Empire. During this war, Chinese labor battalions assisted the Allies in the trenches of the Western Front.
parts.answer: World War I [or First World War or Great War]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Anger over unsatisfactory outcomes for China at the peace talks led to the birth of this student-led protest movement. China refused to sign the Treaty of Versailles due to the influence of this movement, which is named for the date on which protests started.
parts.answer: May 4th movement [or New Culture Movement or Wusi]

parts.label: L
parts.question: After his wife accuses him of not caring about her nerves, this character responds, “They are my old friends. I have heard you mention them with consideration these last twenty years at least.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character. After his wife threatens to disown their daughter if she doesn’t marry the pompous clergyman who proposed to her, this character quips that he would disown her if she does marry him.
parts.answer: Mr. Bennet [or Elizabeth’s father or any answer indicating the male parent of the Bennet family; prompt on Bennet]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In addition to rejecting Mr. Collins’ proposal, Elizabeth Bennet also rejects this character’s first proposal, though she accepts his second proposal at the novel’s end. In their first interaction, this character describes Elizabeth as “tolerable; but not handsome enough to tempt me.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Elizabeth Bennet agrees to marry Mr. Darcy at the end of this novel by Jane Austen.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about monetary policy:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This organization uses monetary policy, like open market operations and the discount rate, to control the U.S. economy. The current chair of this organization is Jerome Powell.
parts.answer: Federal Reserve [or the Fed; accept Federal Reserve System or Federal Reserve Bank]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This term refers to monetary policy aimed at increasing aggregate demand. To combat a recessionary gap, the Fed may use this type of monetary policy, such as by buying bonds or lowering the reserve ratio.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Expansionary monetary policy results in a decrease in these rates, increasing propensity to consume and decreasing propensity to save. These rates determine the amount of additional payment a borrower owes to a lender.
parts.answer: interest rates [accept nominal interest rates or real interest rates]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The general Siyaj K’ak’ overthrew the king of this city in 378 CE and replaced him with a ruler from Teotihuacan. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Mayan city in modern-day Guatemala that was home to the Lost World complex. This city fought a series of wars with the rival city of Calakmul.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tikal’s Lost World Complex was centered on one of these structures. Teotihuacan was home to two of these structures named for the Sun and Moon, and the ancient Egyptians built a “Great” one of these structures at Giza.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Mayans also constructed a pyramid named El Castillo, or the Temple of Kukulcán, in this city. This city in the Yucatán peninsula also contained the Great Ball Court.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Victor Vasarely is considered the leader of an art movement that focused on creating these things, which he used in works such as Zebra. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
