parts.question: Lord Kelvin invented an early device employed in this discipline that used a piano wire with a lead weight attached. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this field of study which measures the depth of oceans or lakes at different points to produce a terrain map of the seabed or lake bed.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Bathymetry often uses multibeam echosounders, a type of this technology, to map the seabed. This technology measures distance based on the reflection of sound waves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another method used in bathymetry is lidar (“LYE-dar”), which reflects the beams produced by these devices off the seafloor. These devices emit light via stimulated emission and can be found in pointers for presentations.
parts.answer: lasers [accept laser beams or light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about process art, in which the method by which art is created is just as important as the final product:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Process art is often thought of to have originated from this other art movement. Helen Frankenthaler was a member of this movement, as was another artist of “drip paintings” like Lavender Mist.
parts.answer: abstract expressionism [prompt on AbEx; prompt on action painting or color field by asking, “What broader movement was that a part of?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Critics consider this American artist of Equal-Parallel as part of the process art movement. This artist’s installation Tilted Arc was removed from public view after critics derided the sculpture as awkward and ugly.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] One work by process artist Robert Morris titled Untitled (Corner Piece) entirely consists of one of these shapes in the corner of a room. These shapes have three sides.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Duke of Schomberg was killed while crossing this battle’s namesake river, despite advising against the crossing. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1690 battle at which forces loyal to William III defeated those of James II during the Williamite War. This battle is commemorated by a holiday known as the Twelfth.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Williamite War began after this 1688 event that resulted in the passage of the English Bill of Rights. A letter from the “Immortal Seven” sparked this event in which William and Mary took the English throne.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Battle of the Boyne took place on this island, whose Catholic majority had much of its land confiscated by the Protestant English government. This island was later the site of a great potato famine under British rule.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An essay by W. V. O. Quine criticizes “two dogmas” of this position, including a form of reductionism derived from verification theory. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this epistemological position held by John Locke and David Hume. This position claims that all or almost all knowledge comes from sensory experience.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The other dogma attacked in Quine’s essay is the distinction between analytic truths and truths of this type. Immanuel Kant defined a priori propositions as being of this type if they were not derived from pure reason.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In his attack, Quine argued that any explanation of analyticity requires an explanation of this property, which in turn requires an explanation of analyticity. Two words are said to have this property if they have the same meaning.
parts.answer: synonymy [or word forms like synonym or synonymous]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The speaker asks, “Was Christ Himself not nailed to a tree?” at the end of a poem about one of these events by Angelina Weld Grimké. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these events. Another poem about these events describes the “scent of magnolias, sweet and fresh” and is titled “Strange Fruit.”
parts.answer: lynchings [accept hangings; prompt on murder or killing]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This poet described “little lads” who “danced round the dreadful thing in fiendish glee” in his poem “The Lynching.” This poet, who was born in Jamaica, pleaded, “If we must die, let it not be like hogs” in his poem “If We Must Die.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Angelina Weld Grimké and Claude McKay both became prominent during this 1920s movement, which saw an explosion of African-American art and literature. This movement is named for a neighborhood in New York.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about colonial explorers who met violent ends:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This Spanish explorer was put on trial and beheaded in Panama by a rival colonial administrator. Earlier, he was the first European to cross the Isthmus of Panama and lay eyes on the eastern shore of the Pacific Ocean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The conquistador Francisco Pizarro, who conquered this empire, was killed in a violent attack orchestrated by Diego de Almagro II. Pizarro himself had this Andean empire’s ruler Atahualpa executed in 1533.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Pedro de Valdivia, the first royal governor of Chile, was killed by these indigenous people. Conflicts between Chile and this indigenous people of the Araucanía region over logging and water use are still ongoing.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this artist who painted The Disrobing of Christ. This mannerist artist depicted the Alcázar Citadel on the right as a storm gathers in the background in his View of Toledo.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] El Greco was one of many artists to depict this woman’s assumption into heaven. El Greco also depicted the archangel Gabriel appearing to this mother of Jesus in his Annunciation.
parts.answer: Virgin Mary [or Madonna, or the Virgin; accept The Assumption of the Virgin or The Assumption of Mary]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This painting by El Greco shows St. John raising his hands towards heaven to the left of the canvas while angels cover naked figures in robes in the background. Picasso studied this painting while creating Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.
parts.answer: The Opening of the Fifth Seal [or The Fifth Seal of Apocalypse or The Vision of Saint John or Profane Love; do NOT accept or prompt on “Sacred and Profane Love,” which is by Titian]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Lin-Shu density wave theory:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Density wave theory offers a solution to the winding problem of these structures, explaining how they maintain their shape without being distorted by differential rotation.
parts.answer: spiral galaxies [or spiral galaxy; accept spiral arms; prompt on galaxies or galaxy]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Under density wave theory, spiral arms are quasi-static – meaning the Solar System will one day leave its current place in this galaxy’s Orion-Cygnus arm.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Density wave theory can also model these galactic features. Spiral galaxies with these features, like the Milky Way, lie on the lower branch of the Hubble tuning fork and are denoted “SB.”
parts.answer: bars [accept barred spirals or barred spiral galaxies]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A poem about one of these events begins by addressing “God! giver of breath and bread.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these events. A poem about one of these events, “The Convergence of the Twain,” describes “The Immanent Will that stirs and urges everything” and has the epigraph, “Lines on the loss of the ‘Titanic.’”
parts.answer: shipwrecks [or wrecks; accept synonyms like a ship sinking; accept “The Wreck of the Deutschland”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] “The Convergence of the Twain” was written by this poet. This author borrowed a line from Thomas Gray’s “Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard” for the title of his novel Far From the Madding Crowd.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This poet wrote of a shipwreck in “The Wreck of the Deutschland,” which was dedicated to five Franciscan nuns. This Catholic priest pioneered sprung rhythm and wrote highly alliterative verse, describing the “morning morning’s minion” and “dapple-dawn-drawn Falcon” in “The Windhover.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: An exhortation by this thinker condemns consumerism as in opposition to “integral ecology” in its section “An Ecological Dream.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this thinker who blamed pollution and climate change on a “throwaway culture” in his encyclical Laudato si’. The title of that encyclical comes from the Canticle of the Sun, which was written by this thinker’s namesake.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Francis reprised the themes of Laudato si’ in his exhortation following a Synod for this region, which proposed a definition of “ecological sin.” Many illegal fires in this region have been set by cattle ranchers.
parts.answer: the Amazon [or the Pan-Amazon Region or Amazonia or Pan-Amazonia or the Amazon rainforest]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] One of the benchmarks in the Laudato Si’Action Platform released in 2021 is divestment from this category of fuels formed by dead ancient plant matter. Oil, gas, and coal are in this category of fuel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lithium niobate is a crystal employed in circuits that use these particles instead of electrons. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these massless particles that carry the electromagnetic force. These particles are the quanta of light.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The high error rate of the photonic circuits used in these devices has led critics to claim that these devices cannot attain “supremacy.” These devices use bits that are capable of superimposing into more than two states.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Photonic circuits are used to implement a quantum computation model that “samples” from particles of this type. These particles are not affected by the exclusion principle and can thus exist in the same quantum state.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Catholic Church partially explains this doctrine with the concept of transubstantiation, while the Orthodox Church leaves it unexplained. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this doctrine, which holds that the bread and wine of the Eucharist actually become the body and blood of Christ. Many Protestant denominations reject this doctrine, holding that the transformation is merely symbolic.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Christians believe that the Eucharist is a reenactment of this event, in which Christ shared a meal with his apostles before he died. This event is depicted in a painting by Leonardo da Vinci.
parts.answer: Last Supper [or Lord’s Supper or Mystical Supper or Secret Supper; prompt on Supper]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] At the Marburg Colloquy, Martin Luther defended the real presence in a debate with this reformer, who denied it. This Swiss reformer invoked the doctrine of sola scriptura to defend a man who ate a sausage during Lent.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2021 paper in the American Political Science Review by Alrababa’h, et al. claims that Mohamed Salah’s arrival to a Premier League club in this city was followed by reduced hate crime and Islamophobia. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Merseyside city. Fans in this city created a chant calling Salah “a gift from Allah,” but that club’s fans are better known for their heartful renditions of the song “You’ll Never Walk Alone.”
parts.answer: Liverpool [accept Liverpool F.C. or Liverpool Football Club]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This American basketball player is a partial owner of Liverpool F.C. This small forward played in eight consecutive NBA Finals, split between the Heat and the Cavaliers, before moving to the Lakers in 2018.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Liverpool was one of the twelve clubs across Europe that announced this would-be breakaway league and would have become permanent members of it. This proposed league soon dissolved after backlash from fans.
parts.answer: European Super League [or The Super League or ESL]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A leader of this country used the term “salami tactics” to describe the method by which the Smallholders’ Party and other enemies were defeated. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this country. Mátyás Rákosi (“MAH-tahsh RAH-koh-shee”) was ousted three months before the beginning of an anti-Soviet revolution which saw Imre Nagy (“Nahj”) rise to power in this country.
parts.answer: Hungary [or Magyarország; accept Hungarian People's Republic or Magyar Népköztársaság]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Rákosi’s position in Hungary faltered after this 1956 address denouncing Joseph Stalin was delivered at the 20th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.
parts.answer: Khrushchev’s Secret Speech [or “On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] After Nagy replaced Rákosi as Prime Minister, Hungary briefly withdrew from the Pact named for this city, the capital of Poland.
parts.answer: Warsaw [or Capital City of Warsaw or Warszawa]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, an aristocrat releases fireflies to illuminate a woman hidden by a curtain, thus entrancing his half-brother. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this 11th-century novel centered on the title “Shining Prince,” who supposedly dies in the blank chapter “Vanished Into the Clouds.” Earlier, this novel’s protagonist marries Lady Aoi, the daughter of the Minister of the Left.
parts.answer: The Tale of Genji [or Genji monogatari]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Tale of Genji describes the Heian-period court life of this country. Jun’ichirō Tanizaki translated The Tale of Genji into the modern form of this country’s language.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Genji kidnaps this ten-year-old girl after falling in love with her. This niece of Lady Fujitsubo eventually dies, leaving Genji grief-stricken.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Choruses sung by soldiers changing guards, street children, and cigarette girls precede this aria, during which the soloist flirts with a crowd of men. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this aria that begins with the soloist singing a chromatically descending melody starting on the note D over a continuous cello ostinato. In this aria, the chorus repeatedly sings “Prends garde à toi” (“prawn gard ah twa”).
parts.answer: Habanera [or “Love is a rebellious bird” or “L’amour est un oiseau rebelle”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Habanera is sung by this opera’s title character before she tosses her flower at Don José. Escamillo (“eh-skah-MEE-yo”) introduces himself in the “Toreador Song” in this opera by Georges Bizet (“bee-ZAY”).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Habanera is adapted in the first moderato movement of the Carmen Fantasy, a work for this instrument by the Spanish virtuoso Pablo de Sarasate. Itzhak (“eets-HAWK”) Perlman and Jascha Heifetz (“YAH-sha HIGH-fits”) also played this instrument.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the evolutionary benefits of honest signalling:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The large, blue and green eye-spotted tail plumage of these male birds demonstrates the handicap principle, since it’s costly to maintain and thus provides an honest signal of fitness to potential mates.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In the green beard effect, genes encoding this behavior also provide honest signals in the form of perceptible physical traits. This term refers to any action an organism takes to increase another’s fitness at the cost of its own.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Organisms with strong defence mechanisms mutually benefit from this process, in which they develop the same aposematic warning patterns in order to honestly signal their danger to predators.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One story by these people sees a straw, a coal, and a bean meet an unfortunate end after the coal burns up the straw and the bean splits itself laughing. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these German brothers who collected many fairy tales in their Children’s and Household Tales. That collection includes the stories of Cinderella and The Little Red Riding Hood.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The title girl of this story is named after a vegetable grown in a witch’s garden that her mother craved while she was pregnant. In this story, a man is blinded after being thrown into a thorn bush from a tower.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In one story, a girl who guards these animals with Conrad chants, “Falada, Falada, thou art dead,” daily. In another story, Simpleton receives a golden one of these animals, whose magical abilities make a princess laugh for the first time.
parts.answer: geese [or goose; accept “The Goose Girl” or “The Golden Goose”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Rumors that delegates at this convention seriously considered the secession of New England have been strongly contested by modern historians. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1814-1815 convention whose delegates called for the passage of several constitutional amendments, such as removing the three-fifths compromise, and opposed the War of 1812.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The attendees of the Hartford Convention were largely New Englanders who belonged to this political party, which lost much of its influence after the convention. This party opposed the ruling Democratic-Republicans.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Hartford Convention also opposed the Embargo Act of 1807, which was signed by this third president. This president’s successor, James Madison, was in office during the proceedings of the Hartford Convention.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This neighborhood’s Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Louis is located near Jackson Square. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this neighborhood south of Tremé. After the nearby red light district, Storyville, was closed in the 1920s, this neighborhood’s Bourbon Street became the center of its city’s nightlife.
parts.answer: the French Quarter [or the Quarter or Vieux Carré]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The French Quarter is part of this Louisiana city on the Mississippi River. The French Quarter was largely spared when this city was devastated by Hurricane Katrina.
parts.answer: New Orleans [or Nola or Nawlins; prompt on the Big Easy]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Another remnant of Louisiana’s French heritage is its division into these regions, the equivalent of counties. In the Catholic Church, a diocese is divided into these regions, which are each presided over by a priest.
parts.answer: parishes [accept civil parish or eccesiastical parish or parish priest]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The main character of this film interrogates an accused witch about Satan, saying, “I want to ask him about God. He, if anyone, must know.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1957 film about the knight Antonius Block’s search for meaning during the Black Plague. In this film, Block is portrayed by Max von Sydow, and he plays a game of chess to extend his life.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Block plays that game of chess against a personification of this thing. The final scene of the film draws on the medieval Danse macabre motif, where the inevitability of this thing is represented by dancing skeletons.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Seventh Seal was directed by this director, who also directed Wild Strawberries. The nurse Alma takes care of the actress Elisabet Vogler after she stops talking in this Swedish director’s film Persona.
parts.answer: Ingmar Bergman [do NOT accept or prompt on “Ingrid Bergman”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Clayton Alderfer extended one of this psychologist’s models by developing the ERG theory. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this humanistic psychologist who posited the “hierarchy of needs” in “A Theory of Human Motivation.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Maslow criticized behaviorism for using this general class of beings as simplified models of human motivation. Psychologists sometimes use members of this biological kingdom, such as monkeys and rats, as test subjects.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Illustrations of Maslow’s hierarchy of needs often split the pyramid into two larger sections, with self-actualization at the top of the upper section and physiological needs at the bottom of the lower section. Give the name of either large section.
parts.answer: growth OR deficiency needs [accept d-needs in place of deficiency]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The use of mass internment in response to this rebellion is discussed in Caroline Elkins’ 2005 book Imperial Reckoning. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this event that saw the Land and Freedom Army fight against British rule under the leadership of Dedan Kimathi and General China. The Kapenguria Six were put on trial for being the purported ringleaders of this event.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Mau Mau uprising took place in this east African country. Many British colonists settled in this country’s capital of Nairobi during the colonial period.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This Ugandan dictator participated in the Mau Mau uprising as an officer in the King’s African Rifles. This dictator was forced out of power after a failed invasion of Tanzania in the Kagera War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: James Baldwin described first appreciating Shakespeare after hearing this character’s lines, “How many ages hence / Shall this our lofty scene be acted over, / In states unborn and accents yet unknown!” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this character. Earlier, this character tells another that “the fault… is not in our stars, / But in ourselves, that we are underlings.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Cassius convinces Brutus to help assassinate the title Roman general in this tragedy by William Shakespeare.
parts.answer: Julius Caesar [or The Tragedy of Julius Caesar]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This character calls Cassius and Brutus traitors in a passage lamenting the stab wounds on Caesar’s corpse. This character commands, “Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears” to begin his oration at Caesar’s funeral.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This search algorithm works by recursing down a tree, choosing to go left or right at each node based on whether that node’s value is greater than or less than the value being searched for. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this search algorithm which is much faster than linear search. In addition to its tree version, this algorithm can also operate on a sorted array by repeatedly splitting the searched area in half.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Appropriately, given its name, binary search only works in trees with at most this many children per node. This is also the number of possible values of a single bit.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Binary search has time complexity big-O of this function of the number of nodes. That’s because binary search operates on one node per tree level, and binary tree height is at most this function of the number of nodes.
parts.answer: logarithm [or base-two logarithm or log or log n or logarithm with any other base; accept big-O log n]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The apocryphal “Acts of” this person contains the earliest known attestation of the tradition that he asked to be crucified upside-down. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this person considered to be the first Pope. The doctrine of papal infallibility holds that the pope cannot err when speaking “from the chair” of this person.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Saint Peter [or Simon Peter; prompt on Simon]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The doctrine of papal infallibility draws on this idea, which holds that the authority of bishops has been passed down continuously from the first followers of Christ. Rome claims special eminence according to this idea, since the church there was founded by Peter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In Catholicism, apostolic succession is transferred during Ordination through the laying on of these body parts. The wounds of Christ include stigmata on his feet and these body parts, which were nailed to the cross.
parts.answer: ANSWER: hands [accept laying on of hands; accept palms or wrists]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this film, Thomasin attempts to milk her family’s nanny goat, but she only produces blood. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 2015 horror film set in 1630s New England. At the end of this film, the billy goat Black Phillip transforms into a man and leads Thomasin to a coven in the forest.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In this film, Heather and Mike believe the screams they hear at night are a trick by the title witch to lure them out of their tent. This 1998 film is framed as footage recovered from three students who disappeared while recording a documentary.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Though films with witches are often horror films, this comedy contains a scene where a woman is proved to be a witch by being weighed against a duck. King Arthur quests for the title object in this Monty Python film.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Monty Python and the Holy Grail

parts.label: L
parts.question: This conflict began after John Sassamon revealed a plot to attack colonial settlements. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this conflict fought by the Narragansett and Wampanoag tribes against the New England Confederation. Over 600 Narragansett warriors were killed in the Great Swamp Fight during this conflict.
parts.answer: ANSWER: King Philip’s War [accept First Indian War or Metacomet’s War or Metacomet’s Rebellion or Pometacomet's Rebellion or Pometacomet's War]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] John Sassamon warned this colony’s governor Josiah Winslow of the plot to attack colonial settlements. Metacomet’s father Massasoit earlier established relations with William Bradford and Myles Standish of this colony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Much of the fighting in King Philip’s war took place in what is now this state, where Native Americans attacked the settlement of Sudbury. Over 50 Native Americans were executed in Boston Common in what is now this state.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At sufficiently low concentrations, the Debye-Hückel equation can be used to calculate this quantity in an electrolyte solution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this quantity which corrects deviations from a liquid solution’s ideal behavior.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] According to Debye-Huckel theory, the activity coefficient is proportional to the square root of the “strength” of these species. These species are prefixed “cat-” or “an-” depending on if their charge is positive or negative.
parts.answer: ANSWER: ions [accept ionic strength or cations or anions]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The formation of ions via electrospray ionization or MALDI occurs in this laboratory technique. Molecules are analyzed based on their mass to charge ratio in this technique.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The main character of this novel learns about the Soul of the World, which is described as “‘the principle that governs all things.’” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel in which Santiago attempts to fulfill his Personal Legend by travelling to the Egyptian pyramids in search of treasure.
parts.answer: ANSWER: The Alchemist [or O Alquimista] (by Paolo Coelho)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In The Alchemist, Santiago learns that the Master Work of alchemy is creating the Elixir of Life and this object, which can turn lead into gold. Nicolas Flamel owns this object in the first Harry Potter novel.
parts.answer: ANSWER: the philosopher’s stone [accept the sorcerer’s stone or Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone or Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] At the beginning of the novel, Santiago works in Spain as one of these people, who are often depicted in pastoral literature. One of these people tells his lover, “Come live with me and be my Love” in a poem about a “passionate” one by Christopher Marlowe.
parts.answer: ANSWER: shepherds [accept “The Passionate Shepherd to His Love”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A red-haired woman curls up into a ball while she is showered by golden rain in this artist’s painting Danae. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this artist who painted two portraits of Adele Bloch-Bauer. This artist used gold leaf throughout a painting of two lovers embracing on a flower-covered cliff.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Klimt was from this country. Joseph Maria Olbrich sculpted the Secession Building to exhibit artworks from this country’s Vienna Secession movement, which was co-founded by Klimt.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Austria [or Republic of Austria or Republik Oesterreich]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In the central section of this Klimt painting, three gorgons stand on the left of Typhoeus, who is shown as a hairy brown monster. This painting was featured at the fourteenth Vienna Secessionist Exhibition to celebrate its title composer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Numbers in this system can also be expressed as a combination of four two-by-two imaginary matrices. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this extension of the complex numbers that introduces the j and k units. Multiplication in this system is noncommutative.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Multiplying the quaternions i, j, and k together gives this number. In the complex number system, i is defined to be a square root of this number.
parts.answer: ANSWER: negative one [or minus one or -1; do NOT accept or prompt on “one”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] William Hamilton allegedly carved the quaternions into one of these physical structures upon conceiving of them on a walk. Leonhard Euler pioneered graph theory with a problem about seven of these structures in Königsberg.
parts.answer: ANSWER: bridges [accept Seven Bridges of Königsberg]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of this author’s books ends with Almitra standing on the sea-wall and remembering the title character’s saying “A little while, a moment of rest upon the wind, and another woman shall bear me.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Lebanese-American author who wrote about Almustafa’s farewell discussions with the citizens of the fictional island Orphalese in The Prophet.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In his final lecture, Almustafa claims that fear of this concept is “but the trembling of the shepherd when he stands before the king.” A poem by Emily Dickinson begins, “Because I could not stop for [this concept].”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Gibran’s The Earth Gods may have been inspired by The Four Zoas, a collection of mythology by this poet. Like Gibran, this poet also worked as a painter, illustrating his own collection Songs of Innocence and Experience.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Karl Jaspers termed the concurrence of major schools of thought in these two countries and China in the first millennium BCE the “Axial Age.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these two modern-day countries. Pyrrho and Aristotle lived in one of these two countries at the same time that Buddhist and Hindu thinkers like Nāgārjuna lived in the other.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Greece AND India [accept answers in either order]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The skeptic Pyrrho of Elis may have adopted his idea of ataraxia after learning about this similar concept from Buddhist ascetics in India. This state of freedom from suffering literally translates to “blowing out.”
parts.answer: ANSWER: nirvana [or nibbana; accept moksha or mukti]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Like Pyrrho, this student of Leucippus likely studied with Buddhist ascetics. This thinker’s determinism was later opposed by Lucretius’ proposal of the swerve.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s namesake empire fought a protracted war with the Adal Sultanate in the mid-16th century. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country in the Horn of Africa where that Christian empire was ruled for 700 years by the Solomonic dynasty. This country’s final ruler, Haile Selassie, ruled from its capital of Addis Ababa until 1974.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Ethiopia [accept Abyssinia or the Ethiopian Empire or the Abyssinian Empire]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ethiopia was nearly defeated by Adal before soldiers from this empire pushed back the invaders. This empire’s naval rivalry with the Ottoman Empire led them to support Ethiopia against the Ottoman-backed Adal Sultanate.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Portugal [or Kingdom of Portugal or Reino de Portugal; accept Portuguese Empire]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The commander of the Portuguese force in Ethiopia, Cristovaõ, was the son of this explorer. This explorer had earlier asked for trade concessions from the Zamorin of Calicut during his first expedition to India.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Mulholland Drive, a man brings his friend to visit Winkie’s Diner because he saw a terrifying thing behind it during one of these events. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these events that may be represented in film through “sequences” that depict a distorted reality. Much of Mulholland Drive takes place during one of these events that ends when the Cowboy says, “time to wake up.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In a film by this director, the screen flashes red throughout a dream sequence in which Jimmy Stewart’s character recalls failing to save Madeleine Elster from jumping out of a tower. That film by this director uses the dolly zoom to represent Scottie Ferguson’s fear of heights.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Alfred Hitchcock (The film is Vertigo.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This director showed a man struggling to get out of a locked car before floating up into the sky in a dream sequence that opens his film 8½ (“eight and a half”). This Italian also directed La Dolce (“DOLE-chay”) Vita.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Martin Luther attacked this friar’s belief that remorse was not necessary for atonement if one bought an indulgence. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Dominican friar who sold indulgences with the slogan, “When the coin in the coffer rings / the soul from purgatory springs.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tetzel claimed that buying an indulgence would offer the buyer remission for these things, reducing the time spent in Purgatory. The Catholic Church recognizes seven “deadly” examples of these things, such as lust and wrath.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The sale of indulgences was eventually banned at this mid-16th century council, although the doctrine of Purgatory was affirmed. This council, convoked by Paul III, is often cited as the start of the Counter-Reformation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Huitzilopochtli:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Huitzilopochtli is the war god of this Mesoamerican people. In this people’s mythology, Tezcatlipoca frequently clashes with the feathered serpent Quetzalcoatl.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Huitzilopochtli is born when this goddess is impregnated with a ball of feathers. This Aztec earth goddess is also the mother of the Centzon Huitznahua, who are the four hundred Southern stars.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Many depictions of Huitzilopochtli either show him as a hummingbird or this other bird. Legendarily, the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan was founded at a spot where one of these birds was holding a snake while sitting on a cactus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The presence of beta-amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles composed of tau protein characterizes this disease. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this neurodegenerative disease. It is the most common cause of dementia in the elderly.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Tau tangles and amyloid plaques can be detected in living patients by tracking the presence of fluoride-18 in the brain using this imaging technique. This technique measures beta-plus decay of tracers to quantify metabolism.
parts.answer: ANSWER: positron emission tomography [or PET scan]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Experimental diet-based therapeutics for Alzheimer’s are based on the link between brain processes and metabolites produced by this community in the GI tract. It is composed of organisms like E. coli and B. fragilis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote, “You were born, you had body, you died. / It is just that you never giggled or planned or cried,” in a poem addressed to all of the unborn children she aborted. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this poet who lamented, “Believe me, I loved you all,” in “the mother.” Another poem by this author describes “two who are Mostly Good” for whom “dinner is a casual affair.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] “the mother” first appeared in Brooks’ collection A Street in Bronzeville, which was inspired by the South Side neighborhood of this city. A Carl Sandburg poem addressed to this Illinois city calls it “Hog Butcher of the World.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Brooks’ poem “We Real Cool” is often cited as an example of this poetic technique. In this technique, a line break is inserted in the middle of a sentence without any punctuation or grammatical pause.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the trial of Gaius Verres, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] In the 70s BCE, Gaius Verres was the Roman governor of this large Mediterranean island at the tip of Italy. Some of his more infamous deeds include pillaging a temple found in this island’s city of Syracuse.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The orator Cicero’s successful prosecution of Verres helped him get elected to this public office. This office, which oversees festivals, games, and public buildings, follows the quaestorship on the cursus honorum.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During the trial, Cicero accused Verres of using the chaos caused by this man’s revolt in order to extort Sicilians. This man’s revolt ended when Crassus defeated him and had the survivors crucified along the Appian way.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Materials with this property are used on the stripes of credit cards because of the “memory” they can retain. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property of materials whose electron spins are aligned, producing a permanent magnetic field.
parts.answer: ANSWER: ferromagnetism [accept word forms like ferromagnetic]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ferromagnetic materials exhibit this phenomenon, where magnetizing the material follows a different path than demagnetizing it. More generally, this phenomenon refers to the dependence of a system on its history.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The SI derived unit for magnetic field strength is named for this Serbian-American inventor who pioneered alternating current during his rivalry with Thomas Edison.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these buildings in Oslo advertises on its website “please walk on the roof” in reference to its large ramp that allows pedestrian access to its roof. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these buildings. Ove Arup helped engineer the concrete ribs that support another one of these buildings designed by Jørn (“yearn”) Utzon.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That aforementioned opera house is adorned with white, sail-like concrete shells and occupies Bennelong Point in this Australian city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This architect designed an opera house in Guangzhou (“gwong-joe”) meant to resemble two pebbles washed up by the Pearl River. This architect’s futuristic design for the 2020 Olympics Stadium was scrapped because it was too expensive.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name these companies trying to “disrupt” the nature of how we consume food, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This company sold its self-driving car division in January 2021, focusing instead on its “Eats” food-delivery service. This company’s ridesharing platform is the most widely-used in the U.S., ahead of competitors like Lyft.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Uber [accept Uber Eats or Uber ATG]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This company founded by Rob Rhinehart creates meal-replacement products supposed to contain all necessary nutrients. This company’s 2.0 products include ready-mixed drinks and bars as well as the original powder mixes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This vegetarian burger uses soy-derived heme as its protein base. Burger King has put out a version of the Whopper based on this meat replacement product.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Impossible Burger [accept Impossible Whopper or Impossible Foods]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, Addie narrates how she did not love her husband nor her children, except for Jewel, who she conceived in an affair with Whitfield. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this novel in which Addie Bundren’s family attempts to honor her request to be buried with her family in Jefferson. Like many of its author’s works, this novel is set in Yoknapatawpha County.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] As I Lay Dying is a novel by this modern American author. This Southerner also wrote “A Rose for Emily” and The Sound and the Fury.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In the novel, this youngest of the Bundren children drills holes in the lid of Addie’s coffin to help her breathe, though he ends up drilling into her face as well. After being asked to clean a dead fish, this character concludes, “My mother is a fish.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This artist used French Orientalist techniques in his The Death of Sardanapalus (SAR-duh-NAH-puhlus). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this artist of the Orientalist panting The Women of Algiers who also created Liberty Leading  the People.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Orientalist painting grew in popularity after Napoleon's invasion of Egypt, which also inspired this  artist's Bonaparte Visiting the Plague Victims of Jaffa (YAH-fah).
parts.answer: Antoine-Jean Gros (ahn-TWAH jawn GROH) [or Jean-Antoine Gros]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Orientalist artist Jean Ingres (jawn AHNG) created a circular painting depicting many nude women  in a bathhouse in this present-day country. Sedefkar Mehmed Agha (sed-ef-KAR mek-MED AH-gah) designed the Blue Mosque here.
parts.answer: Turkey [or Republic of Türkiye; or Turkey Cumhuriyeti]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Belief in these beings is listed second among six articles of faith that also include belief in God's  oneness and prophets. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these creatures made of light. One of them called Jibril revealed the Quran to Muhammad.
parts.answer: angels [or malak; or mala'ik; or mala'ikah; or archangels]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Scholars debate whether the tempters Harut and Marut, mentioned in this surah, are fallen angels.  This longest chapter of the Quran contains the Throne Verse.
parts.answer: surat al-Baqarah [or The Cow; or The Heifer; or surah 2; or the second surah]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Because this Kurdistani ethnic group venerates Melek Tawus (MAY-lek TAO-oos), an angel who  shares traits with Iblis, some Muslims have accused them of “devil worship.”
parts.answer: Yazidis [or Yezidis; or Ezidis; or Yazidism]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Tacitus (TASS-it-us) wrote an ethnography about this region describing such groups as the Ingaevones  (ing-ai-VOH-nays). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this region to the north of the Roman Empire, also inhabited by the Marcomanni (MAR-kohMAH-nee) and Alemanni (AH-lay-MAH-nee). Romans were killed here during a battle in which Arminius  (ar-MIN-ee-us) betrayed Varus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] After this 9 AD battle in Germania, at which Roman forces were destroyed by the Cherusci (chayROO-skee), Augustus supposedly said, “Quintilius (kwin-TIL-ee-us) Varus, give me back my legions!”
parts.answer: Battle of the Teutoburg (TOY-toh-burg) Forest [or Teutoburger Wald]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Germania was often defined as being east of this river in present-day western Germany. A “land”  named for this river included Cologne.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a play by this author, the title character is saved when Trygaeus (trug-AY-us) rides a dung beetle to  heaven. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this author of Peace as well as a play in which Philocleon (fil-AH-KLEE-on) is addicted to  court cases, The Wasps.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In this Aristophanes play, Dionysus and Xanthias (ZAN-thee-us) travel to the underworld to bring  back Euripides (yur-IP-id-eez). The title creatures of this play chant “Brekekekéx-koáx-koáx.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Xanthias has this relationship to Dionysus at the beginning of the play, though the roles later  switch. The Roman playwright Terence was released from this status as an appreciation of his talent.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This program was named for the Secretary of State who proposed it in a 1947 speech at Harvard. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this American aid program that paid to rebuilt countries including West Germany after World  War II.
parts.answer: Marshall Plan [or European Recovery Program; or ERP]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Marshall Plan funds were implemented in West Germany by this Christian Democratic Chancellor,  whose 1949 to 1963 time in office oversaw an “economic miracle.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] West Germany's coal and steel industries were severely restricted for five years after this 1945  Allied conference held outside Berlin, which decided how to administer Germany after World War II.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poem was devoted to Queen Elizabeth I, whom it depicts as Gloriana. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this epic poem by Edmund Spenser. It focuses on the Redcrosse Knight, who fights enemies  such as Sansjoy and Error.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Redcrosse battles Archimago (arch-ee-MAH-goh), an evil character of this type. Another character  with this powerful identity, who assists Vortigern (VOR-tig-urn) and Arthur, is Merlin.
parts.answer: wizard [or sorceror; or mage; or magician; or warlock]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Mary Thomas Crane has argued for a re-evaluation of this poet's importance in Elizabethan  literature. This author of “Doubt of Future Foes” and “On Monsieur's Departure” etched poems into a  prison cell at Woodstock and delivered the “Golden Speech.”
parts.answer: Elizabeth herself [or Queen Elizabeth I; or the Queen; since Elizabeth has already been  mentioned in this question, further specificity is not needed]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This law states that the restoring force is equal to displacement, and its formula has a constant, k,  which measures a spring's stiffness. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this law which defines the force necessary to extend a spring.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Hooke's law describes how the elastic force causes a mass on a spring to oscillate, resulting in this  kind of motion.
parts.answer: simple harmonic motion [prompt on harmonic motion]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Simple harmonic motion is independent of this measure of the maximum distance that is traveled by  a mass on a spring.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The real-life pilot Beverley Bass appears as a character in this musical. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this musical by Irene Sankoff and David Hein based on events in Gander, Newfoundland,  that recounts its premise in the song “38 Planes.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Come From Away had a record-breaking run at this theater in Washington, D.C., which was much  earlier the site of an interrupted showing of Our American Cousin in 1865.
parts.answer: Ford's Theatre [Abraham Lincoln was assassinated during Our American Cousin.]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Come From Away centers on the aftermath of this terrorist attack, which suspended Broadway  performances for two days in 2001.
parts.answer: 9/11 [or September 11th, 2001 terrorist attacks; or attack on or destruction of the World  Trade Center or WTC or Twin Towers]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This is the second central moment of a probability distribution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this statistical measure which is calculated as the average of the squared differences.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This measure of how close a data set is to the set's mean is the square root of the variance.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Under the empirical rule of standard deviation, the percentage of values that are expected to lie  within one standard deviation of the mean is closest to this whole number percentage.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The mouth of this river is located in the town of Napoleon, which was damaged during the Civil  War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this river that flows through Pine Bluff and Fort Smith, as well as a city located at the  foothills of the Ouachita (WASH-it-ah) Mountains.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Arkansas River is a tributary of this longest U.S. river, which flows into the Gulf of Mexico.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Arkansas River also passes through this city that contains Oral Roberts University and the  former Greenwood District, also called Black Wall Street.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This woman and her sister Ethel Byrne created a new facility after visiting the Netherlands. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this woman who opened the first birth control clinic in the U.S. and wrote “What Every Girl  Should Know.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Sanger's American Birth Control League later became this alliteratively named organization that  provides reproductive health care.
parts.answer: Planned Parenthood [Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc.]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Sanger's pamphlet Family Limitation led to prosecution under this 1873 act, which banned the  sending of “obscene” materials in the mail.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For the cover of this character's first appearance, he was portrayed as white rather than his normal  color. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this round, pink creature from Planet Popstar, the hero of early games set in Dream Land.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The latest Kirby adventure is this Switch title. In this game, Kirby gains the ability to swallow and  control real world objects such as stairs and cars.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This rival of Kirby has wings and wields a sword. He names the first Colosseum challenge in Kirby  and the Forgotten Land.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The father of this family is the focus of a 2006 Pulitzer Prize winning novel by Geraldine Brooks.  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this family. A member of this family, Beth, dies after contracting scarlet fever.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy March are the main characters of this novel by Louisa May Alcott.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Little Women frequently alludes to this earlier novel. At a younger age, the children in Little Women pretended that their cellar was the City of Destruction from this novel.
parts.answer: The Pilgrim's Progress [The Pilgrim's Progress from This World, to That Which Is to  Come]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In an opera, this woman enters as a bacchante (buh-KANT-ee) at a party where guests dance the  “Infernal Galop.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this character, the wife of the title hero in the opera Orpheus in the Underworld.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Eurydice returns to earth at the beginning of the third act of Orfeo ed Euridice, an earlier operatic  adaptation of the legend by this German composer, who included “The Dance of the Blessed Spirits” in  his score.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The “Infernal Galop” section from Jacques Offenbach's Orpheus in the Underworld uses this  popular music hall dance in which a female chorus line repeats high kicks.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This mammalian taxon has adapted to fill many ecological niches on the island of Madagascar. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this superfamily of mammals that includes the sifaka (see-FAH-kah) and a “ring-tailed”  species.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Lemurs belong to this large mammalian order that includes tarsiers (TAR-seerz), bush babies, and  humans.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This superfamily contains five families, including the only primates with fully prehensile tails and  such species as the capuchins (KAP-uh-chinz) and spider monkeys.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A poem that includes this character was adapted into a 2021 film directed by David Lowery. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this character who gives a challenge on the New Year seeking to be matched in a “beheading  game” in a Middle English poem.
parts.answer: the Green Knight [or Bertilak de Hautdesert]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Green Knight's opponent, Gawain (guh-WAIN), serves in the court of this king, who ruled from  Camelot and founded the Round Table.
parts.answer: King Arthur [or Arthur Gernow; or Roue Arzhur]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] While resisting the temptations of the Green Knight's disguised wife, Gawain accepts a silk belt  after refusing a glove and one of these objects. In other myths, Perceval and Gareth both become  invulnerable by wearing this kind of object.
parts.answer: magic ring [or golden ring; or red gold ring]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In an analysis of this person's laptop, The Washington Post was unable to verify most of the data as  being authentic. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this son of the current President of the United States.
parts.answer: Hunter Biden [or Robert Hunter Biden; prompt on Biden]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Twitter's blocking of links to news stories about Hunter Biden's laptop was used to criticize this  portion of the Communications Decency Act. This section of the law protects website hosts against  liability for content created by third parties.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hunter Biden's role on this Ukrainian energy company's board was also the subject of controversy  in 2020.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A system of carbonic acid and the bicarbonate ion act as this kind of substance in the blood. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these solutions, consisting of a weak acid and its conjugate base, that resist changes in pH.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This equation states that the pH of a buffer solution is equal to the acid dissociation constant plus  the log of base concentration over acid concentration.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] A buffer containing Tris-HCl (triss hydrochloride) and potassium chloride is generally used in this  technique to create optimal conditions for the activity of Taq polymerase (tak puh-LIM-uh-rayz).

parts.question: A novel written by this author revolves around the search for the outlaw Joaquin Murieta (wah-KEEN  moo-ee-AY-tah). For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name this author of the novel Daughter of Fortune and the sequel Portrait in Sepia, who wrote an  earlier story about the magical Trueba (troo-AY-bah) family.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Allende often writes in the “magical” form of this genre. The original form of this genre was a late  19th-century movement that attempted to depict social issues accurately.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Allende wrote a 2005 novel about this pulp hero, who was introduced in Johnston McCulley's 1919  novel The Curse of Capistrano, set in Spanish colonial southern California.
parts.answer: Zorro [or Don Diego de la Vega]

parts.question: When Trinculo first encounters this character, he is mistaken for a fish, but Trinculo then compares  him to a “dead Indian” that people will pay to see. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name this character who swears to be the “true subject” of Stephano because his “liquor is not  earthly.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Caliban is the slave of Prospero, who uses magic during the title event of this play to crash his  brother Antonio's ship on an island.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Tempest is a comedy by this author of The Taming of the Shrew and A Midsummer Night's  Dream.

parts.question: The historiography of this period was once dominated by the Dunning School. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] W.E.B. DuBois (doo BOYZ) wrote about the “Black” version of what period, in which federal  troops occupied the South after the Civil War?

parts.label: B

parts.label: L
parts.question: This TV competition show is in its fifty-second season on the Food Network. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this cooking competition show on which chefs create dishes from a basket of mystery  ingredients.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This Chopped judge, who repeatedly expresses his hatred for raw onions, is the host of the dessert-themed Chopped spinoff, Chopped Sweets.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Another Chopped judge, Alex Guarnaschelli (GWAR-nuh-SHEL-ee), has competed on two iterations  of this franchise. This franchise's original version featured an elaborate fictional backstory about a  gourmand constructing “Kitchen Stadium.”
parts.answer: Iron Chef [or Iron Chef America; or The Next Iron Chef]

parts.question: In September 2022, a campaign in this oblast (OHB-list) retook Balakliya (bah-lah-KLEE-ah) and  Izium (IZ-ee-oom). For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name this province to the northwest of Donetsk (dahn-YETSK) whose northern portion directly  borders Russia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Following the liberation of Kharkiv, residents whose communications were cut off learned of  events in this Sea of Azov (AY-zawv) coastal city in Donetsk, the most affected by Russian atrocities  thus far. 400,000 people lived in this city at the start of the war, though up to 80,000 have now been  killed and 200,000 more have fled.

parts.answer: Yoko Ono [or Ono Yoko; accept, but do not otherwise reveal, Yoko Ono Lennon]

parts.question: [10] The spires of a church dedicated to St. John are the only remaining visible portion of a town outside  of Uruapan (OO-roo-ah-PAHN) in Michoacán (MEESH-woh-KAHN) state that was engulfed in lava  during the 1943 emergence of this volcano.

parts.question: The Thiel-Sen estimator is a method of fitting a line from sample points by taking the median of  these quantities from all pairs of points. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name this measure of how steep a line is and what direction the line moves in.

parts.question: [10] Thiel-Sen is a “robust” method for performing regression, which is more naively done with a  method named for “least” values of this operation on residuals.

parts.question: [M] Name this form of poetry collected in The Seashell Game. The most famous poem of this type describes a frog  jumping into a pond.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The author of The Seashell Game, Matsuo Basho, also wrote this travelog in a combination of prose and haiku.  This work describes a journey Basho made on foot to the region of Oku.
parts.answer: Narrow Road to the Deep North [accept The Narrow Road to the Interior or Oku no Hosomichi]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The first and last lines of a haiku contain this many syllables. There are this many feet in a line of iambic  pentameter.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about lieder, which are 50% poetry, 50% music, and 100% awesome. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this language used to write Der Erlkönig, a poem used in one lied. Wilhelm Müller wrote in this language.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Wilhelm Müller’s poetry inspired this composer of Der Erlkönig to write the lieder cycles Winterreise and Die  Schone Mullerin. This Austrian composer also composed the “Unfinished” Symphony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Schubert’s lied Die Forelle inspired the nickname “Trout” for a piece for this many players. Modest  Mussorgsky was part of a group of this many nationalist Russian composers, known as “the Mighty Handful.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Zeroth law of these objects, created by Isaac Asimov, states that they “may not harm humanity.” For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these automatons that are said to have “positronic brains,” according to Asimov.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Czech science fiction writer wrote about robots taking over the world in his play R.U.R, which introduced  the word “robot."

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In another play by Čapek titled for the war with these animals, Captain van Toch enslaves a race of these  intelligent amphibians for pearl fishing. These animals demand lebensraum and destroy Earth’s landmass.
parts.answer: newts [or War with the Newts; or Vaika S Mloky; or Salamander Wars]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the motion of pendulums, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This quantity equals the amount of time it takes for the pendulum to return to its original position and complete one full  cycle. Frequency equals one over this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The “simple harmonic” type of this type of motion is exemplified by the motion of pendulums. This term is used to refer  to motion that is periodic.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this process, an external force, such as friction, slows down the oscillation of a pendulum, eventually causing it to stop.  Taipei 101 contains an enormous steel ball that is tuned to the tower’s resonant frequency to perform this process.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The desert planet Arrakis features many “crawlers” used to harvest this hallucinogenic resource. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this incredibly valuable fictional resource, which is used to power ships belonging to House Atreides.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Spice is an incredibly valuable resource in this science fiction movie, based on a Frank Herbert novel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This actor plays Dune’s protagonist, Paul Atreides. In Little Women, Jo’s lover Laurie was played by this actor,  who also starred as Elio in Call Me By Your Name.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After a case involving this tribe, a President apocryphally said “John Marshall has made his decision; now let  him enforce it.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this tribe, whose rights to their land were upheld in Worcester v. Georgia. This tribe was forced to  undergo the Trail of Tears.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This President declined to recognize the decision in Worcester v. Georgia. The Trail of Tears was concluded by  this President’s successor, Martin van Buren.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Andrew Jackson also opposed this tribe’s existence during a war started at the “Negro Fort.” This tribe was led  by Osceola at the Battle of Lake Okeechobee.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Because they are often adapted from light novels, shows in this genre often have long names, such as “That Time I Got Reincarnated As A Slime.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this anime genre involving a protagonist transported from the real world to a fantasy world that became popular in the late 2010s. Its name is Japanese for “different world.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: In the 2013 isekai Sword Art Online, Kirito and other people are transported into the world of one of these general works. Fortnite is one of these works.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the 2016 series Re:Zero, Subaru has the power to do this action every time he dies in the fantasy world. The Doctor from Dr. Who has the power to do this action by traveling in the TARDIS.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The speaker of one poem by this author tells the reader to “hope your road is a long one” in his poem “Ithaka.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this poet, who described the title group as “a kind of solution” in “Waiting for the Barbarians.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Cavafy wrote in the modern form of this language. The ancient form of this language was used by Sophocles to write Oedipus Rex.
parts.answer: Greek [or modern Greek; or ancient Greek]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The modern Greek author Nikos Kazantzakis wrote a 33,333 line “modern sequel” to this ancient Greek work. The protagonist of this work uses the pseudonym “Nobody” to escape the cyclops Polyphemus.
parts.answer: The Odyssey [or The Odyssey: A Modern Sequel]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Much of the information about this group’s attempted conquest of Egypt was derived from inscriptions and reliefs at Medinet Habu. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this confederation of people, whose origin remains mysterious. This group contributed to the fall of empires like the Mycenaeans and Hittites during the Bronze Age Collapse.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Sea Peoples may have allied with a group called “Ahiyyawa” from this country. According to Homer, a confederation from this modern-day country fought Troy in the Trojan War.
parts.answer: Greece [or the Hellenic Republic; or Ellas; or Elliniki Dhimokratia]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Unlike most Mediterranean polities, some Phoenician cities peaked after the Bronze Age collapse, such as this Tunisian city founded by Dido. This city’s army was once run by the Barca family.
parts.answer: Carthage [or Kart-hadasht; or Colonia Julia Carthago; or Karchedon]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The tennis racket theorem can be applied to bodies that have three different values for this quantity. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity, the rotational analogue of mass. Torque equals this quantity times angular acceleration.
parts.answer: moment of inertia [prompt on I; do NOT accept or prompt on “inertia” alone]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The moment of inertia for an object for an axis passing through this point is minimized because of the parallel axis theorem. A flat object can be balanced on your finger if you place your finger at this point for that object.
parts.answer: center of mass [accept center of gravity; prompt on center]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The moment of inertia of this shape equals two-thirds, times mass, times radius squared. This round shape with a radius is the 3-D analogue of a circle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Penny dreadfuls were originally meant to emulate or straight-up plagiarize works in this genre, like The Monk. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this genre, characterized by haunting horror stories often set in castles. This genre was pioneered by Anne Radcliffe’s Mysteries of Udolpho and Horace Walpole’s Castle of Otranto.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The penny dreadful The String of Pearls introduced this character, who gives his victims to Mrs. Lovett to make meat pies. This “demon barber of Fleet Street” titles a Stephen Sondheim musical.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A massive penny dreadful is titled for Varney being one of these creatures. Bram Stoker’s Dracula is one of these blood-sucking creatures.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these animals was bound to Mount Mandar during the churning of the ocean. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these animals, known as nagas. Vishnu is often depicted resting on Shesha, who is the king of these animals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Snakes are the sworn enemy of this mount of Vishnu. This half-eagle is the king of the birds, and is the son of Vinata.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Garuda’s brother Aruna is the charioteer of Surya, the god of this celestial body that provides light on Earth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about liquid-liquid extraction, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Liquid-liquid extraction uses a separatory one of these things. These things consist of a tube that is narrow at the bottom and wide at the top, and are used to guide liquids into a narrow opening.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A common solvent mixture for liquid-liquid extraction is dichloromethane and this other compound, which forms the appropriately-named aqueous phase. This compound is often considered a universal solvent.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In a two-phase liquid-liquid extraction, a third layer can sometimes form due to the two liquids forming this kind of mixture. In this kind of mixture, a liquid disperses into another liquid.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these entities, named after Abraham Lincoln, was sponsored by businessman Carl G. Fisher. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these entities, which were landscaped by Lady Bird Johnson’s “beautification act." The most extensive system of these entities in the United States was initially meant for military convoys.
parts.answer: highways [or freeways or interstates; prompt on roads]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Interstate Highway System was developed during the 1950s under this President, who was inspired by the Autobahn while Supreme Commander of Allied forces during World War II.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Eisenhower twice defeated a politician from this state, Adlai Stevenson, to become President. William Ogden was the first mayor of this state’s city of Chicago.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer prominently used the DSCH motif through many of his works. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man, who composed his Fifth Symphony as a “response to justified criticism” of his opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Shostakovich quoted the DSCH motif in his concerto in E-flat major for this instrument. This stringed instrument is also played by Yo-Yo Ma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Shostakovich used the DSCH motif in every movement of his 8th work in this genre. This genre typically consists of two violins, a viola, and a cello.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These four colors symbolize pan-Arab identity, and can be traced to the flag used during the Arab Revolt of World War I. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name two of these four colors, which are used in the flags of Iraq, Jordan, and Sudan.
parts.answer: red, white, black, and green [accept in any order; accept any two of the four answers given]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The flag of Egypt has red, white, and black stripes and a golden one of these birds to symbolize Saladin. The “bald” one of these birds is a national symbol of the United States.

parts.label: C
parts.question: By contrast, the flag of this theocratic country is mostly green, with a sword and the shahada written in white. It is north of Oman and Yemen.
parts.answer: Saudi Arabia [or Kingdom of Saudi Arabia; or Al-Mamlakah al-ʿArabīyah as-Saʿūdīyah]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Benin people made works made from this material, which feature long-haired Portuguese soldiers. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this material, which the Ineh of the Benin people carve for usage in ancestral shrines. A mask made from this material depicts Idia, the first Queen Mother of the Benin people.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Ivory was used in a collection of Benin artworks, whose common nickname features this other material. This material was used for, and is in the title of, an Auguste Rodin sculpture that was accused of using a live model.
parts.answer: bronze [accept Benin Bronzes; or The Age of Bronze]

parts.label: C
parts.question: In March 2022, this institution announced it would return its collection of Benin Bronzes to the Benin people. This collection of museums runs the National Museum of African Art, as well as the Air and Space Museum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Christoph Meili violated a 1934 act’s Article 47, which enforced the secrecy laws of these institutions. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these institutions in a supposedly neutral country, which stored gold from the plunder of occupied territories in World War II.
parts.answer: banks in Switzerland [or Swiss banks; prompt on just “banks” with “from what country?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Swiss banks notoriously stored gold from plunder taken by this party, which ruled Germany during World War II.
parts.answer: Nazi Party [or the National Socialist German Worker’s Party]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Northern European country had its neutrality broken when it was sold out to the Nazis by the traitor Vidkun Quisling.
parts.answer: Norway [or the Kingdom of Norway; or Kongeriket Norge]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Julio Rodriguez, whose new contract could become the largest in MLB history. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Rodriguez is a rookie playing for the Mariners, a baseball team based in this largest city in Washington state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Rodriguez came in second in the 2022 Home Run Derby to Juan Soto, who was traded from D.C.’s Washington Nationals to this West Coast team. Manny Machado and Yu Darvish also play for this team.
parts.answer: San Diego Padres [accept either underlined part]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Rodriguez became the first rookie in MLB history to hit 25 home runs and obtain 25 of this statistic. Rickey Henderson holds the all-time record in this statistic, large amounts of which were accumulated by Billy Hamilton.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The ribonuclease H domain in these viruses degrades the U5 and R regions of one molecule. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these viruses, which use reverse transcriptase to create complementary strands of DNA from RNA. Lentiviruses are a subtype of these viruses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The pol gene encodes for reverse transcriptase in this bloodborne retrovirus, the causative agent of AIDS.

parts.label: C
parts.question: HIV targets these cells by attacking their CD4 surface receptor. Unlike B cells, these cells mature in the thymus.

parts.question: For 10 points each -- answer some questions about people who drowned in Great Britain.
