parts.question: This author drowned herself in the River Ouse in 1941, after writing novels like The Waves and Orlando.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this novel by Woolf, Mr Ramsey claims how “naturally men are drowned in a storm” while on a trip to the Isle of Skye.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Maggie and Tom Tulliver drowned in the title river in The Mill on the Floss, a novel written by this British author. This author wrote about Dorothea Brooke in Middlemarch.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These shapes have an eccentricity of exactly one. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these shapes, which are formed when graphing quadratic equations.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A degenerate parabola forms one of these shapes. One of these straight shapes is formed when graphing the equation y = mx + b, which is known as slope-intercept form.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In a parabola, the latus rectum is parallel to this line and passes through the focus. This line lies behind the vertex at a distance equal to that between the vertex and focus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This mountain overlooks the resort town of Zermatt. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this notoriously dangerous “Peak of the Meadows,” which lies on the border of Switzerland and Italy. This mountain is partly named for its unique shape, which is a result of the collision of four cirques.
parts.answer: Matterhorn [or Mont Cervin; or Monte Cervino]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Matterhorn is one of this mountain range’s namesake “four-thousanders.” This largest mountain range in Europe runs from France to Slovenia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Zermatt is popular for mountaineering and this other winter sport prevalent in Switzerland. Cities in the United States, such as Telluride and Aspen, are popular resorts for snowboarding and this other activity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One holiday of this name celebrates the willingness of Abraham to sacrifice his son and is considered the “Greater” one. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this name of two Islamic holidays, the “Lesser” of which ends Ramadan.
parts.answer: Eid [accept Eid al-Adha; accept Eid al-Fitr]

parts.label: B
parts.question: On Eid al-Adha, there is no call to this activity given by the muezzin. This activity makes up the Islamic pillar of Salat.
parts.answer: prayer [or word forms, such as praying]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Eid al-Adha marks the end of the Hajj, a ritual pilgrimage to this most holy city in Islam.
parts.answer: Mecca [or Bacca; or Macoraba; or Makkah]

parts.label: L
parts.question: After a battle in this country, Francesco Crispi resigned his post in humiliation, though his constituents kept trying to re-elect him. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, which crushed the army of Oreste Baratieri in the Battle of Adowa.
parts.answer: Ethiopia [or Ityop’iya; or Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; or YeEtiyop’iya]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This city was wracked with violent protests after the Battle of Adowa. The Blackshirts marched on this capital of Italy in 1923.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This fascist led the Blackshirts in the March on Rome, and led Italy during World War II.
parts.answer: Benito Mussolini [or Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini]

parts.question: This organization has raised interest rates four times in 2022. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this central bank, which sets American monetary policy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This chair of the Federal Reserve, who replaced Janet Yellen, is in favor of raising interest rates in an effort to combat inflation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 2022, the Federal Reserve announced this policy to increase the amount of liquid assets that banks have. Due to near-zero interest rates in 2008, this policy with a two-word name was employed to fight the Great Recession.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Nina Simone’s cover of this song was sampled in the 2013 song “Blood on the Leaves.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this song, in which the title object hangs “from a poplar tree.” This song contrasts the “scent of magnolia”  with the “smell of burning flesh.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The anti-lynching song “Strange Fruit” was most notably covered by this singer, nicknamed “Lady Day.” A  2021 film titled United States vs. [this singer] explores her relationship to “Strange Fruit.”
parts.answer: Billie Holiday [or Eleanora Fagan; or The United States vs. Billie Holiday]

parts.question: Before “Strange Fruit,” Holiday was a member of the band of Count Basie, a player of this instrument. This  instrument has 88 black and white keys.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A recent 1.3 billion IMF loan allowed this country’s kwacha to briefly become the world’s best performing  currency against the dollar. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this first African country to default on foreign debt during the COVID-19 pandemic. This country’s  capital is Lusaka.

parts.question: Zambia’s default has sparked criticism of this country’s “debt-trap diplomacy.” This country has financed  African infrastructure projects through its Belt and Road Initiative under Xi Jinping.

parts.label: L
parts.question: UPenn professor Martin Seligman electrocuted these animals to induce learned helplessness. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these canines studied by Ivan Pavlov.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Pavlov taught dogs to drool at the sound of a bell, demonstrating the classical form of this phenomenon, which  is contrasted with its operant form.

parts.label: C
parts.question: B. F. Skinner conditioned these animals to exhibit superstitious behavior, such as head-nodding while waiting  for food. Skinner also operantly conditioned these birds to play ping pong and guide missiles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One subsect of this group in Syria is called the Alawites. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this branch of Islam, whose adherents believe Ali to be the true successor to Muhammad. It is the second  largest branch of Islam, after Sunni.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Shia Twelvers believe in twelve figures known by this title. Sunni Muslims refer to their Mosque leaders  by this title.

parts.question: A hidden imam known by this name is said to appear at the end of the world and establish a final caliphate. A  man who claimed to be this figure led a series of Islamic revolts in Sudan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After Spanish decolonization, Mauritania partially administered a territory named after this desert, but later  withdrew its forces. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this desert that names a disputed territory, whose eastern part is governed by the Sahrawi people.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 2020, the United States recognized this former Spanish protectorate’s claim to the Western Sahara, which it  mostly administers. This North African country’s largest city is Casablanca.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Moroccan-controlled part of Western Sahara is separated from the Sahrawi-controlled part by a berm made  up of this material. Much of the Sahara Desert in northern Africa is made up of this material.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some estimates put the number of these organisms in, and on, an average human at 39 trillion. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these ubiquitous microorganisms. They can cause diseases such as tuberculosis, and comprise one of the  three domains of life, with archaea and eukaryotes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A bacteria in the genus Clostridium causes this disease, whose characteristics include drooping eyelids. This  disease’s toxin is also used in a namesake procedure commonly used to remove wrinkles.

parts.question: Botulinum toxin inhibits the release of acetylcholine, one of these compounds, which is used at neuromuscular  junctions. These compounds are secreted by neurons across synapses.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Residents of this country’s colonies that were born in this country were called peninsulares. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this country which colonized most of Latin America aside from Brazil.
parts.answer: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain; or Reino de Espana]

parts.question: The Spanish crown gave grants of forced native labor to landowners in this system. Due to the shift to  agricultural activity in the Spanish colonies, this system was succeeded by the hacienda system.

parts.question: The Barabar Caves were dedicated to “King Piyadassi,” who has been identified with this ruler. For 10 points  each:

parts.question: Name this Mauryan emperor who converted to Buddhism, a grandson of Chandragupta.

parts.question: Prior to converting to Buddhism, Ashoka operated a torture chamber nicknamed for this location. The Greeks  believed this general location was ruled by Hades.

parts.answer: being burned alive [accept equivalents, such as death by fire; accept sitting on a funeral pyre or  equivalents]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One novel by this author ends with the line “Now vee may perhaps to begin. Yes?” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Jewish-American author of Portnoy’s Complaint, who also wrote many works featuring the character  Nathan Zuckerman.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a novel by Roth, the anti-Semitic Eve Frame writes about her marriage to Ira Ringold, who is a member of  this title group. Arthur Miller’s The Crucible is often thought of as an allegory about the persecution of members of  this group.

parts.question: Roth’s character Eve Frame is based on his wife, Claire Bloom, who shared this profession with Eve Frame.  Marilyn Monroe was another member of this profession.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This function is differentiable everywhere, except at x equals 0. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this function denoted with two vertical bars, which converts a negative number to its positive counterpart.

parts.question: The derivative of the absolute value for x less than zero is this value, while the derivative for x greater than zero  is this other value. Name both, and it may help to know the derivative is equal to the slope for this function.

parts.question: The anti-derivative of the function “one over x” equals this function of the absolute value of x, plus C.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An early example of these rankings dates to a 2005 post on a Tekken 4 forum. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this type of ranking, which sorts objects into categories based on their value. Letters are commonly used  to denote the categories in these rankings, with “S” being the top.

parts.answer: Super Smash Bros. [or Super Smash Brothers]

parts.question: TierZoo, a channel with videos using video game jargon to explain biology concepts, is on this website, the most  popular video-sharing site on the internet.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mary Tyler’s publicity helped popularize the “Anti-Saloon League,” which supported the beginning of this  period. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this period begun by the Eighteenth Amendment, in which alcohol was banned.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This President’s wife was nicknamed “Lemonade Lucy” for trying to keep an alcohol-free White House during  his administration. This man became President after the “Compromise of 1877,” which ended Reconstruction.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The anti-alcohol activist Carrie Nation was told in a dream to “Go to Kiowa” in this state and beat up saloons  with a hatchet. This state was nicknamed “Bleeding” in the lead-up to the Civil War.
parts.answer: what’s the matter with Kansas? [or Bleeding Kansas]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one play, a character with this profession first mentions the title “Bald Soprano.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this profession. In a novel, a character with this profession, Guy Montag, is chased by the mechanical  hound.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Bald Soprano is by this Romanian absurdist playwright, who wrote about a character who screams “I’m not  capitulating!” in his play Rhinoceros.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Ionesco wrote The Bald Soprano and Rhinoceros in this language, which was also used by Paris native Jean  Genet to write The Maids.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A member of this house quipped that the infant Baelon was “heir for a day,” despite Baelon only living that  long. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this royal house, the namesake of a “madness” that affected many of its kings, such as Aerys II. Before  succumbing to that madness, a queen from this house had the masters of the Unsullied killed.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Emilia Clarke portrayed the aforementioned Daenerys Targaryen in this HBO show, adapted from George R. R.  Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In season one of Game of Thrones, Daenerys takes care of these creatures’ eggs, inspiring her nickname of the  “mother of [these creatures].” The prequel series to Game of Thrones is titled House of [one of these creatures].

parts.question: Name this Austrian thinker whose theories of psychoanalysis became decidedly more popular in the US than in Europe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Freud was one of several thinkers invited by Clark University to speak in America; another was this colleague, who coined the theory of the “collective unconscious” and recommended that Freud cheat on his wife in order to get some sound sleep. Freud declined.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Freud’s lectures in America were largely based on his 1899 work on The Interpretation of these unconscious events, which mainly occur during REM sleep. Freud complained of having awful examples of these events during his American trip.
parts.answer: dreams (accept The Interpretation of Dreams; accept Die Traumdeutung)

parts.label: L
parts.question: These substances are classified as “strong” or “weak” based on whether it completely dissociates into its ions, not - as commonly misunderstood by beginning chemistry students - on how good it is at reacting with bases. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for solutions with a pH value less than 7.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concentration of an unknown acid can be judged by this lab technique, in which drops of a known base are slowly added to the solution. An indicator is then used to determine changes in pH.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This strong acid is commonly used in high school titration labwork because it is relatively safe to handle. The extremely low pH of gastric juices is due to this acid.
parts.answer: hydrochloric acid (accept HCl; prompt on “stomach acid”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the traditional order of operations in arithmetic, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Multiplication comes before addition in the order of operations because multiplication is repeated addition; similarly, this operation of repeated multiplication comes before multiplication and division.
parts.answer: exponentiation (accept word forms like exponents; accept “raising to a power”; prompt on “squaring”, “cubing”, or other specific examples of an exponent)

parts.label: B
parts.question: These symbols are used to escape the normal order of operations; that is, “3 plus 4 minus 5” will be different if these symbols are placed around the “4 minus 5”.
parts.answer: parentheses (or parenthesis; accept brackets; accept braces)

parts.label: C
parts.question: With that said - addition has this property, so “3 plus 4 plus 5” gives the same result even if you do put parentheses around two of the numbers. Multiplication also has this property, but subtraction does not.
parts.answer: associative property (accept word forms, like associate)

parts.label: L
parts.question: American author Ambrose Bierce frequently wrote about this conflict, during which he fought in the 9th Indiana Infantry. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this war. In Bierce’s short story “Chickamauga,” a small deaf boy unknowingly sleeps through an 1863 battle that was one of this war’s bloodiest.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Bierce also wrote “What I Saw of” this 1862 battle of the Civil War, during which he actually fought. The short story gives a soldier’s view of Grant’s victory at this Tennessee battle, which was also called Pittsburg Landing.
parts.answer: Shiloh (accept Battle of Shiloh; accept What I Saw of Shiloh)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In a short story titled “An Occurrence at” this place, Confederate civilian Payton Farquhar [FAR-kwar], who is executed by the Union for trying to sabotage the title structure.
parts.answer: Owl Creek Bridge (accept An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge; do not accept or prompt on partial answers or on answers that are out of order)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the myriad ways that western colonization of Australia ruined things, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Most obviously, colonizers sought to assimilate or remove these indigenous people of mainland Australia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1859, Thomas Austin released 24 of these animals into Australia, assuming they could do little harm; they had no predators and bred very quickly. Within 50 years, Western Australia started building a 2,000-mile-long fence meant to keep these creatures out.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 1932, Western Australia deployed machine gunners to deal with these flightless birds. The attempts didn’t really prevent farm losses, so Australia infamously lost the “War” against these birds.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This type of wave is audible if its frequency is between 20 and 20,000 Hertz. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this phenomenon whose vibrations travel through room temperature air at roughly 3443 meters per second.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The intensity of a sound wave is measured in this logarithmic unit, which also has several applications in electronics. A jet engine’s noise commonly registers 140 of these units.
parts.answer: decibel (accept dB; accept bel or B)

parts.label: C
parts.question: While moving through air, sound waves are classified as this type of wave, because the medium moves perpendicular to the motion of the wave. In the main alternative, a transverse wave, the medium moves in parallel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Heats of reaction are often provided in this unit of energy, rather than kilojoules, because they are convenient to measure in calorimeters. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this imperial unit of heat energy that’s about 4.18 Joules. Most often, it’s used to measure the energy content of foods.
parts.answer: calories (accept cal; accept kilocalories or kcal)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Heats of reactions are convenient to write using calories because calorimeters are often filled with water, and in imperial units, this quantity for water is exactly 1 calorie per gram degree Celsius.

parts.label: C
parts.question: If the heat of reaction is measured in one of these devices of fixed volume, you’ll probably see it reported in Joules. These calorimeters have intrinsic heat capacities reported by the manufacturer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1996, Billy Bailey became the most recent, and possibly last, person to suffer this fate, which is only legal in Delaware, New Hampshire, and Washington, and only then as a backup method. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this punishment. It was once commonly performed via the long drop, but it has largely been replaced by more “humane” methods.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Four of this man’s conspirators - including Mary Surratt and George Atzerodt - were hanged at the Washington Arsenal on July 7, 1865. This man was, instead, shot in a burning barn on April 26th.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After the 1862 US-Dakota War, on President Lincoln’s orders, 38 Dakota men were hanged in this state’s town of Mankato, the largest mass execution in American history. A year later, the Dakota were exiled from this state.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This river flows east-to-west into the Atlantic Ocean and lends its name to two African countries on its banks. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this second longest river in Africa.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Congo River separates two national capitals: Brazzaville and this megacity. This capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest city in Africa by size.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Congo River basin is home to both species of the genus Pan: chimpanzees and this smaller relative, whose habitat is south of the river. Scientists speculate that, because these primates can’t swim well, the formation of the Congo River may have caused the speciation between chimpanzees and these primates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In calculus, a line is known by this name if it just barely intersects a curve at one point, as contrasted with a secant line, which cuts through the curve at two nearby points. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this mathematical term. In trigonometry, this word names a function that is equal to the sine function divided by the cosine function.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Finding a tangent line provides a way to calculate this value for a curved line at a given point. For a straight line, finding this value is much simpler; it’s always the same, and it is equal to the line’s rise over run.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This French mathematician’s work on finding tangent lines helped lay the foundation for calculus, but he’s better known today for inventing the rectangular coordinate system. Please give the name of the man, not the coordinate system.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A poem by this man opens with the advice “Go home and write / a page tonight. And let that page come out of you- Then, it will be true.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this co-leader of an early 20th century cultural movement in New York, a Black American jazz poet who wrote “Theme for English B” and the collection The Weary Blues.
parts.answer: Langston Hughes (accept James Mercer Langston Hughes)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Hughes was a dominant figure in the “Renaissance” of this Manhattan neighborhood, which was predominantly Black in the early 20th century. A short Hughes poem named for this place opens by asking “What happens to a dream deferred?”

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Hughes poem from The Weary Blues notes “I am the darker brother. They send me to eat in the kitchen / When company comes.” This poem is a direct response to Walt Whitman’s “I Hear America Singing,” and its title is the first two words of the poem.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Tref is, essentially, the opposite of this adjective, which is equivalent to halal in Islam. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Hebrew adjective that describes foods that observant Jews will eat.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Invertebrates are generally not kosher, except for these insects, which conveniently abound in the Bible. These insects terrorize the Egyptians in the eighth plague in Exodus and are consumed by John the Baptist in the wilderness.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Observant Jews also refuse to eat this meat, according to a prohibition against eating animals that chew their own cud. This meat is foresworn by Muslims as well.
parts.answer: pork (accept pig meat; prompt on “bacon”, “sausage”, or other foods that could be made from pork or other sources)

parts.label: L
parts.question: On one particularly deadly day during this decades-long conflict, Lord Mountbatten was assassinated by a bomb planted on his boat and a convoy was ambushed at Warrenpoint. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this period of off-and-on sectarian violence and rioting that was largely ended by the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Troubles took place in cities like Derry, Belfast, and Dublin on this island, whose Northern region remains part of the United Kingdom.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In April 1916, a massive rebellion swept through Ireland and was brutally suppressed, with most of its leaders being executed. The rebellion began on the day after this major religious holiday, and thus became known as this holiday’s “Rising.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man reproduced a still image from 1953’s Niagara for his Marilyn Diptych silkscreen, which features 25 hypercolored copies and 25 smudged black and white copies of Marilyn Monroe’s face. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Pop artist.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Warhol’s most famous silkscreens are likely his depictions of these common grocery items, produced by Campbell’s.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In addition to his paintings and silkscreens, Warhol created over 100 of these artworks, including a five-hour-long one titled Sleep that depicts John Giorno sleeping and an eight-hour-long one that depicts a slow-motion view of the Empire State Building.
parts.answer: films (accept movies; accept anti-films or anti-movies)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Sinkholes are common when groundwater is able to circulate and the underlying ground is made of this rock. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this rock that is made up of various forms of calcium carbonate, such as calcite. Metamorphosis of this rock can create marble.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The dissolution of limestone can create these empty underground spaces, where stalactites and stalagmites from from dripping mineral water.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Caves, sinkholes, and underground rivers are commonly found in this type of limestone-rich landscape with a German name.
parts.answer: Karst (accept additional information, like karst landscape, karst topography, etc.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The first page of a novel by this author is a bonafide checklist for common tropes in the rest of his writing: a male protagonist is alone in his apartment, cooking pasta and listening to classical music, when he is disturbed by a phone call from a mysterious woman. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this modern Japanese author of The Wind-up Bird Chronicle.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Toru Okada, the protagonist of The Wind-up Bird Chronicle, is tasked with finding one of these missing pets, who also appear in almost all of Murakami’s works. Okada eventually finds the pet waiting at home, meowing as though Okada were the missing one.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Okada de-stresses by ironing these items of clothing, for which he has a 12-step process that cannot be done out of order. In The Great Gatsby, Daisy becomes hysterical at the sight of a closet full of these items in Gatsby’s house.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man wrote five essays under the name of “Helvidius,” arguing against Alexander Hamilton’s “Pacificus” in essays regarding American neutrality. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this American founding father who served as Thomas Jefferson’s Secretary of State and, later, as the fourth US President.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Madison is known as the “Father of” this foundational American document, having drafted much of the theory behind its seven articles.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before quarreling with Hamilton, Madison and Hamilton joined with John Jay to write the pro-Constitution Federalist Papers. The essays were published under this joint pseudonym, meant to evoke a Roman sense of friendliness toward the people.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Christian texts have provided lyrics for many pieces of European music. Answer the following about Christian choral music, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The King James Bible inspired Handel’s Messiah oratorio, which includes this chorus that celebrates the “King of Kings and Lord of Lords.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Catholic prayer begins “Ellen’s Third Song,” a work by Franz Schubert in which the singer pleads to the title religious figure to “hear a maiden’s prayer.” This prayer’s full version is addressed to the “Mother of God.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Sung texts like the “Credo” [kray-doh] and the “Kyrie” [kee-ree-ay] are among the sections of these pieces of Catholic liturgical music. Mozart left a Requiem one of these pieces unfinished at his death.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The AvengerCon scene of this show’s first episode reveals that, in the world of the MCU, Groot is only known to the general population as “Mr Tree.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: After wearing a golden bangle, Kamala Khan becomes the title superhero of this show, whose six episodes premiered in summer 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Kamala Khan is played by this Pakistani-Canadian actress. The show is her first acting credit, and she will reprise the role in an upcoming MCU film.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Ms. Marvel premiered on this streaming service, which owns the rights to the MCU, as well as Star Wars.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Women languishing with mysterious or false illnesses appear frequently in fiction. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: In an Edgar Allan Poe short story about the “Fall of” this family, Madeline becomes sick and seems to die, only to claw her way out of her tomb to actually die alongside her brother, Roderick.
parts.answer: Usher (accept House of Usher; accept The Fall of the House of Usher)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this Charlotte Perkins Gilman work, the narrator is locked in her room at a guest-house to help her recover from post-partum depression, only for her to become manically obsessed with the title wall covering.
parts.answer: The Yellow Wallpaper (do not accept or prompt on “Wallpaper”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This novel gets bonus points for having TWO languishing women: Mina Harker and Lucy Westenra. Abraham Van Helsing hangs garlic in their bedrooms when he realizes that the title vampire is draining their strength.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A multidimensional “landscape” named for this quantity plots genotype against it, and generally assumes that successful organisms fall into local minima. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity that broadly translates to “evolutionary success,” since individuals with the greatest amount of it survive to reproduce.
parts.answer: biological fitness (accept word forms like fittest)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concept of survival of the fittest drives this mechanism of evolution, which was postulated by Charles Darwin in The Origin of Species.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The notion that natural selection slowly explores rugged fitness landscapes, in which successful adaptations are very shallow local ditches, is challenged by this more radical theory of rapid-bursts of successful trait evolution, proposed by Stephen Jay Gould.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Frisky tourist agencies in this country warn of drop bears, which are predatory marsupials that will fall out of trees and attack visitors. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country whose most dangerous animals tend to look more like taipan snakes or redback spiders, and less like koala bears.

parts.label: B
parts.question: By any reasonable set of criteria, the best Australian cryptid is this monster of Aboriginal myth that feasts on unsuspecting humans visiting billabongs. This animal is some sort of linear combination of bird, frog, and alligator.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Aboriginal creation myths speak of a “Rainbow” one of these creatures that inhabited the pre-historic Dreamtime and is associated with rainfall.
parts.answer: serpent (accept snake; accept Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake)

parts.label: L
parts.question: These devices are often crystals of semiconducting material with a p-n junction. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these circuit elements that allow current to flow in just one direction.

parts.label: B
parts.question: For current to flow in one direction in a hypothetically ideal diode, this quantity for the circuit is zero in one direction and infinity in the other. This quantity is measured in ohms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Light-emitting diodes can display different colors based on changes in the size of this region that separate occupied and empty energy levels. Semiconductors have small examples of this region, and doping can make them even smaller.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about spooky stories, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Henry James novella is a ghost story about Miles, Flora, and the ghost of Peter Quint.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This author’s horror collection The Last Seance includes stories featuring Miss Marple and Hercule Poirot, who feature in her more commonly known genre of detective mysteries.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The cursed title object of this 1902 W.W. Jacobs short story “twisted [...] like a snake” after Mr White uses it to wish for two hundred pounds. In modern retellings, its fingers often curl to indicate that a wish has been made.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2022 wildfire damaged many of these sculptures in the Rano Raraku crater. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name or describe these rock figures that were created by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.
parts.answer: moai (accept descriptions of large stone heads; prompt on description of human sculptures, as some of the heads feature torsos)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Large stone heads are a common motif in historical art. This Mesoamerican civilization, which invented a ball game popular in later cultures, carved large heads out of boulders in cities like La Venta.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Several Persian and Greek gods are depicted in massive stone heads on Mount Nemrut, which is in this modern-day country. A decidedly older ancient ruin in this country, C¸ atalhoy¨ uk¨ [chat-ull-HOY-ook], dates to nearly 10,000 years ago.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about 20th century philosophy Martin Heidegger, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Through works like 1927’s Being and Time, Heidegger was a major influence on this philosophical movement, later championed by Jean-Paul Sartre [sart] and Albert Camus [ca-moo], that studies how a human can “be.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Beyond philosophy, Heidegger is best known for his membership in this German political party from 1933 to 1945. Heidegger later distanced himself from this party, but his posthumously-published notebooks include several examples of anti-semitism.
parts.answer: Nazi Party (accept National Socialist German Workers’ Party; accept Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei; accept NSDAP)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Heidegger’s less controversial post-war work includes The Question Concerning this concept, an essay that eventually defines it as including the “equipment, tools, and machines, the manufactured and used things themselves.” Stone tools and computers are commonly cited on opposite ends of humanity’s history of this concept.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name some types of humanoid creatures with animal attributes from Greek myth, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: One of these creatures, Chiron, taught both Jason and Achilles. Chiron was unusual among these creatures because his front pair of feet were often depicted as human, and only his back two feet were horse hoofs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Naiads and dryads were two types of these feminine nature spirits. Echo was one of these creatures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In art, nymphs have often been depicted frolicking with these masculine nature spirits that had the ears and legs of goats, similar to the god Pan.
parts.answer: satyr (accept satyros; accept faun; accept silenos)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan Benazir Bhutto became the victim of this crime in December 2007, leaving her son, Bilawal Zardari, as her political successor. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this criminal-political action that was committed against Bhutto by someone using both a gun and a shrapnel bomb.
parts.answer: assassination (accept word forms like assassinate; accept equivalents like murdering or killing a head of state)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This politician was succeeded as Prime Minister by her son, Rajiv, after her assassination in 1984. This leader was assassinated by her bodyguards after her attack on the Golden Pavilion of Amritsar in her home country.
parts.answer: Indira Gandhi (both underlined parts required; accept Indira Priyadarshini Gandhi with both underlined parts required; prompt on “Gandhi” alone)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Gandhi’s bodyguards-turned-assassins were members of this religion. The Golden Temple is this religion’s central gurdwara.
parts.answer: Sikh (accept Sikhi; accept believers in Sikhism)

parts.label: L
parts.question: These chemicals are usually either lipids, such as testosterone, or proteins, such as insulin. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these chemical signals used throughout the endocrine system.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Most of the hormones produced by this gland found in the base of the brain, such as HGH and FSH, are proteins.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This peptide hormone is made in the hypothalamus but secreted by the posterior pituitary. This “love hormone” is responsible for the evolutionarily useful process of social bonding between parents and their newborns.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This novel’s protagonist romantically pursues Léon Dupuis and Rodolphe Boulanger [roh-DOLF boo-lawn-JAY] to distract from her boring life with Charles. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this novel by Gustave Flaubert [goo-STAHV floh-BAYR] about Emma, a frustrated woman who tries to become independent of her country doctor husband.

parts.label: B
parts.question: To give her time for her affair with Léon, Emma Bovary pretends to take lessons in this instrument. In Kate Chopin’s The awakening, Edna is entranced to pursue her own independence by the chords Mademoiselle Reisz plays with this instrument’s keys.
parts.answer: piano (accept pianoforte or fortepiano; accept specific answers like grand piano)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Both Madame Bovary and The Awakening end tragically, with their protagonists performing this general action.
parts.answer: killing themselves (accept synonyms like suicide; accept specific types, since Emma drinks poison and Edna drowns)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In addition to painting landscapes, J.M.W. Turner was known for painting these vessels, such as one being “tugged to her last berth,” The Fighting Temeraire. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these subjects of nautical paintings.
parts.answer: ships (accept boats; accept specific types, like steamships, warships, sailboats, etc.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a massive oil canvas on display at the Louvre, Théodore Géricault depicted one of these decidedly less seaworthy objects carrying the survivors of the wrecked Medusa.
parts.answer: rafts (accept The Raft of the Medusa; accept Le Radeau de la Méduse)

parts.label: C
parts.question: A Black fisherman braces himself in a small boat in choppy, shark-infested waters in this 1899 painting by Winslow Homer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Harper Lee modeled the character of Dill Harris on this eccentric author, who was her childhood friend growing up in Alabama. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man who wrote Other Voices, Other Rooms and a novel about Holly Golightly.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Harper Lee helped Truman Capote [kah-POH-tee] collect notes for his non-fiction novel In Cold Blood, which chronicles a 1959 home invasion that culminated in this crime, which destroyed the Cutter family.
parts.answer: murder (accept elaborations like mass murder; accept synonyms like killing them)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this other novel by Truman Capote, Holly Golightly is a society girl who earns a living by socializing with wealthy New Yorkers. In a 1960s film adaptation of this novel, Holly is played by Audrey Hepburn.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The idea of using this substance to turn a turbine is centuries old, but it took until the 1700s for its power to be unleashed. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this superheated water vapor that, beginning in the 18th century, was used to power engines that pumped water and powered ships, sparking the Industrial Revolution.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Thomas Newcomen created the first properly functional and practical steam engine, but this Scotsman often gets credit for “inventing” the steam engine because his condenser improved immensely on Newcomen’s design.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Steam engines and modern combustion engines each create rotational power from the back-and-forth motion of these parts. A modern V-8 engine has one of these parts within each of the eight cylinders.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the history of getting your stuff to you, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The US Postal Service is led by the Postmaster General, a post whose first holder was this founding father and inventor of the lightning rod.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This short-lived service promised that its riders would bring mail between Missouri and California in less than two weeks. Maintaining stables was expensive, so this service quickly folded after the invention of the telegraph.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Pony Express’ assets, including its logo, were sold to this stagecoach company for use in its armored car service. Today, this company exists as one of America’s “Big Four” banks, and it came under scrutiny in 2016 for fraudulently creating accounts for, and charging fees to, its customers.
parts.answer: Wells Fargo and Company (accept Wells Fargo Bank)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a common misconception, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding never actually uses this term, preferring the phrase “white paper” instead. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for the status of the mind at birth, according to philosophers who oppose innatism [in-NATE-ism]. We’re looking for a two-word term in either Latin or English.

parts.label: B
parts.question: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding was written by this English Enlightment philosopher, who inspired the Declaration of Independence with a theory about the importance of “life, liberty, and estate.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Studies of identical twins often attempt to answer the debate of “[this concept] versus nurture.” Pro-tabula rasa philosophers like Locke would generally take the “nurture” side, while innatists would take this side.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2021 tweet jokes that this athlete constantly does things that haven’t been done since “’Tungsten Arm’ O’Doyle of the 1921 Akron Groomsmen,” but his team loses anyway. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 2021 AL MVP, a Los Angeles Angel who is developing a case as the greatest baseball player of all time due to his prowess at both hitting and pitching.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Ohtani isn’t favored to win the the 2022 MVP award because Yankees slugger Aaron Judge broke an AL record by amassing 62 of these impressive hits.
parts.answer: home runs (accept homers; accept HRs; prompt on other putative synonyms)

parts.label: C
parts.question: While Judge worked on his single-season home run record, this probably-42-year-old slugger reached 703 home runs for his career - passing Alex Rodriguez for 4th all time - during his farewell season with the St. Louis Cardinals.
parts.answer: Albert Pujols (accept Jose Alberto Pujols Alcantara)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about simple computations involving the numbers three and two, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: “Three times two” gives six, which is the smallest example of these numbers because “three times two times one” equals “three plus two plus one”. The next largest example of these numbers is twenty-eight.

parts.label: B
parts.question: “Three to the power of two” gives the third of these numbers. The list of these numbers begins “1, 4, 9, 16, 25...”, and these are the only numbers that give an integer when they are raised to the one-half power.

parts.label: C
parts.question: “Three to the height of two” is repeated exponentiation, also called this operation. Because this operation comes after addition, multiplication, and exponentiation in the list of hyperoperations, mathematicians gave it a name referencing its spot in fourth place on that list.
parts.answer: tetration (accept word forms like tetrate or tetrating, but do not accept or prompt “tetra” alone)

parts.label: L
parts.question: While speaking as a Member of Parliament, philosopher John Stuart Mill was the first to use this term in its modern understanding: the antonym of a word popularized by Sir Thomas More. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for literature that depicts a catastrophic fate for society, typically set in an unsettling future.
parts.answer: dystopia (accept word forms and additional information, such as dystopian literature)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this dystopian novel by Aldous Huxley, babies are grown in laboratories and engineered into one of five castes, then conditioned with the drug soma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: “It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.” is the opening line of this dystopian novel by George Orwell, in which “Big Brother is watching you.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Julius Caesar’s Commentaries on the Gallic Wars says that these religious figures burned sacrificial victims alive in wicker men, and Pliny describes a ritual in which these people would cut down mistletoe from oak trees for use as a healing elixir. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these ancient Celtic priests.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Modern druidic practices grew out of a British movement that uses this landmark for rituals and ceremonies, even though we don’t have archaeological evidence that ancient druids did. This circular rock formation on the Salisbury Plain was built over 4,000 years ago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Scholars debate whether Stonehenge served this chronological purpose. The Romans developed the Julian variety of this system.
parts.answer: calendar (prompt on “timekeeping,” or similar descriptions of the action, that don’t use the word “calendar”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scientist’s work outside the laboratory include being a signatory on the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and serving on a national commission for science education. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this American chemist whose work inside the laboratory includes the discovery of ten transuranic elements, one of which was named for him while he was still alive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A plaque above a water fountain in this university’s chemistry building honors the location where Seaborg discovered element 97, which is now named for this school. Seaborg served as chancellor of this public university.
parts.answer: University of California, Berkeley (accept UC Berkeley; accept berkelium; prompt on “(University of) California” or “Cal”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Just before berkelium on the periodic table is the element named for this much earlier Polish-French chemist, who kicked off the study of radioactive elements when she discovered radium and polonium.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After Siegfried slays one of these creatures, tasting its blood gives him the ability to understand birdsong. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this type of mythical creature. In a series of 19th century German operas, Fafnir turned from a giant into this creature to guard a horde of gold.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Siegfried kills the dragon Fafnir in the third of the four operas in this cycle by Richard Wagner [ree-kart VAHG-ner], which begins with Das Rheingold.
parts.answer: Ring Cycle (accept Ring of the Nibelung cycle)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This final opera in the Ring cycle typically takes five or more hours to perform, and ends with Valhalla itself burning to the ground.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many authors create a powerful feeling of a setting by setting otherwise unrelated works in a single fictional location based on real life. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Nobel laureate from the American South set Absalom, Absalom!, The Sound and the Fury, and nearly every other one of his works in the fictional Yoknapatawpha [yawk-na-pa-TAW-fa] County in Mississippi.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This English author’s setting of Wessex shares its name with a real medieval English kingdom, but is otherwise fictional. In one book, Jude Fawley moves to Christminster, this author’s version of Oxford.
parts.answer: Thomas Hardy (Jude is the protagonist of Hardy’s Jude the Obscure.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: New England was heavily fictionalized by H.P. Lovecraft for his “Mythos” of this eldritch horror, who “waits dreaming” according to a cultist chant in one story.
parts.answer: Cthulhu ([k’THOO-loo], but be incredibly lenient; accept The Call of Cthulhu)

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these astronomical objects named for Swift and Tuttle would have an impact more than 20 times more devastating than the impact that killed the dinosaurs. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these “dirty iceballs” that grow a tail when they pass by the Sun.

parts.label: B
parts.question: As the comet approaches the Sun, dust and ice sublimating into gases, creating this fuzzy envelope surrounding the comet. The tail is then formed by solar pressure pushing small particles out of this region.

parts.label: C
parts.question: These celestial events occur when the Earth passes through the debris trail left behind by a comet. The Swift-Tuttle comet generates one of these events that appears to originate from Perseus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Woodrow Wilson made this film the first movie to be shown inside the White House, and a white supremacist quote from Wilson appears on title cards during it. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 1915 silent film by D.W. Griffith, often considered the most racist film of all time.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Birth of a Nation spurred a revival of this white hood-wearing hate group.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the KKK’s original incarnation, this Confederate general was the group’s first Grand Wizard. The massacre of hundreds of surrendering Union soldiers by this man’s troops at Fort Pillow is often cited as the darkest day of the Civil War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This religion’s adherents follow an ital [“eye”-tahl] diet and believe that western society, or “Babylon,” is harmful to people from Africa, or “Zion.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this religion founded in Ethiopia, in which wearing dreadlocks honors the Lion of Judah
parts.answer: Rasta (accept Rastafari; accept word forms like Rastafarianism)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Rastafari, the Lion of Judah is a symbol of this emperor of Ethiopia, who is sometimes considered the second coming of Jesus.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Rastafari, grounding ceremonies often incorporate the smoking of this substance, which is valued for its
parts.answer: marijuana (accept ganja; accept synonyms like cannabis; accept slang like pot)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The main, “Greater” band of this mountain range runs west to east across Georgia and Azerbaijan, north of the Armenian Plateau. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this mountain range on the boundary of Asia and Europe, considerably southwest of the Ural Mountains. Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe, is in this range.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Caucasus Mountains span from the Black Sea in the west to this sea in the East. The capital of Azerbaijan, Baku, lies on the shores of this sea, the world’s largest totally-inland body of water.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Dagestan and Chechnya, in the northern foothills of the Caucasus Mountains, are republics of this largest country by land area in the world.
parts.answer: Russia (accept Russian Federation; do not accept or prompt on the Soviet Union, etc.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Unpopular explanations for the origin of this astronomical body include the capture hypothesis. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fifth-largest satellite in our Solar System; note that all four larger satellites are beyond the asteroid belt, and this body is not.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The leading theory for the Moon’s formation is that a hypothetical planet, given this name, collided with Earth over 4 billion years ago. The resulting debris combined together to form the Moon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The far side of the Moon’s surface is covered with craters, some of which created impact-driven volcanic activity on the near side of the Moon; that led to the creation of these dark basaltic plains. You can answer with the official Latin name or its English translation.
parts.answer: seas (accept lunar maria; accept lunar mare [mar-ay])

parts.label: L
parts.question: Ulrich Zwingli and John Calvin rebelled against this denomination’s ban on clerical marriages and the use of icons. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Christian denomination, led by the Pope, that Protestants rebelled against during the Reformation.
parts.answer: Catholic (accept word forms like Catholicism; accept Roman Catholicism)

parts.label: B
parts.question: During the Reformation, this former Catholic friar posted Ninety-Five Theses, and ultimately founded a namesake Protestant denomination.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Martin Luther’s Ninety-Five Theses disputed the Catholic sale of these religious items. By purchasing these things, Catholics could buy freedom from some common sins.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Antoine Gallard added a story about this man to a collection of middle eastern folk tales. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man who enters a magic cave and finds an oil lamp containing a powerful genie who grants his wishes.
parts.answer: Aladdin (accept Ala ud-Din; accept Ala ad-Din)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gallard added the story of Aladdin to this collection of folk tales that also contains the stories of Ali Babba and Sinbad the Sailor.
parts.answer: The Thousand and One Nights (accept One Thousand and One Nights; accept The Arabian Nights; accept The Thousand and One Arabian Nights or One Thousand and One Arabian Nights; accept The Arabian Nights’ Entertainments; accept Les milles et une nuits)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the frame story of the Thousand and One Nights, all of the folk tales are told to the ruler Shahryar by this woman, his wife, who uses the stories to capture her husband’s attention and prevent her execution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This style of music has a regular rhythm, primarily for the benefit of military bands playing it on the move. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this musical genre, exemplified by “The Washington Post” and “The Stars and Stripes Forever.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The aforementioned marches earned this American composer and instrument inventor the title of “the March King”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Another patriotic Sousa march is named for this symbolic item, which is kept in Independence National Historical Park in Philadelphia.
parts.answer: Liberty Bell (accept the Liberty Bell March)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Georgia Gold Rush provided additional impetus for this event, which was legally enabled by the Indian Removal Act of 1830. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this decades-long event in which tens of thousands of Native Americans were forcibly and brutally relocated from southern states to “Indian Territory”.

parts.label: B
parts.question: While this seventh US President is often blamed for the Trail of Tears, modern scholars note that forced relocation of Native Americans was the general goal of the US government long before and long after his two terms in office.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Several decades later, the Indian Territory was admitted to the union as this US state, removing further sovereignty from its Native American population.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This novel’s title character is caught staring across a bay toward a home in East Egg. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this “Great American novel” in which Nick Carraway narrates the wild lifestyle of his neighbor in Jazz Age New York.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In The Great Gatsby, Gatsby stares longingly toward the home of this East Egg woman. This woman, Nick’s cousin, embraces upper class frivolity when she hopes her daughter will be a “pretty little fool.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: When Gatsby and Nick travel from West Egg to downtown New York for parties, they pass through the Valley of Ashes, where Nick is unnerved by the eyes on a billboard advertisement for what optometrist?

parts.label: L
parts.question: It’s Morbin’ time! Answer the following about Morbius, the (sarcasm) INCREDIBLY WELL-RECEIVED film that has 138% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Morbius is based on a Marvel character known as the “Living” one of these common monsters that suck blood from their victims to survive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This actor basically killed the “Morbin’ time” meme by acknowledging it on Twitter. In addition to Morbius, this man made a nuisance of himself while playing Joker in Suicide Squad.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Leto keeps making himself impossible to work with because of his approach to this acting style. This system of acting was created by Konstantin Stanislavski, and demands that actors stay in character both in and out of scenes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This physical force opposes the weight of an object submerged in a fluid. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this force. As an adjective, this term often describes objects that float, such as small floating weather research stations.
parts.answer: buoyant force (accept buoyancy; accept buoys; accept upthrust)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This ancient Greek thinker and inventor of a supposed death ray shouted “Eureka!” upon realizing that buoyancy was the key to finding the volume of irregularly shaped objects.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Archimedes developed a water pump consisting of this simple machine, which is really an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder. As a crank is turned, this simple machine turns and carries water up between its threads.
parts.answer: screw (accept additional information, like water screw or screw pump)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In September 2022, this country launched a surprise counter-attack to retake Kharkiv, causing Vladimir Putin to mobilize reservists. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country that was invaded by Russia in February 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This President of Ukraine and former actor gained international renown for his response to the Russian invasion.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The counter-offensive is pointed toward this coal-rich region of eastern Ukraine, whose separation was recognized by Russia in the lead-up to the war. You can answer with either of the two separatist oblasts, or with the geographic region that those oblasts comprise.
parts.answer: Donbass region (accept Donets Basin; accept Luhansk Oblast; accept Donetsk Oblast; accept Luhansk People’s Republic; accept Donetsk People’s Republic)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man asked permission to celebrate the Toxcatl [tosh-COT’ll] festival, where Pedro de Alvarado’s men committed a massacre on May 22, 1520. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Aztec emperor, the last to effectively rule the empire before the Spanish conquest.
parts.answer: Montezuma II (accept Moctezuma II; accept Moctezuma Xocoyotzin)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Montezuma was killed in the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan [ten-oak-teet-lan], whose ruins are now within this modern-day capital city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Shortly after the death of Montezuma, Hernan Cortez ordered this secret escape from Tenochtitlan, in which hundreds of Spanish soldiers were killed.
parts.answer: La Noche Triste (accept the Night of Sorrows)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The dragon Nidhogg lives in the roots of this tree, and sends the squirrel Ratatosk to run messages to an eagle at the top of it. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this “World Tree,” a giant ash tree that links the nine realms in Norse myths.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This one of the nine realms, sometimes called “Middle Earth,” is the realm inhabited by humans.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Midgard is linked to the gods’ realm, Asgard, by the Bifrost, a bridge in the form of one of these colorful phenomena in the sky.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Heron’s formula calculates this value by taking the square root of the product of four different measurements, each of which has units of length. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this specific type of measurement. The most commonly used formula to find this quantity multiplies the length of a base, times the length of an altitude, times one-half.
parts.answer: area of a triangle (both underlined parts required; prompt on “area”; prompt on “size of a triangle”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: By using a type of analysis named for this mathematical concept, you can show that Heron’s formula must calculate some kind of area; after all, “the square root of length to the fourth power” must be “length to the second power.” Quantities like area have a value of two for this concept, while volume has a value of three.
parts.answer: dimension (accept word forms like dimensional analysis)

parts.label: C
parts.question: As typically written, Heron’s formula includes a variable s to indicate this measurement of the triangle. The lengths that are multiplied together in Heron’s formula are this measurement, along with each side length subtracted from this measurement.
parts.answer: semiperimeter (accept equivalents like “half of the triangle’s perimeter” or “the perimeter divided by 2”; prompt on answers that are equivalent to “a plus b plus c, all over 2” by asking the player “what is that called?”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Schoolteacher Ichabod Crane moves to this village, where he hears the story of a spectral soldier searching for his head. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this east coast village where Ichabod encounters the Headless Horseman.
parts.answer: Sleepy Hollow (accept The Legend of Sleepy Hollow; prompt on “Greensburg;” prompt on “Tarry Town”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow is by this American author of the short stories “The Devil and Tom Walker” and “Rip Van Winkle.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Both “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow” and “Rip Van Winkle” appear in Irving’s short story collection The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon, which claims the stories were recorded by this fictional Dutch historian.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Checkpoints in this process prevent spindle fibers from attaching to the centromeres unless DNA has been replicated properly. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this process of cell division that produces two daughter cells often contrasted with meiosis.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Assuming the cell passes its checkpoint, the spindle fibers retract and sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles of the cell, in this phase of mitosis that comes right after metaphase.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The DNA replication checkpoint measures the lengths of these tips of the chromosomes, which get shorter over the course of multiple cell divisions. Most cells won’t divide once these disappear.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Leslie Groves of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers led this effort, which culminated in the 1945 Trinity test. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this World War II-era “project” that developed the first nuclear bombs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: As head of the Los Alamos Laboratory, this scientist spearheaded the Manhattan Project. During the Trinity test of the first nuclear weapon, this man recalled a quote from Hindu scripture, “Now I am become Death, destroyer of worlds.”
parts.answer: J. Robert Oppenheimer (accept Julius Robert Oppenheimer)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before building the lab at Los Alamos, the Manhattan Project seized land in Tennessee to build this laboratory, which remains an important nuclear research facility today.
parts.answer: Oak Ridge Laboratory (accept Oak Ridge National Laboratory)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This playwright wrote about families separated by shipwrecks caused by storms in plays like The Winter’s Tale and Pericles, Prince of Tyre. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this ultra-famous playwright of the Elizabethan era, who also included a shipwreck that separates twins Viola and Sebastian in his play Twelfth Night.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this Shakespeare play, a storm separates a pair of twins both named Antipholus [an-TIH-foh-luss] and their servants, a pair of twins both named Dromio. Hilarity ensues.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This other Shakespeare play is named for a sea-storm summoned by Prospero, a sorcerer who wrecks Ferdinand’s ship on the island where he lives with MIranda, Caliban, and Ariel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man named his only son Georges [zhorzh] Washington, in honor of his commander. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Frenchman who assisted the Americans at the Battle of Yorktown. Thomas Jefferson later helped this member of the Estates General [eh-STAHT zhen-ay-rall] write the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
parts.answer: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Marquis de Lafayette was named in honor of an ancestor who fought against the English in this war, which lasted from 1337 to 1453.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lafayette’s modern descendants include Philippe, the current king of this country. The Duchess of Brabant is in line to be this country’s first queen.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Italian Baroque [bah-ROHK] artist Artemisia Gentileschi [ahr-teh-MEE-see-ah JEN-tih-LES-kee], for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: After being assaulted in her father’s studio, Artemisia frequently painted biblical scenes in which women, like Judith and Jael, do this to their enemies, Holofernes and Sisera.
parts.answer: killing them (accept synonyms like murder; accept descriptions like “driving a nail through the temple or beheading)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Like many of her contemporaries, Artemisia worked for years in this Italian city. Her painting Judith Slaying Holofernes is displayed in this city’s Uffizi Gallery [oo-FEET-zee Gallery].

parts.label: C
parts.question: While in Florence, Artemisia was patronized by members of this powerful banking family founded by Cosimo.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2020, the first new deep mine for this commodity in England in 30 years was opened, even though the UK plans to close all of its power plants that run on this fuel by 2025. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fossil fuel whose miners went on strike in the 1970s and 80s against pit closures in Yorkshire and Kent.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The newest deep coal mine in England is in Cumbria. Cumbria and Northumberland are the two northernmost English counties and, thus, form England’s border with this British constituent country.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Striking was particularly strong in 1984 in this northern English historic county, by far the largest by area. This county inspired the names of several English colonial cities, including one that was absorbed into Toronto.
parts.answer: Yorkshire (accept County of York; accept City of York; accept Yorks)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about group 15 of the periodic table, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The lightest element in group 15 is this most common gas in Earth’s atmosphere. Its chemical symbol is N.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Two rows below nitrogen is this metalloid that is particularly poisonous to humans, a fact that users of some 19th century makeups or the pigment Emerald Green eventually learned.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The heaviest group 15 element, moscovium, was discovered by bombarding atoms of americium in one of these devices. A magnetic field confines the charged particles within this device as they reach incredible speeds.
parts.answer: particle accelerator (accept cyclotron; accept particle collider)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote a work in which a man kills his wife over an affair with a violinist and another in which the title woman throws herself under a train after having an affair with Count Vronsky. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Russian author of very short novels like The Kreutzer Sonata [KROYT-zer Sonata] and very long novels like Anna Karenina.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This novel is Tolstoy’s longest. It follows the complicated five noble families during and after Napoleon’s 1812 invasion of Russia.
parts.answer: War and Peace (accept Voyna i mir)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this short novel by Tolstoy, the title man goes from being a well-liked socialite to suffering alone after he is fatally injured while hanging curtains.
parts.answer: The Death of Ivan Ilyich (accept Smert Ivana Ilyicha)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The term “helminths” refers generally to these animals, and not just the “flat” ones, which are in the genus Platyhelminthes. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these simple invertebrates whose “pin” variety is an extremely common animal parasite, and whose “earth” variety are useful for composting soil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This worm, a proper platyhelminth, also parasitizes humans and lives in the gut. The longest of these worms ever recorded was more than 80 feet long, which is a pretty good reason for cooking pork before eating it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Worms are convenient model organisms for studying embryonic development, too: the most common example is C. elegans, which is in this worm phylum. You can give either its common or Latin name.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This god defeated the Python and fell in love with the nymph Daphne, who escaped him by transforming into a tree. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Greek god of prophecy and light, the twin brother of Artemis.
parts.answer: Apollo (accept Phoebus Apollo or Phoibos Apollo)

parts.label: B
parts.question: As the god of prophecy, Apollo had a temple at this Greek settlement, where the Pythia sat on a tripod stool over a thermal vent and foretold the future.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Pythia at Delphi ritually inhaled smoke from these leaves, which were sacred to Apollo. Daphne was transformed into one of these trees, whose leaves represented victory in Greece and Rome.
parts.answer: laurel (accept bay laurel; accept bay leaves)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This caudillo [kow-DEE-yoh], who served 11 distinct stints as President, had his wooden leg captured by an infantry unit from Illinois in 1847. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general who lost the Texas Revolution of 1836 and the Mexican-American War.
parts.answer: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna (accept Antonio de Padua Maria Severino Lopez de Santa Anna y Perez de Lebron)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Davy Crockett, James Bowie, and roughly 200 others were killed by Santa Anna’s men at this San Antonio mission in March 1836.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Texian soldiers paired the rallying cry “Remember the Alamo!” with “Remember” this other massacre, which took place three weeks later. Santa Anna ordered the deaths of several hundred prisoners of war in this massacre.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This former member of One Direction made his acting debut playing a British soldier in the 2017 film Dunkirk. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this singer of “As It Was” and “Music for a Sushi Restaurant,” who plays a gay man surviving the 1950s in the movie My Policeman.

parts.label: B
parts.question: At the premier of film Don’t Worry Darling, Styles allegedly spat into the lap of this man, his co-star. This man plays James T. Kirk in the “Alternate Original Series” Star Trek movies.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Don’t Worry Darling was directed by this actress, who starred in the TV series House in the mid-2000s. Styles dated this actress, but is rumored to have broken up her shortly after the movie’s release.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This painting was completed in, and was inspired by a view from, an asylum in Saint-Remy-de-Provence [sawn reh-mee-duh-proh-vons]. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 1889 painting in which numerous bursts of yellow light and a golden crescent moon in the top right corner are set amidst a swirling dark blue sky.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Starry Night was painted by this Dutch artist a year after he dramatically lost part of his ear.
parts.answer: Vincent Van Gogh (accept Vincent Willem Van Gogh)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In The Starry Night, a set of these trees stand in the foreground, just below and to the left of a brightly shining Venus. Van Gogh also painted these tall, narrow trees standing near wheat fields.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Of China’s two Special Administrative Regions, this is the “older” of the two - at least, in the sense that it was transferred to China in 1997, two years before Macau. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this formerly British city in southern China. China’s “one country, two systems” policy explains the governance of this major financial hub.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Hong Kong and Macau lie on opposite sides of the delta of this river, whose English name was inspired by the round, white-colored shells found upstream near Guangzhou [gwan-jo].
parts.answer: Pearl River (accept Zhu Jiang; accept Canton River)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Most of Hong Kong lies on this peninsula. A densely populated Walled City of the same name was, legally, Chinese territory during British control of Hong Kong, until it was demolished in the mid 1990s.
parts.answer: Kowloon (accept Kowloon Peninsula; accept Kowloon Walled City)

parts.label: L
parts.question: These authors wrote Agnes Gray as well as books about Mr Rochester and Heathcliff. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: What surname is shared by a group of three novelists who wrote under the pen name “Bell:” sisters Anne, Charlotte, and Emily?
parts.answer: Bronte (accept Anne, Charlotte, and/or Emily Bronte; accept the Brontes or the Bronte sisters)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Mr Rochester is the title character’s love interest in this novel by Charlotte Bronte. This novel’s title woman discovers that Bertha Mason has been locked up in Thornfield Hall, where she works as a governess.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Heathcliff appears in this novel by Emily Bronte. This novel follows the complicated relationships of the Linton and Earnshaw families, who live near each other in Thrushcross Grange and the title manor house.
parts.answer: Wuthering Heights (be careful; do not accept “withering heights”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these things developed for military applications was named in honor of Ada Lovelace, the daughter of Lord Byron who’s often considered the first computer scientist. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these things, other examples of which include Python, Java, and C++.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other computer science pioneer developed what turned into the programming language COBOL while she was serving as a rear admiral in the US Navy.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hopper is also credited with coining this term, widely used among programmers to indicate a flaw in a piece of software, after she found a physical moth stuck inside a computer switch.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this battle was won by an alliance of Athenian and Plataean [pla-TAY-un] warriors, news of the result was very quickly sent to Athens by a single runner, who legendarily dropped dead on arrival. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 490 BCE battle that inspires the name of a modern, 26-mile-long footrace.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This is the Greek term for a spear-and-shield wielding footsoldier. Ten thousand of these soldiers from Athens joined another thousand from Plataea at Marathon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hoplite soldiers became much more effective after they adopted this defensive formation, which was first used against a foreign enemy at Marathon. In this formation, hoplites are arrayed in long lines, with each using their shield to protect both themselves and the hoplite on their left.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about polytopes, which are geometric objects with “flat sides” in various dimensions, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
