parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about caged panthers in literature:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] In Franz Kafka’s story “A Hunger Artist,” the title character starves to death in his cage after taking this action for 40 days, after which he is replaced by a panther. This action involves not eating for a prolonged period of time.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A panther “paces in cramped circles” “like a ritual dance around a center” in a poem by this poet. This poet asked “Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the angelic orders?” in the first of his Duino Elegies.
parts.answer: Rainer Maria Rilke [or René Karl Wilhelm Johann Josef Maria Rilke] [RYE-ner muh-REE-uh RIL-kuh]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Claire Zachanassian arrives with a caged panther that escapes in The Visit, by Friedrich Dürrenmatt, who is from this country. A character who spends seven years in this country notices a humanist’s name contains seven in Italian.
parts.answer: Switzerland [or Swiss Confederation or Schweiz or Suisse or Svizzera or Svizra or Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft or Confederation Suisse or Confederazione Svizzera or Confederaziun Svizra]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the role of women in 20th-century Christian philosophy:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Before her death in the Holocaust, Edith Stein published Finite and Eternal Being, the culmination of her attempt to synthesize phenomenology with the work of this author of the Summa Theologica.
parts.answer: (Saint) Thomas Aquinas [or Doctor Angelicus or Doctor Communis; prompt on Saint Thomas]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This British ethicist was also influenced by Aquinas. This author of the paper “Modern Moral Philosophy” followed Frank Ramsey in translating much of Ludwig Wittgenstein’s [VIT-gun-shtyne’s] work into English while at Cambridge.
parts.answer: G.E.M. Anscombe [or Gertrude Elizabeth Margaret Anscombe or Elizabeth Anscombe]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In a letter to her priest, Simone Weil [vay] wrote that she became a devout Christian while traveling the world in support of this ideology. This political philosophy seeks to abolish the government.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Art and destruction sometimes go hand-in-hand. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] This artist's work Comedian, which consisted of a banana duct-taped to a wall, was eaten by "hungry artist" David Datuna. This artist also assembled an 18-karat gold toilet titled America.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A Banksy work titled Girl with [this object] was intentionally shredded by its frame after being sold at an auction, after which it was renamed Love is in the Bin.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Banksy hails from this country. In 2003, Banksy entered its Tate Gallery disguised as a pensioner to display a police-tape-covered landscape painting whose imagery was borrowed from this country’s artist John Constable.
parts.answer: United Kingdom [or Great Britain; or the U.K.; or the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Island; prompt with England with “Can you be less specific?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one novel by this author, Joseph is plagued by nightmares after learning of the Massacre of the Innocents, but choosing to only save his son. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this author of The Gospel According to Jesus Christ. In another novel by this author, everybody but the doctor’s wife is afflicted with the title plague of Blindness.
parts.answer: José Saramago [or José de Sousa Saramago]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] José Saramago was born in this Iberian country. One work by Saramago describes an alternate history of this country in which crusaders did not help capture its city of Lisbon.
parts.answer: Portugal [or the Portuguese Republic or República Portuguesa]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this José Saramago novel, the Iberian peninsula breaks off from Europe and floats into the Atlantic Ocean. Characters in this novel include “The King of Starlings,” a girl who finds an endless ball of yarn, and a mute dog.
parts.answer: The Stone Raft [or A Jangada de Pedra]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about reforestation projects, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This rainforest has naturally recovered land about the size of the United Kingdom amidst deforestation largely caused by cattle ranchers. This South American rainforest is the largest in the world.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Three-North Shelterbelt Program has been an effort to stop the expansion of this desert by planting trees. This desert is home to the endangered Przewalski [per-zhuh-VAL-skee] horse and the brown bear relative of the Mazaalai.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The grassroots Green Belt Movement to stop the growth of the Sahara was founded by a person from this country, Wangari Maathai. This country home to the Kikuyu and Luo people is the northernmost country where the Maasai people migrate.
parts.answer: Kenya [or the Republic of Kenya; or Jamhuri ya Kenya]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A quadruple alliance of countries in this region was formed to take advantage of the “Sick Man of Europe’s” weakness during the Italo-Turkish War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this region that a leader predicted “some damned fool thing” would come out of in a speech that dubbed this region the “Powder Keg of Europe.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Calling the Balkans a “powder keg” was one of many quips by this “Iron Chancellor” who plotted the unification of Germany.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Balkan League’s attack followed a 1908 revolution by this movement that forced Sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the Ottoman Constitution. This group perpetrated a genocide that involved many being sent on death marches into the Syrian desert.
parts.answer: Young Turks Movement [or Jöntürkler; accept Committee of Union and Progress or CUP]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A* [A-star] algorithms are often used to perform this task in video games. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this task that is accomplished by Dijkstra’s [DIKE-struh’s] algorithm. The traveling salesman problem is a variation of this task.
parts.answer: pathfinding [accept equivalents like finding the shortest path]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pathfinding algorithms must be performed on these kinds of graphs, in which each edge of the graph has an associated numerical value.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Pathfinding algorithms are classified as this general type of algorithm, whose types include binary and linear. Namesake “engines” use these algorithms to return results from the internet.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Congratulations! You are traveling the Oregon Trail and haven’t died of dysentery! For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] You encounter a family traveling from Nauvoo, Illinois to this territory. Brigham Young allowed polygamy amongst the Mormon settlers he led to this territory.
parts.answer: Utah Territory [accept the State of Deseret]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] As you eat some chunky bison soup, you shudder thinking of this 1846 expedition that took the Hastings Cutoff to reach California, but resorted to cannibalism after being trapped in the Sierra Nevada mountains.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Your wagons are rescued from a river by members of this tribe, who allied with the Arapaho people under leaders like Black Kettle. This tribe names the capital of the state that contains Fort Laramie.
parts.answer: Cheyenne [accept specific branches such as the Northern or Southern Cheyenne; or Tsitsistas; or Tsétsêhéstâhese; or Notameohmésêhese; or Sutaio, or Heévâhetaneo’o]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One poem by this poet describes coming into the world “like Water willy-nilly flowing.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this poet, who described “a Book of Verses underneath the Bough, a Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread–and Thou” in one work.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] One poem from Khayyam’s Rubaiyat describes a “potter thumping” some of this substance. Another poem from the Rubaiyat describes being surrounded by “shapes” of this substance, which can be shaped on a pottery wheel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In a poem from the Rubaiyat, one of these things says, “lo laughing, into the world I blow.” In another poem, one of these objects is cultivated “in June as in January.”
parts.answer: a rose [accept “I Cultivate a White Rose” or ‘Cultivo Una Rosa Blanca”; prompt on “flower”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Cutting one of these shapes in half results in a longer loop with two half-twists. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these shapes that have only one side. They can be made by twisting a strip of paper and gluing together the ends.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Möbius strips are some of the non-orientable surfaces studied in this branch of mathematics. This field, loosely the study of shapes, examines properties that are invariant under continuous deformations like stretching and twisting.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other non-orientable surface is formed by twisting one end of a cylinder inside-out and gluing together the ends. This shape, which cannot be constructed without self-intersection in three dimensions, also only has one side.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A man with this profession holds a giant lollipop in Richard Hamilton’s collage Just what is it that makes today's homes so dif erent, so appealing?. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this profession governed by the WBF whose practitioners follow tips from Lou Ferrigno and Eugene Sandow’s “Grecian Ideal,” as well as the techniques of bulking and cutting.
parts.answer: bodybuilding [accept bodybuilders; prompt on weightlifters or weightlifting]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The documentary Pumping Iron followed this bodybuilder on a quest for a Mr. Olympia title. This actor was elected Governor of California after starring in movies such as The Terminator.
parts.answer: Arnold Schwarzenegger [prompt on Arnold; begrudgingly accept any answers done in a bad accent]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This author judged the first bodybuilding competition in London in 1904. Fans convinced this author to bring back a character who fell off the Reichenbach Falls in the story “The Final Problem.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This architect’s design for a Guggenheim Museum in Vilnius, Lithuania had its construction postponed amid allegations of embezzlement in 2010. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this British-Iraqi architect, whose Zaragoza Bridge Pavilion has 26,000 triangular shingles and whose Guangzhou Opera House resembles “two pebbles” being washed away by the Pearl River.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Hadid also designed the London Aquatics Centre, which was the venue for the swimming, diving, and synchronized swimming events in the 2012 edition of this athletic competition.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Hadid designed this state’s Contemporary Arts Center. I.M. Pei designed two glass pyramid “tents” for this state's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of this religion speak with the lwa [low-UH] Maman Brigitte by offering her dark rum with chili peppers. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Anthropologists popularized the inaccurate idea that members of what Haitian religion stick pins in dolls?
parts.answer: voodoo [or vodun; or vodoun; accept voodoo dolls]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Offering grilled steak and potatoes catches the attention of this lwa who appears as an old man with a cane, straw hat, and dog. This lwa offers to communicate with spirits at crossroads.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Communicating with the orisha of love, Oshun, involves leaving offerings at these places. The largest gathering of humans in the world is the Kumbh Mela [cumb MAY-luh], a Hindu pilgrimage to one of these places that has issues with pollution.
parts.answer: rivers [accept streams; prompt on bodies of water; prompt on the Ganges]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Carl Czerny [CHEHR-nee] wrote the didactic collection The School of Velocity to train players of this instrument. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this instrument, virtuosos for which may study Charles-Louis Hanon's 60 exercises for it or study Muzio Clementi’s sonatinas.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Piano players often practice these “broken” chords that are played one note at a time in rising or descending order.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Piano players also often practice these musical sequences ordered by pitch up and down the piano. Common types of these sequences include chromatic, major, and minor ones.
parts.answer: scales [accept specific types of scales such as the chromatic scale; or the major scale; or the minor scale]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the oldest written complaint, the 1750 BCE Complaint to Ea-Nasir. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Nanni’s complaint about low-quality copper ingots was written in this ancient writing system, which involves pressing cut reeds into clay to make triangle-shaped marks.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Ea-Nasir hailed from Babylon, a city in this ancient region home to the Assyrians and Sumerians. This region corresponding to modern-day Iraq is named for being between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The complaint tablet is held by this museum. Activists have increasingly called for this museum to repatriate artifacts like the Elgin Marbles and Easter Island moai [MOH-eye] which were secured under Queen Victoria.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Molecules tagged with mannose-6-phosphate are sent to this organelle. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] In a disorder named for Philippe Gaucher [go-shay], what organelle is defective, causing macrophages to appear like “tissue paper” due to an inability to process the lipid intermediate gluco•cerebro•side?

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Gaucher’s disease is caused by a defective one of these compounds that degrades glucocerebroside. These compounds act as catalysts in living organisms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During this process, protein-degrading enzymes in the lysosome are released into the cytosol. This process of programmed cell death is contrasted with necrosis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a novel set in this state, Benjy recalls his childhood while searching for golf balls with Luster. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this state home to families such as the Snopes and the Bundrens. An author from this state drew detailed maps of Yoknapatawpha [YOK-nah-pa-TAW-phuh] County, a fictional county located in this state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Yoknapatawpha County is the setting of many novels by this author of Absalom, Absalom! and The Sound and the Fury.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this Faulkner novel, a bootlegger named Joe Christmas slits a woman’s throat after she tries to force him to pray. The title of this novel refers to the burning of Joanna Burden’s house.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In his book The Open Veins of Latin America, Eduardo Galleano argues that returns on Dutch investments in this crop were responsible for the growth of capital in Europe. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this crop which was stored as molasses or distilled into rum after being harvested in the Caribbean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Caribbean sugar plantations were centered on these estates that evolved from the encomienda system and bound workers with debt to the land. Hernán Cortés was the first patrón of one of these estates in Oaxaca [wha-HAH-kuh].
parts.answer: haciendas [accept the hacienda system; accept haciendas azucareras]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] On this island, the colono sugar farmer class emerged with the opening of its first sugar mill in 1873. Ponce de León was the first governor of this island, which was defended by a fort called El Morro.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Donna Tartt’s book The Goldfinch was inspired by a Carel Fabritius painting which disappeared after a gunpowder arsenal exploded in this city. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this city where the painting The Little Street was produced by the artist of The Milkmaid. Peasants stand near herring boats on a riverbank in a landscape of this city.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Virgin Mary watches over two children playing with a goldfinch in one of this artist’s many landscapes with Madonnas. Plato points a finger in the air while walking in this Renaissance artist’s The School of Athens.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Paintings of goldfinches appear alongside the now-extinct passenger pigeon and great auk in this French-American naturalist’s collection Birds of America. A modern bird conservation group is named after him.
parts.answer: John James Audubon [accept the Audubon Society]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The introduction to a translation of this poet’s work quotes Aristotle, who says, “[This author] says that to die is evil: so the gods judge. For they do not die” and explains the translator’s use of brackets. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this poet who Anne Carson translated in the collection If Not, Winter. This ancient Greek poet from Lesbos described the title “Deathless…child of Zeus” in “Hymn to Aphrodite.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Anne Carson also wrote about the ancient Greeks in one of these works “of Red,” which opens “He came after Homer and before Gertrude Stein,” referencing an author who wrote one of these works about her lesbian lover.
parts.answer: autobiography [or autobiographical; prompt on biography or biographical; accept Autobiography of Red; accept The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Anne Carson’s “The Glass Essay” details the speaker’s obsession with this author’s use of the word “whacher” [watcher], and describes reading the part in this author's novel Wuthering Heights “where Heathcliff clings at the lattice in the storm.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some groups of these insects have evolved to “farm” various fungi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these colonial insects of the family Formicidae. They come in several forms including “workers,” “soldiers,” and “queens.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This group of ants practice highly sophisticated fungal agriculture using three different types of workers. These ants get their common name from slicing apart a certain food source.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Other groups of ants perform “dairy farming” by protecting these sap-sucking insects and harvesting their nutrient-rich honeydew secretion.
parts.answer: aphids [or greenflies or blackflies or Aphidoidea]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This theorist argued that the distance between moving heavenly spheres like the Sun created ratios that were the root of musical harmony. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this music theorist who discovered that halving a string raises its pitch by an octave when struck or plucked after listening to a blacksmith’s hammer.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Pythagoras established the perfect fifth as an easy base for this activity. This activity can involve modifying string tightness with pegs to match the pitch of a two-pronged fork.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Ancient Greeks would study and compose songs called teletai based on this figure. An “Infernal Galop” that was adapted into the Can-Can appears in a Jacques Offenbach opera about this figure.

parts.label: L
parts.question: As Georg Cantor Orwell once said, all infinities are big, but some infinities are bigger than others. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] The cardinalities of different infinite sets can be expressed by a sequence of numbers denoted by this letter. The natural numbers have cardinality “this letter”-zero.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Sets with cardinality aleph-zero, like the integers and the rational numbers, have this property, since they can be mapped one-to-one to the natural numbers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Cantor’s diagonal argument shows that the set of these numbers is not countable. These numbers return positive values when squared, as opposed to imaginary numbers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the many titles of Jesus, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] In the Book of Revelation, John weeps when Jesus opens the scroll of God’s judgment, revealing him as the “Lion” of this tribe. Solomon and David come from this one of the surviving two tribes of Israel.
parts.answer: Tribe of Judah [accept the Lion of Judah; prompt on Judea]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In contrast, Jesus is also known as this gentler animal of God, as he is the perfect and ultimate sacrifice. Isaiah 53 describes a virtuous servant facing his death like one of these animals led to the slaughter.
parts.answer: lamb [accept the Lamb of God; accept sheep]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Another title for Jesus is the Alpha and the Omega, two letters that are inscribed on a candle lit on this holiday. Maundy Thursday in the week preceding this holiday is celebrated with a foot-washing ceremony.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The nearly vertical Precipice Trail can be found in this national park, which is also home to many metal rungs on its Beehive Loop. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this national park located on Mount Desert Island in Maine. The tallest mountain in this national park, Cadillac Mountain, is the first to see the sunrise in the U.S. for parts of the year.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Acadia National Park and Bar Harbor lie southwest of this bay that separates New Brunswick and Nova Scotia. The Mi’kmaq people fished in this bay on which Saint John was settled.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Katahdin Woods north of Acadia is a more popular spot to see these animals. This largest member of the deer family is common in boreal forests on the U.S.-Canada border.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the lexicon of Edgar Allen Poe:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Poe wrote this poem about a bird who repeatedly croaks “Nevermore.” This poem also describes a “pallid bust of Pallas just above my chamber door.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This poem by Poe describes the “tintinnabulation” of its title objects that “[Keep] time, time, time, / In a sort of Runic rhyme.” The second line of each stanza in this poem describes those things as “gold,” “silver,” “iron,” and “brazen.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In Poe’s short story, “The Murders in the Rue Morgue” C. Auguste Dupin uses “ratiocination” [ra-TEE-oh-sen-AY-shun] to deduce that Madame L'Espanaye was stuffed up a chimney by one of these animals. In another Poe short story, Hop-Frog dresses up royalty as these animals for a masquerade.

parts.label: L
parts.question: May 3rd, 1791 saw the adoption of the world’s second-ever modern constitution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The constitution was adopted by the “commonwealth” between this country and its northern neighbor Lithuania. Soon after, this country was partitioned three times among its neighbors.
parts.answer: Poland [accept Commonwealth of Poland; accept Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The May 3rd Constitution was inspired by this other country’s constitution, which was written in 1787 to replace its Articles of Confederation.
parts.answer: United States of America [or U.S.A; accept any underlined portion]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The May 3rd Constitution was nullified due to Russian bribery at a 1793 meeting of this parliament of the Commonwealth. It shares its name with the lower house of Poland’s modern-day parliament.

parts.label: L
parts.question: “Pillow” examples of this substance are extruded at mid-ocean ridges. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Give this term for molten rock on the Earth’s surface. It is contrasted with magma.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This volcanic rock names a type of fast-flowing lava with a low proportion of silica [SILL-ih-kuh]. The solidification of this rock creates shield volcanoes in places like Hawaii.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This Hawaiian term refers to lava flows with a rough, jagged surface that is difficult to walk across. It is contrasted with a smoother type of lava known by a different name.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote about the unnamed two-hundred-year-old dictator of a Caribbean island in The Autumn of the Patriarch. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author. In another work, this author wrote about Pelayo, who keeps the title senile character in a chicken coop.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This lifelong enemy of Gabriel Garcia Marquez fictionalized the day of Rafael Trujillo’s assassination in his novel The Feast of the Goat. This author also wrote Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Vargas Llosa and Garcia Marquez are both authors who blend fantasy with the careful depiction of daily life, a genre known as the “magical” form of this broader style. This style seeks to represent things as they actually are.
parts.answer: realism [accept magical realism or magic realism]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Annie Malone’s “Poro agents” who sold products for this substance included the first self-made female millionaire, Madame C.J. Walker. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this substance, which as part of the Black is Beautiful movement, was stylized into afros, cornrows, and dreadlocks.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This activist advised “Do not remove the kinks from your hair; remove the kinks from your brain” in support of natural Black hair. This activist founded the Black Star Line as part of the “Back to Africa” movement.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Marcel Wave and Josephine Baker’s Eton Crop were hairstyles popular amongst this generation of women in the 1920s exemplified by Clara Bow’s “It Girl” wearing revealing dresses and androgynous hairstyles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer questions about famous swines in mythology, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Because he got hungry, the pig was the twelfth and last animal to finish a race hosted by the Jade Emperor that determined this twelve-year calendar. 2022 is the year of the Tiger in this calendar.
parts.answer: Chinese zodiac [prompt on the Chinese calendar]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This nasty piggy was sent to ravage an Aetolian [ee-tol-EE-an] kingdom by Artemis after King Oeneus [EE-nee-us] forgot to include her in his offerings. This boar was hunted by heroes like Meleager and Atalanta.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This Norse goddess’s servant Óttar turned into the boar Hildisvíni for her to ride into battle. This daughter of Njord had a similarly named brother who owned a boar whose bristles glowed in the dark.
parts.answer: Freyja [or Freya; or Freyia; or Freja; reject “Freyr”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about Debra Austin, the first Black principal dancer at a major ballet company:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Austin’s accomplishment is sometimes misattributed to this contemporary dancer who was the first Black principal dancer at the American Ballet Theatre.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] One of Austin’s lead roles was for Filipo Taglioni’s La Sylphide, which was written to show off this technique. A special box in ballet shoes helps dancers perform this technique which involves moving on the tips of the toes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Austin was known for her ability to perform these types of moves. Examples of these steps in ballet include the pas de chat and grand jeté in which both feet leave the ground.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Boris Johnson’s resignation, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] In May 2022, Boris Johnson was fined for violating his own COVID-19 regulations during one of these events at 10 Downing Street in 2020. Finnish PM Sanna Marin attracted controversy for her conduct at one of these events.
parts.answer: parties [accept equivalents like social gatherings; accept Partygate]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In June 2022, 41 percent of this body’s Conservative members submitted no-confidence votes against Johnson. This body, divided into the House of Lords and the House of Commons, meets in the Palace of Westminster.
parts.answer: British Parliament [or Parliament of the United Kingdom]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Johnson resigned in July 2022 shortly after several ministers left his cabinet, including this former Chancellor of the Exchequer. This MP was announced as Liz Truss’s successor in October 2022.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, name these results in electrostatics that have analogs for gravity:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This law describes the electric field due to one or more point charges. A constant appearing in this law equals one over 4 pi times the permittivity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Coulomb’s law states that electrostatic force is proportional to the inverse square of this quantity. Gravitational force drops off with the square of this quantity by Newton’s law of universal gravitation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The differential form of this law holds that the divergence of an electric field is equal to the charge density divided by the permittivity. Newton used its analogue for gravity to prove the shell theorem.
parts.answer: Gauss’s law [accept Gauss’s flux theorem; reject “Gauss's law for magnetism”]

parts.label: L

parts.question: This American author who died in 2016 wrote To Kill a Mockingbird.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lee's friendship with Truman Capote inspired this character in To Kill a Mockingbird. This character visits Maycomb every summer from Meridian and quickly becomes friends with Scout and Jem.
parts.answer: Dill Harris [or Charles Baker Harris; accept any underlined portion]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a dispute over where to build this city, its eventual founder claimed to have seen twelve auspicious birds to his brother's six. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city in modern-day Italy, named for the brother of Remus. It eventually became the center of an empire whose gods included Jupiter, Mars, and Pluto.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Romulus and Remus were legendarily raised by one of these creatures, who were honored in the festival of Lupercalia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After Romulus and Remus were abandoned on the banks of this river, its god saved them. This third-longest river in Italy flows through Rome.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The current holder of this position, Tenzin Gyatso, is one of only two living people who were heads of state during World War II. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this position held by the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, currently occupied in exile in Dharamsala, India due to oppression by the Chinese government.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Tibetan Buddhists often worship by repeatedly chanting these sacred phrases, which include "om mani padme hum".

parts.label: C
parts.question: Tibetan Buddhists are split into schools named after "Red" and "Yellow" types of these garments. Muslims often wear one of these garments called a taqiyah during prayer.
parts.answer: hats [accept specific types of hats like skullcaps]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Parkinson's disease, the body produces lower amounts of this neurotransmitter. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this neurotransmitter often associated with pleasure and emotional highs. Anticipation of rewards increases the amount of this chemical in the brain.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other neurotransmitter is believed to play major roles in mood and appetite, among other things. Its reuptake is inhibited by SSRIs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: SSRIs are often prescribed to treat this mental health condition which may be caused by a lack of serotonin. It can cause low self-esteem, a prolonged lack of happiness, or a loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities.
parts.answer: clinical depression [or major depressive disorder or MDD]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about unusual self-portraits.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This man depicted himself with the title features in his Self-Portrait with Seven Fingers. He depicted a burning synagogue in his depiction of the Crucifixion, and his most famous work, I and the Village, was inspired by a village in Belarus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This man depicted himself thrice in his Triple Self-Portrait. He also painted for the Saturday Evening Post, and depicted Ruby Bridges walking to school escorted by National Guardsmen in The Problem We All Live With.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Rockwell also created a series of paintings depicting this many freedoms. In another unusual self-portrait, Belgian surrealist René Magritte painted himself with this many arms, two more than the usual number.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This number is so large that if a perfectly efficient computer the size of the Earth were to store its value, it would collapse into a black hole. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify this number equal to the value of an extremely large exponentiation tower, which was popularized in a 1977 column by Martin Gardner, at which point it was the largest number ever used in a serious mathematical proof.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Graham's number is the upper bound to a problem from Ramsey theory, a subfield of graph theory which involves doing this process to graphs in certain ways. A famous computer-assisted proof by Haken and Appel showed that any map can have this process done to it with only four different labels.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Specifically, the problem asked for the smallest dimension n in which a complete graph on the vertices of an n-dimensional hypercube, if each edge were colored red and blue, must contain a mono-colored one of these shapes. These shapes have four equal sides and four right angles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Over 250 of these things are currently being stored in Moses Lake, Washington. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these things which were withdrawn from service worldwide in March 2019 following two deadly accidents in 6 months caused by a faulty MCAS system which the manufacturer of these things failed to mention in their manuals.
parts.answer: 737 MAX airplanes [prompt on airplanes or passenger airplanes or 737 airplanes; accept but DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL answers like Boeing 737 MAX]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American aircraft manufacturer founded in Seattle produces the 737 MAX. Their primary competitor is Airbus, and their other planes include the double-decker 747.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A recent Boeing 737 crash that was not caused by manufacturing faults, meanwhile, occurred in January 2020 when Ukraine International Airlines flight 752 was shot down shortly after departing from Tehran, the capital of this country, by its military.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about oceanic trenches, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Ocean trenches are formed by this geological process, in which one tectonic plate slides under another at a convergent plate boundary.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The regions near subduction zones often contain large numbers of this type of mountain, examples of which include Mount St. Helens in Washington and Kilauea in Hawaii. These mountains typically eject large amounts of magma when they erupt.

parts.label: C
parts.question: These other undersea formations are caused by volcanic activity, usually at divergent plate boundaries. They may form “black smokers” or “white smokers”, and release warm, nutrient-rich water through the seabed, creating habitats for animals like the giant tube worm.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Isaac Newton first formulated a universal law of this force. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this force whose magnitude is equal to the product of the masses of two objects, times a namesake constant, divided by the square of the distance between them.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A common system involving Newton's laws of gravitation is a problem involving this many bodies orbiting each other. Newton also formulated this many laws of motion.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lagrange found special cases of the three-body problem in which the bodies could exist in stable or unstable versions of this state. When the net force on an object is zero, it's in this state.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This prime minister was nicknamed "Milk Snatcher" after cutting school meal benefits. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this first female European Prime Minister who was almost killed in an IRA bombing in Brighton.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Thatcher was the prime minister of this country, whose regions include Wales and Scotland and which has also been led recently by David Cameron.
parts.answer: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland [accept the UK or Great Britain; do NOT accept or prompt on "England"]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Thatcher successfully ended a nationwide strike of people in this profession led by Arthur Scargill. This profession was concentrated in northern England and the Welsh mountains, and is also common in the U.S. in states like West Virginia.
parts.answer: coal mining [accept word forms; prompt on mining by asking “for what resource?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this movie, the main character kills his girlfriend after a Ferris wheel breaks down. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 2017 movie adaptation of a manga and anime series about Light Turner finding a book with the power to kill.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Death Note adaptation was headed by this streaming service after they bought the rights to the movie from Warner Bros. This streaming service's first original TV series, House of Cards, achieved widespread popularity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In summer 2020, Netflix brought this animated series to its online streaming services. This series depicts Aang (rhymes with “bang”), who has the power to perform four different kinds of magic.
parts.answer: Avatar: The Last Airbender [or ATLA; prompt on Avatar alone]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Aristotle tutored this man, who died in Babylon at age 32, leaving his empire to be split among the Diadochi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this king of Macedon who built an empire spanning from Greece to India. He named many cities after himself, including one in Egypt home to a famous lighthouse.
parts.answer: Alexander the Great [or Alexander III of Macedon, or Alexandros ho Megas, or Alexandros III ho Makedon; prompt on Alexander or Alexandros]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This man was Alexander the Great's father. He was assassinated by one of his bodyguards and led the League of Corinth.
parts.answer: Philip II of Macedon [or Philippos II ho Makedon; prompt on Philip]

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander defeated Darius III, the ruler of this large empire centered on modern-day Iran.
parts.answer: the First Persian Empire [or the Achaemenid Empire, or Xšāça]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This collection includes tales told by the Pardoner and the Nun's Priest. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this collection in which pilgrims tell stories on a pilgrimage to the tomb of Thomas Becket.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This British author wrote The Canterbury Tales and was a contemporary of Giovanni Bocaccio.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This character in The Canterbury Tales tells a tale about Arcite and Palamon, who both fall in love with Emily upon seeing her. This character's tale follows the work's general prologue.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This novel's lesser characters include 'party enemy' Emmanuel Goldstein, who may or may not actually exist, and a philologist named Syme. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this dystopian novel by George Orwell about Winston Smith's life under the repressive regime of Big Brother, named for the year in which it takes place.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1984, Winston has a secret affair with a woman with this name. Mario Vargas Llosa (YO-sa) wrote a novel partially titled for a character with this first name "and the Scriptwriter".
parts.answer: Julia [accept Aunt Julia and the Scriptwriter; also, I guess you can accept pronunciations that say "HOO-lia" because Vargas Llosa wrote in Spanish]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Early in the novel, Winston's suspicions that Julia is a member of a resistance group are confirmed when she hands him a note containing this three-word confession.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Benjamin Edes printed a famous engraving of this event. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify this 1770 event in which British soldiers shot and killed several people protesting colonial laws in the capital of Massachusetts.
parts.answer: Boston Massacre [accept the Incident on King Street from traitorous royalists]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This dock worker was the first victim of the Boston Massacre. Most historians agree he is both of African and Native American descent.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Boston Massacre was depicted in an engraving by this silversmith. This freedom fighter orchestrated a signal to light one lantern if British forces were advancing by land and two if by sea in one of his most famous feats.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about words prefixed with re-, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This word refers to an item defined based on itself, such as a sequence where each number is defined as a function of previous numbers in the sequence.
parts.answer: recursion [or recursive or other word forms]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This term can describe an election to remove a politician in the middle of their term, a notice not to use a certain product, or your ability to remember things like the answer to this bonus.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This word means compensation paid by a government for a historical wrong. Ta-Nehisi Coates wrote an essay in the Atlantic titled "The Case For" this word, arguing that Black Americans should be paid to compensate for a history of oppression.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The pivotal event of this play comes after Hally spits in Sam's face and orders him to call him by the title name. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this play about the increasing mistreatment of two black servants by their master's teenage son, the magnum opus of Athol Fugard.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Fugard was from this country, where authors like Nadine Gordimer and Alan Paton wrote about apartheid.
parts.answer: Republic of South Africa [or RSA, or Republiek van Suid-Afrika, or iRiphabhuliki yaseNingizimu Afrika, or answers in any of South Africa’s other eight official languages -- consult Wikipedia if you actually need to]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Alan Paton wrote this novel about the elderly Zulu priest Stephen Kumalo who travels to Johannesburg and deals with his son Absalom's murder of Arthur Jarvis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You are the Lorax. Speak for some trees, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Most trees are covered in these objects, at least during the summer. These flat green structures allow the trees to "breathe", and during the fall they may change color.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Trees whose leaves change color and fall off every winter are referred to by this term, which is contrasted with "evergreen".

parts.label: C
parts.question: Many evergreen trees fall into this category of plants which bear exposed seeds, whose name comes from the Greek for "naked seed". They are contrasted with angiosperms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After one man performed this action in 1865, he jumped onto the stage of a theatre and shouted "Sic Semper Tyrannis". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify this action, which was also performed on November 22, 1963 in Dallas, Texas. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: assassinating the President of the United States [accept any answers which involve killing or murdering or shooting the President; accept POTUS in place of “the President”; prompt on just murder or assassination or similar answers by asking "who was the victim?"]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This actor shouted "Sic Semper Tyrannis", or "thus always to tyrants", after shooting Abraham Lincoln in 1865.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After the assassination of William McKinley, Congress passed a law to task the Secret Service with protecting the president. The Secret Service was originally a branch of the Treasury Department tasked with preventing this crime.
parts.answer: counterfeiting money [accept obvious equivalents like making fake money] <Singh, History>

parts.label: L
parts.question: A bay in this island contains the smaller Gonave Island. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Caribbean island split between two countries, the French-colonized Haiti in the west and a larger Spanish-speaking country in the east.
parts.answer: Hispaniola [or La Española, or Ispayola; note that the indigenous name for the island is "Haiti" but we cannot accept that as it's already in the question]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This country occupies the eastern portion of Hispaniola. Its tourist attractions include Pico Duarte and Lake Enriquillo, and its capital is Santo Domingo.
parts.answer: Dominican Republic [or Repúblicana Dominicana, do NOT accept or prompt on Dominica as that is a completely different Caribbean island country]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This is the most popular sport in the Dominican Republic. David Ortiz, Sammy Sosa, Bartolo Colón, and Albert Pujols are among the many Dominicans who have achieved success as professional athletes in this sport.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Benoît Mandelbrot (ben-WAH MAN-del-broh) argued that Great Britain's coastline was one of these things. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these self-similar figures which include the Sierpiński triangle, the Cantor set, the dragon curve, and others.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A fractal named for Niels von Koch and this kind of figure can be constructed by starting with a triangle, then adding triangles with smaller bases onto the straight lines, and repeating infinitely.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Fractals have a "Hausdorff" variety of this concept which can be a non-integer and measures the complexity of a fractal. Shapes like circles and squares exist in a plane, which has two of these, whereas solid objects like cubes have three of them.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During a study at Yale University, subjects demonstrated an unexpected willingness to take this action. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Describe this action, the focus of Stanley Milgram’s obedience experiment. In that experiment, subjects were instructed to do this to “learners” who failed at a word-memorization task, and generally did so despite being told that it could be extremely painful.
parts.answer: giving them an electric shock [accept any answers indicating shocking them or electrocuting them; prompt on hurting them or causing pain or similar answers by asking “in what manner?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Milgram was inspired to conduct the experiment to determine whether the millions of people involved in perpetrating this atrocity could have been merely "following orders". During this event, over six million Jews were killed and millions more forced to flee Europe.
parts.answer: the Holocaust [or the Shoah, or HaShoah; prompt on World War II]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This German-American Jewish philosopher also explored the motivations of Holocaust perpetrators, coining the phrase "the banality of evil" to explain it. She also wrote the books Eichmann in Jerusalem and The Origins of Totalitarianism.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man depicted a skull in the title object in his painting Eye, and he depicted two hands drawing each other in his Drawing Hands. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Dutch artist known for his tessellations and depictions of paradoxes such as waterfalls which flow into themselves.
parts.answer: M. C. Escher [or Maurits Cornelis Escher]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Escher's Hand with Reflecting Sphere is an unusual form of this type of artwork, in which the artist depicts themselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Escher also painted a paradoxically infinite one of these structures in Ascending and Descending. Marcel Duchamp produced a painting of a "Nude Descending" one of these structures.
parts.answer: a staircase [accept obvious equivalents like a stairwell or stairway or just stairs] <Young, Fine Arts>

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer some questions about very badly named military operations:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The goal of Operation Chattanooga Choo Choo was to bomb tracks for these vehicles, which passengers on the Trans-Siberian Railroad used.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Operations Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Supper, and Dessert were launched to bomb this country neighboring Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
parts.answer: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The U.S. occupied New Georgia in Operation Toenails in this war, which also included the battles of Iwo Jima and Okinawa.
parts.answer: World War II [or the Second World War] <Kher, History>

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about geographical locations related to the song "Take Me Home, Country Roads":

parts.label: A
parts.question: "Take Me Home, Country Roads" is the official state anthem of this U.S. state. The song claims that this state is "almost heaven" and compares its mountains to a motherly figure.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This is the last name of the singer of "Take Me Home, Country Roads." This is also the name of a city nicknamed the "Mile High City", the capital of Colorado.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The second line of "Take Me Home, Country Roads" mentions both the Blue Ridge Mountains and this Virginia river, the largest tributary of the Potomac. A folk song with the same name as this river says "we're bound away / across the wide Missouri".

parts.label: L
parts.question: The stew cholent (kho-lent) is traditionally eaten for one meal on this day. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Jewish observance that falls on the seventh day of the week. Observant Orthodox Jews often refrain from work on this day.
parts.answer: Shabbat [or Shabbos or the Sabbath; prompt on Saturday]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The challah bread is covered while this blessing is recited during Shabbat. This blessing is recited over wine or grape juice during the first meal of the Shabbat, on Friday night.
parts.answer: kiddush [do NOT accept or prompt on "kaddish", which is a different Jewish prayer]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Wine or grape juice is also used to extinguish one of these objects at the end of Shabbat. One of these objects is lit on each day of Hanukkah.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about carbon-12's role in chemical measurement, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This unit of quantity is equal to the number of particles in 12 grams of carbon-12. The mass of one of these units for a specific element is that element's molecular weight.

parts.label: B
parts.question: One mole is equal to 6.02 x 10 23 , a number named for this Italian scientist.
parts.answer: Amedeo Avogadro [or Lorenzo Romano Amedeo Carlo Avogadro; accept Avogadro's number]

parts.label: C
parts.question: One mole of the "ideal" form of this state of matter will occupy a volume of 22.4 liters at standard temperature and pressure. This state of matter expands to fill its containers and is the least dense of the three primary phases.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Anorthosite is a rock comprised almost entirely of this mineral. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: What mineral which forms the continuous branch of Bowen's reaction series is the most common mineral in the Earth's crust?

parts.label: B
parts.question: Feldspar's molecular structure includes eight atoms of this element, which comprises almost half of the Earth's crust. The primary component of sand is a compound of silicon and this element called silica.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Feldspar typically contains silicon, oxygen, an alkali metal, and this element, the most common metal in the Earth's crust. It is symbolized Al, and is commonly used to make foil.
parts.answer: aluminum [or aluminium; prompt on Al] <Sethi, Science>

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some of America's most celebrated writers were terribly shy people. For 10 points each, answer the following about some reclusive American authors:

parts.label: A
parts.question: There is only one known surviving photograph of this Massachusetts poet who spent much of her adult life in isolation. Her poems include "I'm Nobody! Who are you?" and "I heard a Fly buzz— when I died”.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This postmodernist author of The Crying of Lot 49 has managed to stay out of the public eye for six decades. He wrote about Tyrone Slothrop and the V-2 rocket in Gravity's Rainbow.
parts.answer: Thomas Pynchon [or Thomas Ruggles Pynchon, Jr.]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Novels by the reclusive Cormac McCarthy include Blood Meridian and All the Pretty Horses, two examples of this literary genre. Actor John Wayne is also associated with this broad genre of fiction which frequently involves cowboys, sheriffs, and outlaws.
parts.answer: Western fiction [or Westerns; accept Wild West; accept American Old West] <Kang, Literature>

parts.label: L
parts.question: One star in this constellation experienced a drastic dimming during winter 2020, believed to have been caused by "starspots" covering over half its surface. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this constellation depicting a hunter from Greek mythology. Its most famous feature is the three stars that make up its belt.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This supergiant variable star, which experienced the aforementioned dimming, is usually the second brightest star in Orion. It forms one of Orion's "shoulders".

parts.label: C
parts.question: Astronomers believed that Betelgeuse's dimming could be a sign that it will undergo one of these events soon. In these events, a massive star collapses in on itself and explodes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event occurred after a driver made a wrong turn to a street where, according to popular legend, its perpetrator had stopped to get a sandwich. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Describe this event was perpetrated by Gavrilo Princip in Sarajevo by a Serbian nationalist group.
parts.answer: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand [accept any obvious equivalents, prompt on but DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL answers like the start of World War I]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Franz Ferdinand's death sparked the beginning of this war which lasted from 1914 to 1918.
parts.answer: World War I [or the First World War, or the Great War; accept The War to End All Wars]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer these questions about livestock in mythology and folktales, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: After this Mesopotamian love goddess is rejected by Gilgamesh, she unleashes the Bull of Heaven on him, leading to the death of his friend Enkidu.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This giant lumberjack in American folklore is accompanied by Babe the Blue Ox.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The goat Heiðrún (HAY-dhroon) grazes from the tree Læraðr (LIE-rah-dhur) atop this location, and produces vast quantities of mead. This giant hall owned by Odin is the final resting place for the einherjar (AIN-hair-yaar), the souls of fallen warriors, who are led to this place by valkyries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Seven small kingdoms fought for control of this country during the Warring States period, which resulted in the state of Qin (chin) emerging supreme. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country whose capital during the Qin Dynasty was located at Xi'an (SEE-ahn).

parts.label: B
parts.question: This first emperor of the Qin dynasty united China, ending the Warring States period. He is traditionally held to have perpetrated a burning of books and mass murder of scholars, which may not have actually happened.
parts.answer: Qin Shi Huang [or Qin Shi Huangdi, or Zhao Zheng, or Ying Zheng, or Zheng, King of Qin; prompt on Zheng; prompt on First Qin Emperor]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Qin Shi Huang (chin shur hwahng) ordered the construction of a massive army of sculptures of soldiers made of this substance to protect him in the afterlife.
parts.answer: terracotta [prompt on ceramic or clay or pottery]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man penned an elegy for himself, writing that “I hope to see my Pilot face to face / when I have crossed the bar”. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this British poet of "Crossing the Bar". Another of his poems is set during the Crimean War and describes a cavalry unit at the Battle of Balaclava.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Tennyson poem opens "Half a league, half a league / half a league onward”. Its final stanza asks "When can their glory fade? / O the wild charge they made!".

parts.label: C
parts.question: “The Charge of the Light Brigade” describes the cavalry riding into the “valley of” this concept. An Emily Dickinson poem begins “Because I could not stop for [this concept] -- / He kindly stopped for me”.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This painting depicts James Monroe holding up an American flag. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Emmanuel Leutze (LOYT-zuh) painting depicting the first president of the United States sailing a boat across a river during the Revolutionary War.
parts.answer: Washington Crossing the Delaware [do not accept or prompt on “George Washington Crossing the Delaware”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American regionalist artist painted Daughters of Revolution, a work that depicts three people who may be Ben Franklin, Thomas Jefferson and George Washington in drag standing in front of Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Grant Wood also created this painting, depicting a farmer standing next to his daughter and holding a pitchfork in front of a house in Eldon, Iowa.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the work of Italian biologist Camillo Golgi, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Golgi discovered a large organelle which is named for him and which packages these molecules. These molecules are made up of amino acids and are a nutrient provided in food like nuts and meat.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Golgi also invented a form of this technique that allows neurons to be visualized. Hans Christian Gram names another form of this technique that can be used to classify bacteria.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Gram staining classifies organisms based on the thickness of this organelle, which surrounds the cells of some organisms. It is made of cellulose in plants and is not present in animal cells.
parts.answer: cell wall [do not accept or prompt on "cell membrane"]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event will be preceded by Fimbulwinter, a series of three successive winters that will kill all humans except for Líf and Lífþrasir (LEEF-thraa-seer). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify this event whose name means "Fate of the Gods" in Old Norse. During this event, Odin will be swallowed whole by the wolf Fenrir.

parts.label: B
parts.question: During Ragnarök, this god of thunder will kill and be killed by the sea serpent Jörmungandr (YOR-moon-gahn-der). He is probably better known for wielding the weapon Mjölnir (myol-neer).

parts.label: C
parts.question: Heimdallr will blow the Gjallarhorn (GYAH-lar-horn) to warn the occupants of this home of the gods about Ragnarök starting. In another myth, a giant and his horse attempted to build walls around this location.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event was described by Franklin Delano Roosevelt as "a day which will live in infamy". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this event in which the USS Arizona was sunk in an American naval base by a surprise attack.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Pearl Harbor is a naval base in this U.S. state consisting of a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean. Its capital of Honolulu is near Pearl Harbor.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Japanese admiral commanded the pilots at Pearl Harbor. His plane was shot down on Bougainville Island during Operation Vengeance in 1943.
parts.answer: Isoroku Yamamoto [or Yamamoto Isoroku, since Japanese names are traditionally written in reverse order]

parts.label: L
