parts.question: Name this astronomical object that can experience namesake “spots,” dark regions on its surface caused by magnetic activity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sunspots are still very bright; they only look dark compared to this layer, the “visible” surface of the sun, where energy is released as light.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This other phenomenon can make parts of the sun appear dark. In these events, a syzygy, or the lining-up of three astronomical objects, causes the moon to block out the Earth’s view of the sun.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The last ruler with this title was overthrown by the Bolsheviks. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this title for rulers of Russia prior to the October Revolution. The last man to hold this title was Nicholas II, who was executed along with his family.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This youngest daughter of Nicholas II was rumored to have survived the royal family’s execution. Many women impersonated this girl in attempts to claim her fortune.
parts.answer: Anastasia Romanov (accept Anastasiya Nikolayevna Romanov; prompt on “Romanov”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This mystic and advisor to Nicholas II avoided being executed along with the imperial family because he had already been poisoned, stabbed, shot, and drowned.
parts.answer: Grigori Rasputin (accept Grigori Yefimovich Rasputin; accept Grigori Novykh)

parts.label: L
parts.question: When this literary character uses a brass knob from a fire grate to propose, he is rejected because his love interest is angry that he has already been engaged to Amy Lawrence. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fictional boy from Missouri who, in an adventure novel named for him, finds Injun Joe’s treasure hidden in McDougal’s Cave.
parts.answer: Tom Sawyer (accept either underlined name; accept Thomas Sawyer; accept The Adventures of Tom Sawyer)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Tom Sawyer’s proposal is rejected by this girl, the daughter of a local judge. Later in the novel, she and Tom get lost together in McDougal’s Cave.
parts.answer: Becky Thatcher (accept Becky Thatcher; prompt on “Thatcher” alone)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer is by this American author of The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the mythical daughter of Priam and Hecuba, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This princess in Greek mythology had the gift of being able to see the future, but was cursed so that people would never believe her prophecies.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Cassandra received the ability to see the future from this Greek god of light and prophecy, who was the twin brother of Artemis. He cursed her after she turned down his romantic advances.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Cassandra was a princess from this city. She foresaw its fall to Agamemnon’s Greek army.
parts.answer: Troy (accept Troia; accept Ilium or Ilion or Ilios)

parts.label: L
parts.question: On the Allred-Rochow scale, elements in this group have electro-negativities between 1.8 and 2.2. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this group of roughly six elements that includes boron, arsenic, and germanium. This group’s name reflects that its properties are between those of elements like gold and oxygen.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The semiconductor industry relies heavily on germanium and this element with symbol Si to build components like transistors and microchips.
parts.answer: silicon (do not accept or prompt on “silicone” or “silica”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: When the metalloid antimony is blended with tin, the result is this alloy, traditionally used to make dishes, pitchers, and beer tankards.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a novel by this author, Abel Magwitch is deported to Australia for fighting in prison, although the man he fought is given a lighter punishment because of his well-bred manner. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this English author who highlighted Victorian social inequality in works like David Copperfield and A Christmas Carol.
parts.answer: Charles Dickens (accept Charles John Huffam Dickens)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Abel Magwitch appears in this Charles Dickens novel, in which he makes a fortune in Australia and uses it to help the young orphan Pip become a gentleman and befriend Magwitch’s estranged daughter, Estella.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Great Expectations, Estella is raised not by her father, but by Miss Havisham, who tries to mold Estella into a cruel heartbreaker. Miss Havisham wears a tattered dress and keeps the clocks in her house stopped at twenty minutes to nine to remind herself of this event, during which she was left at the altar.
parts.answer: her wedding (accept similar terms like marriage; accept descriptions of her being abandoned or left by her fiancé)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Introductory algebra classes often focus on the factoring of these expressions, such as “x squared minus four x plus four.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for an expression that includes coefficients and variables that are combined by addition and multiplication.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Polynomials can be classified based on their number of terms; for example, “two x” is a monomial, and “two x plus two” is one of these.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Polynomials can also be classified by this quantity, the largest exponent on any of its terms. For example, for “x to the one-hundredth power, minus three x cubed, plus one,” this quantity is one hundred.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about Interstate 10 in the American southeast, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: I-10’s eastern terminus is this massive metropolis, found on the St. John’s River in Duval County in northeast Florida.

parts.label: B
parts.question: After leaving Florida, I-10 intersects I-65 in this Alabama city on a namesake bay. This city’s Mardi Gras celebrations are the oldest in the US, predating New Orleans.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Continuing west from Alabama, I-10 passes through Biloxi in this state before reaching New Orleans in Louisiana.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a speech to Protestant ministers in Houston, this man remarked “I am not the Catholic candidate for president. I am the Democratic Party’s candidate for president, who happens also to be a Catholic.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this politician who became the first Catholic American president when he defeated Richard Nixon in 1960.
parts.answer: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (accept JFK; prompt on “Kennedy”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1960, the Kennedy campaign was particularly worried about anti-Catholic sentiment in the South, so they selected this Texan protestant as Kennedy’s running mate.
parts.answer: Lyndon Baines Johnson (accept LBJ; prompt on “Johnson”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Nixon supporters worried that this mayor of Chicago had committed voter fraud to push Illinois in Kennedy’s favor, but Nixon refused to challenge the election results.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country is home to the playwright of The Glass Menagerie and The Rose Tattoo. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, which is also the home country of playwright Eugene O’Neill, who set the play Long Day’s Journey Into Night in Connecticut.
parts.answer: US (accept USA; accept either underlined portion of United States of America)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Glass Menagerie and The Rose Tattoo are by this American playwright, who set many of his works in the American South.
parts.answer: Tennessee Williams (accept Thomas Lanier Williams III [third])

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this Tennessee Williams play set in New Orleans, Blanche DuBois loses her family’s home, Belle Reve, and moves into an apartment with her sister and brother-in-law, Stella and Stanley Kowalski.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This artist frequently used his wife, Jo, as a model for paintings of women in city settings. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this American painter of Automat and Chop Suey.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this often-parodied painting by Edward Hopper, two men and a woman in a red dress sit at a brightly-lit lunch counter on a dramatically dark street.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hopper’s paintings frequently emphasize the crowds and isolation of this American city. Hopper died in Manhattan, a borough of this east coast city.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This function is the “CAH” [kah] portion of the popular mnemonic “SOHCAHTOA” [soh-kah-toh-ah]. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this function whose input values are typically angles; for example, this function of zero degrees is one.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sine and cosine are two elementary functions of this branch of mathematics, which studies the relationships between the angles and side lengths of triangles.
parts.answer: trigonometry (accept trig; do not accept or prompt on “geometry”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This trigonometric function is the reciprocal of the cosine function.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Following this man’s death, hundreds of Spaniards died trying to flee during La Noche Triste [noh-chay tris-tay]. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this leader who was allegedly stoned to death by his own people after being taken hostage by conquistadors.
parts.answer: Montezuma II (accept Moctezuma II; prompt on “Montezuma” or “Moctezuma” alone)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Spaniard led the conquistadors who captured Montezuma.
parts.answer: Hernan´ Cortes´ (accept Hernan´ Cortes´ y Pizarro Altamirano)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Montezuma II was a leader of this Mesoamerican empire, which was based in modern-day Mexico and conquered by the Spanish after the fall of their capital, Tenochtitlan [tay-nohch-teet-lahn].

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about English author Virginia Woolf, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Virginia Woolf is the author of Orlando, which narrates the life of a three-hundred-year-old person who grows from a boy in the 1600s to a woman in the 1900s. Woolf described Orlando as a “fictional” work in this non-fiction genre, which describes a person’s life.
parts.answer: biography (accept fictional biography; do not accept “autobiography”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In her essay “A Room of One’s Own,” Woolf contrasts the tragic life of a fictional Elizabethan writer named Judith with that of her “brother,” this real-life author of Twelfth Night and A Midsummer Night’s Dream.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This novel by Virginia Woolf follows the Ramsey family on vacation before and after the first World War. At the end of this novel, the surviving family members complete the title journey.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author justified revolution in Rights of Man, and declared “these are the times that try men’s souls.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this early American pamphleteer who attempted to inspire rebelling colonists during the American Revolution with his pamphlet series “The American Crisis.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Thomas Paine argued that it was absurd for a continent to be ruled by an island in this pamphlet, which advocated for the separation of the American colonies from Britain.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Common Sense was published in this year, the same year that the United States declared independence.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the work of Artemisia Gentileschi, the Italian painter of a Self Portrait as the Allegory of Painting, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Artemisia painted Judith and her maidservant killing the general Holofernes in this way. She also painted the princess Salome holding the evidence of John the Baptist’s execution, which was carried out in this manner.
parts.answer: beheading (accept descriptions like cutting off his head; accept Judith Beheading Holofernes; prompt on answers describing “using a knife;” prompt on “amputation”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Artemisia used this color for the dresses of Judith and Salome to highlight her main characters. Her namesake tone of this color mimics the rich color of a precious metal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Artemisia worked during this seventeenth- and eighteenth-century artistic period that followed the Renaissance and preceded Rococo. Art in this period commonly had ornate and dramatic themes and lush textures.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Above eight thousand meters, this layer is called the “death zone” because its effective oxygen percentage is just eight percent, compared to twenty-one percent at sea level. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this lowest region of Earth’s atmosphere, where all weather occurs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The troposphere over large urban areas like Los Angeles and Mexico City tends to trap this visible, toxic form of air pollution that consists of nitrogen and sulfur oxides.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Urban air tends to trap smog close to the ground because of an inversion of this quantity, which normally decreases with altitude toward the top of the troposphere, where it can drop below negative fifty Celsius.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel’s sequel, Go Set a Watchman, Scout sees her father attend a pro-segregation council meeting in the same courthouse where he once defended an unfairly accused Black man. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Harper Lee novel that follows Scout and Atticus Finch through the trial of Tom Robinson in the predominantly racist town of Maycomb, Alabama.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In To Kill a Mockingbird, Scout and her friends spread rumors that this character eats bats because they never see him leave his house. She later changes her opinion about this character when he saves her and Jem from Bob Ewell after a Halloween pageant.
parts.answer: Boo Radley (accept either underlined name; accept Arthur Radley)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Scout attends church with this character, the Finch family’s cook and a mother figure to Scout.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about films directed by Ridley Scott, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: In this 2021 Ridley Scott film, set in medieval France, Adam Driver and Matt Damon prepare for the final officially-sanctioned instance of trial by combat in French history.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this Ridley Scott film, Ripley is the sole survivor of the Nostromo, the rest of the crew having been killed by a monster that bursts out of the chest of a crew member.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The “Tears in Rain” speech is given in this Ridley Scott film, in which the bounty hunter Deckard hunts down rogue cyborgs who are looking to extend their lifespans. Harrison Ford starred in this film and appears in its 2017 sequel, set in the year 2049.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name some ballets by Pyotr Illych Tchaikovsky, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: In this ballet, Odette and Prince Siegfried kill themselves to escape a curse placed by the evil sorcerer Rothbart, who transforms Odette into the title bird.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The heroine of this Christmastime ballet is usually called Marie or Clara. She defeats the evil Mouse King by hitting him on the head with her slipper, and meets the Sugar Plum Fairy in a magical land of sweets in this ballet.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Marius Petipa choreographed Tchaikovsky’s version of this story, in which the Lilac Fairy weakens a curse placed on Aurora by the evil fairy Carabosse.
parts.answer: The Sleeping Beauty (accept Spyashchaya krasavitsa; accept La belle au bois dormant)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Basile’s version of this story, Zezolla is helped by a fairy living in a fig tree. In the German version, Aschenputtel is helped by a bird who lives in a tree planted on her mother’s grave. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this folk tale in which the title girl is forced to be a servant in her family’s house, but marries a prince after her fairy godmother gives her a pair of glass slippers.
parts.answer: Cinderella (accept Cenerentola; accept Aschenputtel before it is read)

parts.label: B
parts.question: A German version of “Cinderella” appears in the Children’s and Household Tales collected by these folk-tale-obsessed brothers.
parts.answer: Grimm brothers (accept Brothers Grimm; accept Jacob Ludwig Karl and/or Wilhelm Carl Grimm)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In addition to studying fairy tales and German mythology, Jacob Grimm worked in this field of study; he is the namesake of Grimm’s Law, a rule that describes a shift between Proto-Indo-European and German.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Dalai Lama has repeatedly undergone this process, through which he has chosen a new body after death fourteen times. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this cycle of birth, death, and rebirth that is common in Indian religions.
parts.answer: reincarnation (accept samsara; accept descriptions like transmigration of souls or metempsychosis; prompt on “rebirth” before it is read by asking “what process is rebirth a part of?”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: A being’s status and species following reincarnation are determined by their positive and negative actions in life, which are collectively known by this term, meaning “deeds.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Indian religion’s texts say that a person will be reincarnated into one of four realms of existence, called gatis. Followers of this religion practice ahimsa, or extreme non-violence.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the particularly small town of Monowi, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Monowi is in this state, which is the only US state whose state government is unicameral. This state’s legislature meets in the capital of Lincoln.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Elsie Eiler is the mayor and only resident of Monowi, but data collected in 2020 by this governmental procedure claimed that Monowi’s population was actually two. Article One of the Constitution requires that this process take place every ten years.
parts.answer: United States Census (prompt on descriptions like “counting people”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Census’ official policy is to occasionally shift respondents between nearby census blocks to preserve privacy in low population areas. So, while Monowi’s block is inaccurate, the data is still accurate at the level of these geographic divisions. These 435 divisions are redrawn - and possibly gerrymandered - after every census.
parts.answer: Congressional districts (prompt on partial answers that don’t include both underlined words)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Along with a flame test, elements in solution can be identified using qualitative analysis. Answer these questions about the process, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Much of qualitative analysis depends on this kind of reaction in which two ions combine to form a solid that sinks to the bottom of a test tube.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Lead [led], silver, and mercury can be identified quickly because they precipitate with this anion found in table salt.
parts.answer: chloride ion (prompt on “Cl−”; do not accept “chlorine”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Because it behaves so much like iron, this metal is difficult to identify in solution, requiring eight steps to form a rose red precipitate. This element has chemical symbol Ni [N-I].

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this novel, little Antanas drowns in a puddle, and a teenager named Stanislovas is eaten by rats in a factory. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this novel about Lithuanian immigrant Jurgus Rudkis [YUR-gus RUD-kus], whose publication inspired the passage of the 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act with its depiction of the meatpacking industry.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Jungle describes the extreme poverty of meatpackers in this American city on Lake Michigan. A Carl Sandburg poem about this Illinois city describes it as the “Hog Butcher for the world.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: This muck-raking author of The Brass Check intended The Jungle to inspire reform of working conditions in the meatpacking industry.
parts.answer: Upton Sinclair (accept Upton Beall Sinclair, Jr)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organization’s COINTELPRO, or Counter Intelligence Program, carried out illegal surveillance of “subversives” like anti-war activists, feminists, environmentalists, and civil rights activists from 1956 to 1971. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this government agency, tasked with domestic security and law enforcement, that largely ignored white supremacist terror in the 1950s and 60s.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This longest-serving director of the FBI ordered much of COINTELPRO’s activities. When Martin Luther King criticized the FBI for ignoring white terror, this man responded by calling King the “most notorious liar” in America.
parts.answer: J. Edgar Hoover (accept John Edgar Hoover)

parts.label: C
parts.question: As Attorney General under his brother John, this man personally authorized some of the FBI’s requests, including wiretapping phones to spy on Martin Luther King.
parts.answer: Robert Francis Kennedy (accept RFK; accept Bobby Kennedy; prompt on “Kennedy” alone)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about rivers of the American west, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This river forms the Mexican-American border for over eight hundred miles in Texas.
parts.answer: Rio Grande (accept Rio Bravo del Norte)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Hydroelectric dams on this river are a source of environmental controversy, since they make breeding difficult for its massive salmon population. This river flows through Hells Canyon on the border between Idaho and Oregon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: An intermittent river of this name runs mostly underground for one hundred miles in southern California. This river flows under, and shares its name with, the hottest desert in America.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A boat’s outboard motor in water produces this type of motion, which is contrasted with laminar flow. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this type of fluid movement in which particles experience unpredictable changes in velocity and pressure. Airplanes experience this phenomenon at the boundaries of air masses moving at different speeds.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The transition from laminar to turbulent flow can be predicted using this dimensionless number named for a British physicist. For a circular water pipe, turbulence occurs when this number is greater than four thousand.
parts.answer: Reynolds number (accept Re; accept Osborne Reynolds)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The dimples on this type of ball increase its Reynolds number to about fifty thousand, greatly reducing air resistance and increasing distance when it is struck with a club such as a three-iron.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
parts.answer: Kaiser Wilhelm II (prompt on “Willy;” prompt on “Wilhelm”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The “Willy-Nicky” telegrams discussed each one’s fears that the other country was beginning this process of readying troops and supplies for war. This process was seen as an act of war, even though “Willy” and “Nicky” tried to convince each other it was not.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Wilhelm II and Nicholas II were related through - among many, many other royals - this English queen who was known as the “Grandmother of Europe.” This woman’s record as longest-serving British monarch was broken by Elizabeth II.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A modified type of this structure called a tableau [tab-low] is used in the simplex method for linear programming. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these mathematical objects that organize values into rows and columns.

parts.label: B
parts.question: If you multiply matrix A times matrix B, you may or may not get the same answer as when you multiply B times A. Thus, matrix multiplication does not have this property.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Multiplying a matrix by this specific type of matrix will always be commutative because multiplying by this matrix does not change the original matrix. In the same way, multiplying any real number by the number one will return the original number because one is a “multiplicative” one of these.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1912, the Royal Albert Hall hosted an enormous benefit concert for the families of the musicians who played during a maritime tragedy. Answer the following about the concert, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The concert memorialized the band of this “unsinkable” White Star Line ship, which sank while sailing from England to America in 1912.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concert included a performance of this composer’s Funeral March. This Polish composer also wrote the Revolutionary Etude ´ and the Minute Waltz.
parts.answer: Fred´ eric ´ Chopin (accept Fred´ eric Franc¸ois ´ Chopin; accept Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This British composer conducted part of the concert, which included a performance of this man’s Enigma Variations.
parts.answer: Edward Elgar (accept Sir Edward William Elgar)

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these objects is at the center of astronomical object 3C 273, which is the most distant object visible through a backyard telescope because it is brighter than all stars in its surrounding galaxy combined. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these astronomical objects that are so dense that not even light can escape from their event horizons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: 3C 273 is one of these objects, the most luminous type of object in the universe. These objects are composed of an active galactic nucleus powered by a supermassive black hole.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Radio astronomer Maarten Schmidt confirmed the vast distance between quasars and Earth by measuring the high degree of this shift, an example of the Doppler effect.
parts.answer: redshift (do not accept or prompt on “blueshift”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: A modern country named for this empire has its capital at Bamako. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this north African empire ruled by Sundiata Keita and Mansa Musa.
parts.answer: Malian Empire (accept Republic of Mali; accept Manden Kurufaba)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Mali Empire was rich in gold and this mined, mineral resource that is essential for human life, and that is the most common food seasoning.
parts.answer: salt (accept table salt; accept rock salt; accept halite; accept sodium chloride or NaCl)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Mali traded salt and gold over this hot desert in northern Africa.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This literary character travels through India, Hong Kong, and the United States, but is described as “one of those English gentlemen who are wont to see foreign countries through the eyes of their domestics.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fictional adventurer who lets his French servant, Passepartout [pas-par-too], do most of the legwork as they circumnavigate the globe as quickly as possible.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Phileas Fogg was created by this French author of adventure novels like Journey to the Center of the Earth and Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Phileas Fogg is the protagonist of this Jules Verne novel, in which he wins a bet against London’s Reform Club by completing the title achievement.
parts.answer: Around the World in Eighty Days (accept Le tour du monde en quatre-vingts jours)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer these questions about Odin’s quest for knowledge, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Odin traded one of these body parts to be able to drink magical water that would give him wisdom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Odin gave his eye to this god so that he could drink the water of wisdom. After this god was decapitated, Odin magically kept his head alive as a source of advice.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Seeking even more wisdom, Odin hung himself from the world-tree Yggdrasil [IGG-drah-zil] with his spear to gain knowledge of these symbols, which were used for writing and fortune telling.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You’ve decided to buy a DNA testing kit and get your genealogical profile. Answer these questions about the process, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Before the company can sequence the DNA in your saliva sample, this process is used to amplify the DNA. This process uses a thermal cycler and Taq [tack] polymerase enzyme.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The company can trace your matrilineal ancestry using DNA from your mitochondria. If you are male, your father’s line can be traced using this chromosome.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Since 2012, companies can look for variants in genes like SPAG17 and TTF1 to determine what percentage of your DNA was inherited from this other humanoid species that went extinct about forty thousand years ago.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This American poet’s works, such as “I’m Nobody! Who are you?” usually lack official titles, and are instead known by their first lines. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this reclusive poet, nicknamed the “Belle of Amhurst,” who wrote “I felt a funeral in my brain” and “A narrow Fellow in the Grass.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The first lines of one Emily Dickinson poem say, “Because I could not stop for [this thing] - / He kindly stopped for me.” The poem describes a carriage ride to a grave with this concept and “Immortality.”
parts.answer: death (accept Because I could not stop for Death -)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In another poem by Dickinson, this animal’s “Blue - uncertain stumbling Buzz” breaks up “the Stillness in the Room.” The title and first line of the poem says, “I heard [this animal] buzz - when I died.”
parts.answer: fly (accept I heard a Fly buzz - when I died -)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the landmark interstate commerce case Gibbons v. Ogden, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The monopoly in Gibbons v. Ogden was ruled unconstitutional by this highest American judicial body. At the time of the judgement, this body was led by Chief Justice John Marshall.
parts.answer: Supreme Court of the United States (accept SCOTUS)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Gibbons v. Ogden, the Supreme Court ruled against a monopoly of these specific vessels, which were used for shipping and transit through the rivers of New York state in the 1800s.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This American entrepreneur, nicknamed “Commodore,” worked as a steamboat captain and business manager for Gibbons, and combatted other steamboat monopolies before building a railroad empire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author developed his most famous argument over time, from its original use in Discourse on the Method to a modified version in Meditations on First Philosophy. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this seventeenth-century French philosopher who famously concluded “Cogito ergo sum,” [koh-gee-toe ayr-goh soom] or “I think, therefore I am.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The statement “cogito ergo sum” is written in this language. Descartes [day-cart] first wrote the statement in French because he feared that using this language would reach fewer people.
parts.answer: Latin (do not accept or prompt on “Italian” or “Roman”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Descartes’s Discourse on the Method revolutionized philosophy by promoting this concept as a starting point. parts.label: L
parts.question: In theory, a meta-material super-lens could be used to see a nano-machine at work because the lens has a negative value for this quantity. For ten points each,

parts.question: Name this optical quantity, the ratio of light’s speed in a vacuum to its speed in a medium. This quantity is about 1.33 for water and 2.42 for diamond.

parts.question: Name this European nation, Burns’s homeland, whose dialect he used to write about schemes that “gang aft agley.”
parts.answer: Scottish (accept Scots English; accept Scotland; accept Alba)

parts.question: Burns wrote “the best-laid schemes o’ [these creatures] an’ men / gang aft agley” in a poem addressed to one of these small mammals when he “[Turned] Her Up in Her Nest With the Plough.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this game series, bells can be used to purchase items and pay off your mortgage. For ten points each,

parts.question: Name this video game series, whose newest release, New Horizons, came out in March 2020. This game series allows players to create their own home and interact with anthropomorphized villagers.
parts.answer: Animal Crossing (accept Doubutsu no Mori [doh-boo-tsoo noh moh-ree])

parts.question: Answer the following about one of the three “Grand Dames” [grahn dahmz] of a nineteenth-century French art movement, Berthe Morisot [bayr-tuh moh-ree-soh], for ten points each.

parts.question: Morisot was part of this French art movement. This movement focused on painting en plein air [ahn plah-nayr] and using broad, sketch-like brush strokes to capture the movement and natural lighting of scenes like Waterlilies and Morisot’s Grain Field.

parts.answer: Claude Monet (accept Oscar-Claude Monet or Claude Oscar Monet; do not accept or prompt on “Manet”)

parts.label: C

parts.answer: balcony (accept Woman and Child On the Balcony)

parts.label: L

parts.label: B

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Spanish founded this city in Florida in 1565, making it America’s oldest city.

parts.question: This ruler was the son of Pepin the Short, and his territory was divided between his three grandsons after the death of his son, Louis the Pious. For ten points each,

parts.question: Name this Medieval king who was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in the year 800.
parts.answer: Charlemagne (accept Charles the Great; accept Carolus Magnus; accept Charles I; prompt on “Charles” or “Carolus”)

parts.label: B

parts.answer: Franks (accept Frankish people; do not accept or prompt on “France” or “French”)

parts.question: Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III [third] on this Christian holiday.

parts.label: B

parts.question: Perfectly elastic collisions and negligible particle volume are two of the assumptions made in the kinetic theory of these substances. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this state of matter whose molecules are in constant, random motion, but with much greater separation between particles than in a liquid.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Using kinetic theory, it is possible to derive Fick’s laws of this process, in which gas particles spread out from an area of high concentration to an area of lower concentration.

parts.question: While kinetic theory assumes an ideal gas, this equation models real gases using a and b parameters to correct for intermolecular attraction and particle volume, respectively.

parts.question: Like later Greek gods, the Titans represented elements of the natural world. The Titaness Selene was the embodiment of this natural satellite of Earth, which dominates the night sky.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Titaness was the Greek goddess of witchcraft. She was the handmaiden of Persephone and the goddess of ghosts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer wrote the Holberg Suite and a musical suite that accompanies a Henrik Ibsen play about a folk hero. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Norwegian composer who included songs like “Anitra’s Dance,” “Solveig’s Song,” and “The Death of Ase” in his Peer Gynt Suite.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This mysterious-sounding song from the Peer Gynt Suite gradually grows louder and faster to represent Peer being chased.
parts.answer: In the Hall of Mountain King (accept I Dovregubbens hall)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The song In the Hall of the Mountain King is set in the home of one of these mythical Scandinavian creatures. These humanoid creatures often have tails, and may turn to stone in the sunlight.

parts.label: L
parts.question: William Travis wrote “VICTORY OR DEATH” in a plea to “the People of Texas & All Americans in the World” during the siege of this fort. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this San Antonio fort that was besieged by Santa Anna’s forces in early 1836.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Another defender of the Alamo was this man, whose proficiency with a long-bladed knife led its type to be named for him.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This frontiersman and hater of Andrew Jackson died alongside James Bowie and William Travis while defending the Alamo.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This list’s one-hundred-tenth and final object, a dwarf satellite galaxy, was added in 1967, nearly two hundred years after its first publication. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this catalog of astronomical objects compiled by a French astronomer in the eighteenth century. In this catalog, M45 is the Pleiades cluster, and M31 is the Andromeda galaxy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Messier referred to most of his objects by this term. However, we now know that only a handful are really these interstellar dust clouds. Two of these objects are M16 and M1, nicknamed the “Eagle” and the “Crab.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: M42 is the nebula named for this constellation, which contains the stars Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka in its belt.

parts.label: L
parts.question: As a baby, this mythical Greek king is sent out to die because his parents fear he will fulfill a dire prophecy. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this mythical Greek figure who fulfills part of the prophecy when he kills his father, Laius [LAH-yuss], and becomes the king of Thebes in a series of plays by Sophocles.
parts.answer: Oedipus (accept Oedipus Rex or Oedipus Tyrannus; accept Oedipus at Colonus)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Oedipus becomes the king of Thebes by solving a riddle posed by this mythical creature, which has the body of a lion and the head of a human.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Oedipus fulfills the second part of his prophecy by marrying Jocasta, a woman who unknowingly has this familial relationship with Oedipus.
parts.answer: she is his own mother (accept equivalents like she is his mom; accept reversed and equivalent descriptions like he is her son or her child)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2017, an armed, all-female unit was established in Zimbabwe to help combat this crime. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this illegal act of hunting or capturing wild animals. A common form of this crime is killing elephants for their ivory.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Black rhinos have nearly gone extinct due to poaching in this African region. This grassland is the namesake of a national park in Tanzania, and reaches the Maasai Mara National Park in Kenya.

parts.label: C
parts.question: During migration season, thousands of wildebeests and this striped equine cross the Serengeti in search of new grass.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The two D-lines are indicative of sodium when light from the Sun is analyzed by this method. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this technique in which the light given off by a heated element is separated into a characteristic pattern of emission lines.
parts.answer: atomic emission spectroscopy (accept spectrometry; accept spectrography)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sodium’s two D-lines are found in this color of the visible spectrum, which is also the color of potassium chromate solution and lead [led] iodide solid.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Two violet, one blue, and one red line are found in the Balmer spectral series of this element, the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poem claims it will “justify the ways of God to man.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this epic poem by John Milton that follows the creation, temptation, and downfall of Adam and Eve.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Paradise Lost fulfills its title when Adam and Eve take “their solitary way” and leave the paradise of this biblical garden.
parts.answer: Garden of Eden (accept Garden of God or gan-Yahweh)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Despite the angels’ efforts, Eve is tempted by this character, who was called Lucifer before the Angelic War. This figure thinks it is “better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer these questions about the many times Zeus transformed himself to seduce women, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Zeus seduced this woman while in the form of a swan. This woman had four children with Zeus, including Helen of Troy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Zeus took the form of gold coins falling from the sky to seduce the princess Danae. Afterwards, Danae gave birth to this hero, who freed Andromeda and killed Medusa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Zeus seduced Europa by turning into one of these animals. Io, another woman seduced by Zeus, was turned into one of these animals by Hera.
parts.answer: cattle (accept equivalents like cows or bulls)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Democrat Pat Schroeder described this man’s presidency as “Teflon-coated” because “nothing sticks to him.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this president who somehow survived scandals like the Iran-Contra Affair during his two terms in office in the 1980s.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Before becoming president of the United States, Ronald Reagan was the governor of this state.

parts.label: C
parts.question: While governor of California, Ronald Reagan legalized the “no-fault” form of this process. Ronald Reagan was the first US president to have gone through this process.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s prime ministers have included Jawaharlal Nehru and his daughter, who ruled with an iron fist during the Emergency, and who ordered Operation Blue Star. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this modern country led for much of the sixties through eighties by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi from its capital, New Delhi.
parts.answer: India (accept Republic of India; accept Bharat Ganarajya)

parts.label: B
parts.question: When she declared a state of emergency, Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay spearheaded a population control strategy in which poor men and women were forced to undergo this medical procedure.
parts.answer: sexual sterilization (accept word forms like sterilize; accept male and/or female sterilization; accept vasectomy or tubectomy)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Gandhi’s time in office came to an abrupt end when she was assassinated by her bodyguards, who were followers of this religion. They were angry over Gandhi’s attack on this religion’s Golden Temple in Operation Blue Star.
parts.answer: Sikhi (accept word forms like Sikhism or Sikhs)

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to Noether’s theorem, quantities like mass and electric charge have this property in a closed system because the physical laws that describe them are symmetric. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term that means that a measurable quantity of a system does not change over time. The first law of thermodynamics states that energy has this property.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Conservation of this quantity, which is equal to moment of inertia times angular speed, explains why a rotating figure skater starts spinning faster when she pulls her arms toward her body.
parts.answer: angular momentum (do not accept or prompt on “momentum” alone; do not accept “linear momentum”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: When two objects experience this type of collision, the system’s linear momentum will be conserved, but its kinetic energy will not.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem named for one of these animals, a free one “leaps / on the back of the wind” while a caged one “sings / with a fearful trill / of things unknown / but longed for still.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this animal whose “wings are clipped” and who “sings of freedom.”
parts.answer: birds (accept the caged bird or the free bird; accept I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings)

parts.label: B
parts.question: “Caged Bird” was written by this American poet and civil rights activist. Her autobiography series begins with the similarly named book, I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Angelou recited her poem “On the Pulse of Morning” for the 1993 inauguration of this forty-second president of the United States, whose wife ran for the same office in 2016.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about currently airing medical dramas, for ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: This David Shore show is about the autistic Shaun Murphy. In the pilot of this show, Shaun saves a young boy who has been struck by falling glass at an airport.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Station-19 is a spin-off of this eighteen-season show, developed by Shonda Rhimes, in which Meredith Grey works at Grey Sloan Memorial in Seattle. Its title is a reference to a classic medical text.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This longest-running American soap opera debuted in 1963, and starred John Beradino and Emily McLaughlin until their respective deaths in the 1990s. Its current cast is led by Maurice Benard, who plays the mobster Sonny Corinthos.
